title.rendered: How to hide caller ID on iPhone when making a phone call

content.rendered:
I sometimes want to make a phone call without handing over my phone number, especially when I’m contacting a business, responding to an unfamiliar listing, or simply don’t want the person to call me back. If you are looking for the same, the good news is that iPhone gives a simple way to hide your Caller ID.

This guide explains how to hide your Caller ID on an iPhone running iOS 27, including the settings path, single-call options, carrier limitations, and how to turn Caller ID back on.

Why you may want to hide your caller ID

Hiding your Caller ID masks your phone number, so the person you’re calling sees an incoming call banner or a full-screen call with a “No Caller ID”, “Private,” or “Unknown” label. No name or number will be displayed. Thus, they won’t be able to know who called them. 

People hide Caller ID for several reasons: 

  • Avoiding callbacks 
  • Protecting privacy when contacting businesses 
  • Making surprise or anonymous calls 
  • Preventing your number from being stored or shared 

Whatever your reason, iOS 27 offers built-in tools to hide your number for all outgoing calls or a single call.

Method 1: Hide your caller ID for all calls (iPhone settings)

This is the easiest and most common way to hide your number. Once enabled, every call you make will display “No Caller ID.” 

How to turn off your Caller ID in iOS 27: 

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Scroll down and tap Apps > Phone.
  3. Select Show My Caller ID.
  4. Toggle off Show My Caller ID.

When this switch is off, your number stays hidden for all outgoing calls unless you intentionally reveal it (more on that later).

Note: Some carriers don’t allow Caller ID disabling systemwide. If the toggle is missing or grayed out, your carrier may require you to use a code (see Method 2) or contact carrier support.

Method 2: Hide caller ID for a single call

If you want to reveal your number normally but hide it for a single call, iOS supports this via a carrier prefix. It temporarily blocks Caller ID for one outgoing call.

The important part here is that the code isn’t universal. It depends on your country and carrier.

  1. Open the Phone app.
  2. Go to the Keypad. 
  3. Dial *67 following the phone number. Example: *67 555-123-4567 for United States carriers.
  4. Tap the Call button to ring the number.  

The person you’re calling will see No Caller ID, whereas your number is visible to others. 

If you use other US carriers, stay in European countries, or travel to countries such as Australia, South Africa, Canada, or India, the code to hide Caller ID is #31#. For South Korea, it is *23#, and for the United Kingdom and Ireland, it is 141. Check the code for your country here.

This is ideal when: 

  • Calling someone you don’t know 
  • Responding to ads or job listings 
  • Contacting businesses that you don’t want calling back 

Method 3: Ask your carrier to block your number

If you want total privacy without relying on settings or prefixes, your mobile carrier can disable your Caller ID at the account level. Also, this method is the only way if your carrier doesn’t support short codes.

What carrier blocking does 

  • Hides your Caller ID permanently for all outgoing calls 
  • Overrides your iPhone settings 
  • Works even if you switch phones 

Some carriers provide Calling Line Identification Restriction (CLIR) for free; others may charge a small fee. You need to enable this option in the carrier’s official app or on its website.

For Verizon, you will have to sign in to your account. Next, under Block Services or Additional Services, you will find the Caller ID option. From here, you can hide it.

For Sprint, sign in to your carrier account. Next, select your phone, then click Change my service > Set up your phone > Block Caller ID.

Note: AT&T and T-Mobile allow you to use the code or the iPhone Settings app to hide the caller ID.

If the app or website method (or the first two methods) does not work, contact your carrier’s customer care via phone, email, or in-store and ask for help blocking the caller ID.

Limitations: When hiding caller ID won’t work

Even when Caller ID is off, there will still be some instances where your number will show.

Caller ID may still show if you call:

  • Emergency services (911)
  • Toll-free numbers 800, 888, etc.
  • Businesses that use special call-routing systems 
  • Contacts who use apps or services that reveal caller identity 

These systems override privacy settings for safety or verification reasons. 

How to show your caller ID on iPhone

If you want your phone number to show normally: 

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Go to Phone.
  3. Tap Show My Caller ID.
  4. Turn the switch on.

Decide who sees your number!

Hiding Caller ID on an iPhone is fast, easy, and even adaptable to your needs. You can make your calls totally private or hide them for just a single call. And you have multiple options that work reliably. If you liked this guide, check out more comprehensive iPhone tips and tricks.

FAQs

Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?

No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

Will text messages show my number?

Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?

No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

Is this supported worldwide?

Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

@graph.name: How to Hide Your Caller ID for All Calls on iPhone
@graph.description: Want to make anonymous calls from your iPhone? Here's how you can hide your caller ID for all outgoing calls using the built-in Phone settings.

step.name: Open Settings and go to Phone
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone, scroll down and tap Apps, then select Phone.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Settings app on your iPhone.
Scroll down and tap on Apps.
Find and tap the Phone option from the list.

step.name: Turn off Show My Caller ID
step.text: Tap Show My Caller ID and toggle it off to hide your number on all outgoing calls.

itemListElement.text: Tap on Show My Caller ID.
Turn off the toggle to disable caller ID display for all calls.

@graph.name: How to Hide Caller ID for a Single Call on iPhone
@graph.description: Need to hide your phone number for just one call? Here's how to quickly use a code on your iPhone to make a single anonymous call.

step.name: Open the Phone app and go to Keypad
step.text: Launch the Phone app on your iPhone and tap on the Keypad tab at the bottom.

itemListElement.text: Open the Phone app on your iPhone.
Tap on the Keypad tab at the bottom of the screen.

step.name: Dial the code with the number
step.text: Type *67 followed by the phone number you want to call. For example, *67 555-123-4567.

itemListElement.text: Dial *67 followed by the full phone number.
Ensure there are no spaces or extra characters between the code and number.

step.name: Tap Call to make the anonymous call
step.text: Tap the green Call button to place your call. Your number will be hidden for this call only.

itemListElement.text: Press the Call button to dial the number with caller ID hidden.

@graph.description: Want people to see your number when you call? Here's how to turn on caller ID visibility from your iPhone settings in just a few taps.

step.name: Open Settings and go to Phone
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone and scroll down to tap Phone.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
Scroll down and tap the Phone option.

step.name: Enable Show My Caller ID
step.text: Tap Show My Caller ID and turn on the toggle to make your number visible on outgoing calls.

itemListElement.text: Tap on Show My Caller ID.
Turn on the switch to enable caller ID display.

blockGraphs.question: Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?
blockGraphs.answer: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

blockGraphs.question: Will text messages show my number?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

blockGraphs.question: Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?
blockGraphs.answer: No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

blockGraphs.question: Is this supported worldwide?
blockGraphs.answer: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

title.rendered: How long does Apple support iPhones: Everything you need to know

content.rendered:
I’ve always considered long-term software support one of the biggest reasons to buy an iPhone. Even an older iPhone can continue receiving major iOS updates years after its launch, which is one reason these devices tend to hold their value so well.

That said, it’s important to consider how long Apple supports each iPhone model when buying an older or refurbished device. In this article, I’ll give you all the details you need to know about Apple’s support for different iPhones, so you know how many years of support to expect for your device.

How long does Apple Support iOS?

Based on Apple’s update history, most iPhones receive six to eight years of iOS support, although Apple does not promise a fixed number of major iOS versions for every iPhone. This is great from a longevity and security standpoint, as it ensures that your device will function optimally for several years.

The latest iOS 27 compatibility list is particularly interesting because Apple still supports the iPhone 11 series, which launched in 2019. That means the iPhone 11 can now run a major iOS release roughly seven years after its original launch.

However, it’s important to note that Apple cannot continue to support devices that are too old, as technology advances rapidly. Older devices lack the technical components such as the processor, available memory, and other hardware capabilities to keep up with the demands of the latest software.

iPhone software support timeline

To make it easier for you, I’ve compiled a table showing Apple’s support for every iPhone model, including its release and discontinuation dates.

Keep in mind that the dates are estimates based on past releases, with an average of 7 years of support. So, they may change in the future as newer devices and iOS versions become available.

What happens when Apple no longer supports your iPhone?

When Apple no longer supports your iPhone, it means the device will no longer receive software updates, including critical security patches and new features. Without these updates, your iPhone becomes increasingly vulnerable to security risks and compatibility issues with apps and services that require newer software versions.

However, the phone doesn’t suddenly stop working. You’ll still be able to use many of the features and apps that already work on the device.

But over time, certain apps may stop working altogether, and you may encounter performance problems with your iPhone as well.

Additionally, if your iPhone encounters hardware issues, you may find it difficult to get repairs or replacements from Apple or authorized service providers as they gradually phase out support for older models. Hence, it’s best to keep your device up-to-date and ensure it’s still supported by Apple.

What are the obsolete and vintage iPhones?

When we consider the question, “How many years does Apple support iPhones in terms of hardware?” here’s what the Apple Support website states:

“Owners of iPhone, iPad, iPod, Mac, Apple TV, Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple Vision Pro and Beats products may obtain a service and parts from Apple service providers for a minimum of five years* from when Apple last distributed the product for sale.”

This support may extend for up to seven years, depending on parts’ availability.

So, if your iPhone was still being sold by Apple up to 7 years ago, you could most likely get it fixed if you run into any issues. This is where we need to consider Apple’s list of obsolete and vintage iPhones.

Obsolete iPhones are those whose sales were discontinued by Apple more than 7 years ago, and as a result, hardware servicing is no longer available for them. Similarly, there are Vintage iPhones. These are those that have not been sold for more than 5 years (but fewer than 7 years). Apple can still service these devices, provided it has access to the needed parts.

Let’s see which iPhones belong to these categories.

What is the oldest iPhone still supported?

At the time of writing this—in October 2026—Apple still supports iOS 15, which means the iPhone 6S is the oldest device to receive occasional critical security updates. However, this model is also on Apple’s list of obsolete devices, so I recommend upgrading your device. The same applies to the first-generation iPhone SE.

Since Apple has discontinued support for iOS 12, the iPhone 5s, iPhone 6, and 6 Plus no longer receive software updates. Therefore, if you own an iPhone 6 or an older model, upgrading your iPhone is advisable.

Which iPhones are compatible with Apple Intelligence?

In June 2024, Apple announced Apple Intelligence, which is all set to revolutionize how you interact with your iPhone.

This advanced technology requires significant processing power, so it can only work on the latest iPhones. Currently, the iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, and iPhone 16 series and later are compatible with Apple Intelligence.

Of course, the upcoming iPhone 18 models are also expected to support this new technology.

Signing off

Apple does a great job of offering support for its iPhones. Thanks to this, you know your money is being invested in technology that will serve you well and last. In addition, it makes it worth buying an iPhone that’s a couple of years old—unless you absolutely need the latest and greatest hardware and software experience.

You can save this guide and refer to it whenever you want to check how long your iPhone will be supported. If you have further questions, let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

mainEntity.name: Will text messages show my number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

mainEntity.name: Is this supported worldwide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

title.rendered: How to stop the iOS 27 update while downloading

content.rendered:
Apple has finally rolled out iOS 27, bringing major changes, including the new Siri AI, expanded Apple Intelligence features, and several improvements across the native apps. But what if you’re not ready to install it yet?

I know plenty of iPhone users prefer to wait before jumping to a major iOS update. Maybe you want to see how the new version performs, you’re running low on storage, or you simply don’t want your iPhone to update right now.

The good news is that you can stop an iOS update before the installation actually begins. If the update has already been downloaded, you can also remove the update file from your iPhone’s storage.

Here’s how to stop an iOS 27 update in progress and prevent your iPhone from automatically downloading or installing future updates.

Can you stop an iPhone update in the middle? 

Yes, you can, but it depends on when you try to stop it. 

  • If the update is still downloading: Easy! You can cancel it right from your iPhone’s settings. 
  • If the update is preparing to install: You can usually still stop it by deleting the update file. 
  • If the update has already started installing: Sorry, at this stage you can’t stop it. Once your iPhone shows the Apple logo and progress bar, it has to finish installing. 

So, the trick is to catch it early, before your iPhone actually begins the installation process. 

How to cancel an iOS update in progress

While Apple doesn’t provide a pause or stop button for updates, you can still cancel an iOS update in progress if you haven’t started the installation process after downloading it.

An over-the-air iOS update generally involves two separate stages: your iPhone downloads the update and then prepares and installs it.

If the download is still underway, you can interrupt your internet connection. If the complete update has already been downloaded, you can remove it from your iPhone’s storage. But once you’ve started the installation, you cannot stop it midway. You must downgrade your iOS after the update is complete.

Here’s what I recommend doing.

Step 1: Stop the iOS update while it’s downloading

Your iPhone needs an active internet connection to download the update from Apple’s server. So, you’ll need to disconnect your iPhone from the internet to stop the download, as explained below:

  1. While the iOS update is downloading, open the Control Center.
  2. Enable Airplane Mode. The tile should turn orange when enabled.
  3. Make sure Wi-Fi is also disabled.

Once you toggle on Airplane Mode and disable Wi-Fi, the download will immediately pause as the connection is interrupted. You can verify the same by navigating to Settings → General → Software Update. Whatever you do, keep the iPhone in Airplane Mode until the next step is completed.

If the update has already finished downloading, move on to the next step.

Step 2: Delete the downloaded iOS update file

The next step is to delete the downloaded software update files. This will prevent the new iOS 27 update from continuing to install and free up storage on your iPhone. 

  1. Go to Settings → General → iPhone Storage. 
  2. Scroll down and tap the iOS update file → Tap Delete Update. 
  3. Finally, tap Delete Update again to confirm your action. 

Once the update file has been deleted, your iPhone won’t have the downloaded iOS 27 package available for installation. Still, you may follow the steps below to verify the update has been terminated before using your iPhone again: 

  1. Swipe down from the top-left corner to open the Control Center → Turn off Airplane Mode.  
  2. Go to Settings →  General → Software Update to ensure that the page has reverted to the initial update screen. If not, you may perform the previous steps again.  

The steps mentioned above will help you prevent the iOS update from installing on your iPhone for the time being. 

What if I can’t find the iOS 27 update in iPhone storage?

Don’t worry if you don’t see an iOS update listed under Settings → General → iPhone Storage. It generally means the update hasn’t been completely downloaded or there isn’t a removable update package currently stored on your iPhone.

If your iPhone is still showing that it is downloading an update, disconnect it from the internet first and give the download some time to stop.

If you still can’t remove the update or the installation continues, Apple recommends updating or restoring the iPhone using a Mac or PC in situations where normal updating doesn’t work.

How to turn off automatic updates on iPhone 

If you don’t want your iPhone to automatically download or install future iOS updates without your permission, you can change the automatic update settings.

Apple currently provides separate controls for automatically downloading and automatically installing iOS updates.

Here’s how to find them:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Select Automatic Updates → Then, toggle off Automatically Install.
  3. Now, an Automatically Download option appears. You must toggle it off If you don’t even want the iOS update package automatically downloaded to your iPhone. 
  4. You can also turn off Automatically Install under System Files.

From now on, your iPhone won’t automatically install the update overnight while charging and connected to Wi-Fi. You’ll still get a notification when a new update is available. 

Alternatively, instead of entirely turning off Automatic Updates on your iPhone, you can just toggle off Automatically Install. 

This way, your iPhone can still auto-download new iOS update files whenever a suitable network becomes available, but they won’t be installed without your knowledge. Every time, you need to check for the new update and tap the Update Now button. 

What happens if iOS 27 has already started installing?

This is where you need to be careful.

If your iPhone has already moved beyond downloading and preparation and is actively installing iOS 27, don’t try to interrupt the process. When you see the Apple logo with a progress bar, leave your iPhone connected to power and allow the installation to finish.

Turning off the iPhone or deliberately interrupting the installation at this stage can cause problems. If your iPhone becomes stuck during an update, Apple provides separate troubleshooting steps for completing the update or using recovery mode when necessary.

Can I stop iOS 27 beta updates too?

If you’re running an iOS beta, you can also control whether your iPhone continues receiving beta software through the Beta Updates setting.

However, turning off beta updates doesn’t downgrade your iPhone or remove the version you’re already running. It simply prevents your device from continuing on the beta update track.

If you want to return to a publicly released version of iOS, that’s a different process and may require restoring your iPhone, depending on the beta version and the version you want to install.

Signing off

By following the steps in this guide, you’ll be able to regain control over your iPhone and decide whether and when to install the latest iOS update. 

Not only that, but you can use the same steps to cancel beta updates for iOS in addition to canceling public releases of iOS updates that are in progress. 

For more awesome iOS hacks, check out the links below:

  • How to download and install iOS with mobile data
  • Can’t update apps on iPhone? How to fix it
  • Unable to Check for Update on iPhone? Here’s the Fix

mainEntity.name: Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

mainEntity.name: Will text messages show my number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

mainEntity.name: Is this supported worldwide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

keyPoints.title: Pausing and Removing iOS Update Files
keyPoints.explanation: You can pause a download by enabling Airplane Mode or disabling Wi-Fi and then delete the downloaded update file via Settings to maintain your current iOS version.

keyPoints.title: Stopping an iOS Download During Download
keyPoints.explanation: To cancel an ongoing iOS update download, disconnect your iPhone from the internet by enabling Airplane Mode and disabling Wi-Fi, then delete the update file from iPhone Storage.

keyPoints.title: How to Delete the Downloaded iOS Update File
keyPoints.explanation: Navigate to Settings > General > iPhone Storage, find the iOS update file, and delete it to prevent the installation of the new iOS version.

keyPoints.title: Verifying the Update Process Has Been Cancelled
keyPoints.explanation: After deleting the update file and disabling Airplane Mode, check the Software Update page in Settings to ensure the update process has been halted.

keyPoints.title: Disabling Automatic iOS Updates to Maintain Control
keyPoints.explanation: Go to Settings > General > Software Update > Automatic Updates and toggle off iOS updates to prevent automatic installations of future updates.

title.rendered: Roblox Navy War codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Navy War Codes on October 30, 2026

It’s time to set sail and take to the seas with Navy War on Roblox! In this game, you’ll build your very own fleet, develop your economy, upgrade your docks, and go toe-to-toe against other players in naval battles. There’s no shortage of action, as you’ll have powerful warships such as Destroyers, Cruisers, Submarines, Battleships, and more.

However, what you’ll need are tons of gems to strengthen your fleet, and that can be difficult to come by. Luckily, we’ve got you covered with a list of all working Navy War codes that can help you get hands on Gems for absolutely free!

All working Navy War codes

  • No active codes as of now.

As of now, these are the only active Navy War codes available. Make sure to redeem them as soon as possible, as codes often tend to expire, leaving you unable to claim rewards.

Expired or unverified Navy War codes

ADMIRALS, DECORATIONS, DIAMONDZ, KRAKEN, SORRYGUYS, SUPERSECRET

How to redeem Navy War codes

Now that you know all the active codes, it’s also crucial to know how to redeem them. Luckily, the process is quite simple and only takes a few minutes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to redeem Navy War codes:

  1. Fire up Navy War on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Open the shop from the left side of the screen and scroll all the way to the bottom
  4. Paste a working code and click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed the rewards, they should be added to your inventory automatically.

Where to find more Navy War codes

The developers don’t release new Navy War codes on a fixed schedule. Most new codes appear alongside major game updates, seasonal events, or community milestones.

To stay updated, you can:

  • Join the official Navy War Discord server for announcements.
  • Follow the game’s Roblox page for update notifications.
  • Bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated whenever new codes are released.

If you’re looking for more Roblox freebies, check out our latest Fabled Legacy codes, Roblox Slayers 2 codes, Hypershot codes and our complete Roblox Game Codes hub.

FAQs

Why is my Navy War code not working?

If your code isn’t working, make sure you’ve entered it correctly. If that doesn’t work, there’s a chance the code might’ve expired, or you’ve redeemed it already.

How do you earn money in Navy War?

You can earn money by building facilities and developing your base. All of the cash can be used to upgrade your fleet.

Can you play Navy War with friends?

Navy War features PvP battles where you can build your fleet and battle out against other players in the same server.

title.rendered: How to edit photos on iPhone like a pro with iOS 27

content.rendered:
Got a great shot that needs a little fixing? iOS 27 makes it super simple with several new editing tools. You can now remove unwanted objects with Clean Up, extend the edges of a photo with Extend, and even change a shot’s perspective with Reframe. Along with improved Photographic Styles, Adjust, Crop, Filters, and Markup tools, there’s a lot more you can do directly in the Photos app.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through what’s new in iOS 27 and how to master these tools to edit your photos on iPhone like a pro. 

Add 3D spatial depth effect to your photos

iOS 26 introduces Spatial Scenes, a brand-new feature that gives your regular photos a subtle 3D depth and motion effect. Using on-device machine learning, it separates the foreground and background, creating a layered scene that gently shifts as you move your phone.

It works especially well with portraits, landscapes, and photos that have clear subjects against a distinct background. Here’s how to turn a 2D photo into a Spatial Scene:

  1. Open the Photos app and select a photo.
  2. If the photo is eligible, you will see a hexagon icon. Tap it in the top-right corner.
  3. Wait a moment as iOS generates the depth effect.
  4. Tilt your iPhone or set the image as your wallpaper to see the 3D motion in action.

Note: Available on iPhone 12 and later, though results are more realistic on iPhone 15 Pro and newer models thanks to enhanced depth sensing and processing.

Use Apple Intelligence editing tools

iOS 27 Photos app adds Clean Up, Extend, and Reframe as Apple Intelligence photo-editing tools. They require an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or iPhone 16 model or later, and availability can vary by language and region.

Clean Up: Remove unwanted objects

With Apple Intelligence, you can remove photobombers or unwanted objects from your photos using the Clean Up tool. All you need to do is:

  1. Open the image and go to the editing interface.
  2. Tap Tools to get the AI editing features.
  3. Select Clean Up from the options.
  4. Tap, brush, or circle the object you want to remove. Some objects may be highlighted automatically.
  5. Clean Up tool will do its magic.
  6. Tap Undo if you want to restore something you removed.
  7. You may choose Auto, Fast, or High Quality processing. With High Quality selected, tap the Clean Up button to process the selected removal.
  8. Once satisfied, tap the checkmark, then tap Done again to close the photo.

Extend the Background

Extend uses Apple Intelligence to expand the edges of the original photo frame.

  1. Open the photo in Photos and tap Edit.
  2. Tap Tools, then tap Extend.
  3. Pinch or drag the photo to extend the background. You can also drag the edge of the frame to crop.
  4. Tap Extend to generate the expanded image.
  5. Tap the checkmark, then tap Done again to close the photo.
  6. To undo the saved Extend result, return to Tools > Extend and tap Reset.

Reframe the Perspective

Reframe lets you change the apparent point of capture after the photo has already been taken.

  1. Open the photo in Photos and tap Edit.
  2. Tap Tools, then tap Reframe.
  3. Touch and drag the photo to adjust its perspective. You can also use two fingers to pan, zoom, and rotate.
  4. Tap Reframe to apply the generated result.
  5. Tap the photo to compare the reframed version with the original.
  6. Once satisfied, tap the checkmark, then select Done again to close the photo.

Navigating the New Photos App in iOS 27 

The Photos app keeps the simplified layout, adapting the Liquid Glass UI. Tabs for Library and Collections have returned, and the new bottom-bar Edit button (three sliders icon) replaces the older top-corner Edit button. 

Here’s how to start editing any photo: 

  1. Go to the Photos app and open the photo you want to edit.
  2. Tap the Edit icon (three sliders) at the bottom of the screen. 
  3. You’ll now see tabs for Adjust, Styles, Crop, Portrait, and Markup, plus Tools if any AI-powered tools are available on your device. 

Adjust Lighting and Exposure

Once you’re on the editing interface, you’ll see multiple editing tools you can use to enhance your photo. Among these, the Adjust tool is where all the fun resides.

You can use the auto-enhance option here to have iOS adjust the image colors and tonality for you, or use the adjustment tools yourself to adjust photos manually. Here’s a list of all the adjustment tools you get in the Photos app:

  • Auto: Tap the auto button (magic wand icon) to let the iPhone apply automatic adjustments for lighting and color.
  • Exposure: Controls the amount of light in your image.
  • Brilliance: Improves brightness selectively, targeting underexposed areas while maintaining the contrast.
  • Highlights: Brightens the lighter areas.
  • Shadows: Enhances the darker areas.
  • Contrast: Increases the distinction between light and dark areas.
  • Brightness: Lets you make your image lighter or darker. Unlike exposure, it affects all pixels in a photo (and not just highlights).
  • Black Point: Adjusts the depth of black in your image, adding contrast and richness, giving your photos a more dramatic feel.
  • Saturation: Makes colors pop, adding vibrancy to your photos.
  • Vibrance: Works similarly to saturation, but only muted colors are affected by it.
  • Warmth: Adjusts the color temperature.
  • Tint: Adds subtle color shifts, perfect for correcting color imbalances.
  • Sharpness: Enhances fine details, though increasing sharpness too much may add visual noise.
  • Definition: Adds clarity and detail to your photo without affecting brightness, which helps make details pop.
  • Noise Reduction: Reduces visual noise and grain, especially in low-light photos, making them appear smoother.
  • Vignette: Adds a subtle shadow around the edges of the photo, drawing focus to the center.

You can access and use any of these adjustment tools like this:

  1. Tap Adjust at the bottom.
  2. Choose one of the currently visible adjustments or swipe right on them to reveal others.
  3. After you select the one you want to mingle with, use the slider below to control it.
  4. Once satisfied, tap Done in the top-right corner to save the changes.

In iOS 27, the adjustment slider animations are smoother, and changes update in real time.

Crop Photos Automatically

While you could always manually crop photos on an iPhone, the latest iOS version can crop photos and adjust the alignment automatically for you. Here’s how to crop photos automatically:

  1. In the editing interface, select the Crop tool in the bottom toolbar.
  2. To crop manually, drag the corners of the crop rectangle or pinch to adjust the crop.
  3. For a preset, tap the aspect-ratio control and choose a ratio such as Square, Wallpaper, 9:16, or 5:7.
  4. Tap the Auto button at the top, and iOS will automatically crop the photo and adjust its alignment.
  5. Hit Done to save.

You can also Rotate, Flip, and Straighten your image right from this interface. What I do is zoom the photo to the level I want to keep and tap the Done button.

Add a Filter to Photos

Other than adjusting the lighting and exposure or cropping the image, you can also add a filter to your photos if you don’t like a photo’s original look. It’s available on iPhone 16e, iPhone 15 series, and previous models. This is what you need to do:

  1. Tap the edit button below the photo you want to edit.
  2. Tap on Filters.
  3. Swipe right through the available filters to try different ones and choose the most appropriate.
  4. Save the image by tapping Done.

On newer generations, like iPhone Air, iPhone 17 series, and iPhone 18 Pro models, Apple uses Photographic Styles to provide a customized look for each image.

Edit Photographic Styles of a Photo

If you own the latest iPhone 16 or later and have enabled it, Filter is replaced by Photographic Styles. Instead of applying a preset look, it adjusts parameters like tone, warmth, and contrast to change the image’s mood while preserving natural skin tones and detail.

In iOS 26 and later, Apple finally lets you edit Photographic Styles even after capturing a photo in High-Efficiency.

  1. In the editing interface, tap the Style icon.
  2. Swipe left or right to choose another available style.
  3. Tap Customize to adjust tone and colour, then use the intensity slider.
  4. On iPhone 18 Pro models, select Palette, then drag the slider below to adjust the intensity level. Tap Texture, then choose a texture such as Soft Skin, Glow, or Film. Next, tap Grain to add film grain to any texture.
  5. Tap Done to save.

Check out our detailed guide on using Photographic Styles to learn everything about the feature.

Markup Your Photos

The Markup tool on iPhone lets you draw, add text, create shapes, and even add stickers and your signature to photos, allowing you to give a more creative touch to your photos. Here’s how to use it:

  1. On the photo editing interface, tap the Markup button (pen icon) in the top-right corner.
  2. Once you are in Markup mode, you’ll notice a row of drawing tools at the bottom. Choose the preferred drawing tool.
  3. You can simply draw any rough shape and keep holding it, and the iPhone will automatically transform it into a perfect one.
  4. Tap the drawing tool again to adjust the thickness and opacity. You can also change the color using the color wheel icon.
  5. Tap the checkmark at the top to save.

Add Stickers, text, and more to a photo

Other than drawing over photos, the Markup tool offers several other useful tools as well to help you add stickers, adjust color, and do more, right in the Photos app.

From the editing interface, select the Markup icon, tap the plus icon at the bottom right corner, and choose any of the following:

  • Add Text: It adds a text box to let you type in. You can adjust the font, size, and color. Tap the text box to move it, or use the handles to resize it.
  • Add Stickers: Select one of the many available stickers on your iPhone.
  • Add Shapes: Choose from shapes like squares, circles, speech bubbles, and arrows. Shapes are perfect for highlighting specific areas of your photo.
  • Add Image Description: Enter a suitable description to use with VoiceOver.

Once you are done, tap the checkmark at the top to save your additions.

Copy and Paste Edits to Multiple Photos

Have multiple photos and want to make similar edits on all of them? Well, you can batch-edit photos on your iPhone by copying the edits made on a single photo and pasting them to multiple photos in just a few taps. Here’s how:

  1. Open the edited photo.
  2. Tap the three-dot button in the top-right corner and select Copy Edits from the menu.
  3. Now, toggle on the edits you want to copy, like Filter, Crop, etc. Ensure to turn on Adaptive as it adjusts the edits for each image automatically.
  4. Finally, tap Copy.
  5. Now, return to your Photos app library and select the photos you want to edit.
  6. Tap the three-dot button in the top-right corner and tap Paste Edits.

Photos automatically adjusts white balance and exposure when pasted edits are applied, helping the edited images match more closely.

Bonus: Preview App Editing

The new Preview app on iPhone allows light image editing, annotation, background removal, and file conversion, just like on macOS. 

Use Preview for: 

  • Cropping, rotating, resizing, and background removal. 
  • Annotating PDFs and images. 
  • Signing or marking documents right from your phone. 

Pro tips to get the most out of iOS 27 photo editing

  • Update your iPhone to the latest iOS version to enjoy all the features.
  • Use Auto Enhance first to set a baseline, then fine-tune manually.  
  • Don’t overuse the Clean Up tool, as it can make photos look artificial. For best results, zoom in and erase small distractions instead of large areas.
  • If you use Spatial Scenes, test them as wallpapers. They look stunning!
  • To edit more precisely, you can change the interface theme. Tap the edit button > the three-dot icon at the top > Appearance, and select between Dark and Light.
  • Every edit in Photos is non-destructive. If a photo doesn’t look right, tap the three-dot icon at the top and select Revert to Original to instantly undo all changes.

Edit Photos Like a Pro!

Now that you know about various editing tools available in the Photos app in iOS 27, you can easily edit photos on your iPhone like a pro. The new pro-level adjustment tools and AI-powered features, among others, ensure you don’t have to depend on any third-party apps to edit your photos unless you need to do something specific that the Photos app can’t help you with.

Feel free to reach out to us via comments if you have questions or doubts.

FAQs

What should I do if the editing tool isn’t working?

Try force-quitting the Photos app or restarting your iPhone. It can help eliminate any software bug that could be causing trouble when trying to access or use the editing tool in the Photos app.

Can I revert my edited photos back to their original version?

Yes, you can. Go to the Photos app, open the edited photo, tap the three-dot button, and select Revert to Original.

keyPoints.title: New Simplified Layout of Photos App in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26 introduces a more streamlined Photos app with Liquid Glass UI, returning to tabs for Library and Collections and adding a bottom-bar Edit button for easier access to editing tools.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Photo Editing Interface and Tools
keyPoints.explanation: The editing interface now features tabs for Adjust, Filters, Crop, and Markup, along with AI-powered tools, making photo editing more accessible and powerful for users.

keyPoints.title: Advanced Lighting, Exposure, and Color Adjustment Options
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26 offers a wide range of adjustment tools like auto-enhance, exposure, contrast, saturation, and vibrance, with smoother sliders and real-time updates for professional-level edits.

keyPoints.title: Automatic Cropping, Filtering, and Photographic Styles
keyPoints.explanation: You can now auto-crop photos, apply filters, or customize Photographic Styles to change the mood and look of your images, with style editing available even after shooting.

keyPoints.title: Innovative 3D Spatial Depth and Object Removal Features
keyPoints.explanation: Spatial Scenes add 3D depth effects, while the Clean Up tool uses Apple Intelligence to remove unwanted objects, both enhancing photo creativity and precision.

title.rendered: 40 Apple Watch tips and tricks I wish I knew sooner on watchOS 27

content.rendered:
I’ve owned and used Apple Watch long enough to think I knew most of its tricks. Then watchOS 27 arrived, changing the interface in several small but meaningful ways.

The new dynamic app grid, one-handed Smart Stack controls, Siri AI, smarter suggestions, and the redesigned Find My experience are easy to miss if you simply update and continue using the watch the way you did before.

Here are the Apple Watch tips and tricks I think are actually worth knowing.

1. Use Single Tap to control Smart Stack with one hand

This is probably my favorite small watchOS 27 trick.

Apple added a Single Tap gesture that lets you select a Smart Stack widget without touching the screen.

From the watch face:

  1. Perform a Double Tap to open Smart Stack.
  2. Double-tap again to move through the widgets.
  3. When you reach the widget you want, perform a Single Tap to open it.
  4. You can also use a single tap to select certain buttons inside a widget, such as Play or Pause.
  5. Perform a wrist flick to return to the watch face.

After testing, I realized how useful it is when my other hand is occupied. For example, when you’re carrying something, cooking, walking, or simply don’t want to touch the screen, you can navigate Smart Stack with your fingers on the same wrist.

Note: Tap Gestures require a compatible Apple Watch and aren’t available in every situation, such as when the watch is locked or certain accessibility features are active.

2. Let Smart Stack predict what you need

I used to think of Smart Stack as just a collection of widgets. watchOS 27 changed the way I think about it.

Smart Stack can now surface suggestions based on things such as your time of day, location, and recent activity.

For example, your watch may surface:

  • A workout suggestion around your usual workout time
  • Your parked car location
  • A birthday reminder
  • A travel card
  • A relevant Live Activity
  • Other information based on your routine

When the watch thinks something is immediately useful, it can even tap your wrist and show a small suggestion at the bottom of the watch face. Tap the suggestion to open Smart Stack.

Thus, you don’t have to remember where everything is.

3. Pin your most important Smart Stack widgets

There’s a simple way to stop your favorite Smart Stack widgets from getting lost.

Open Smart Stack → scroll to the bottom → tap Edit.

From here, you can:

  • Add widgets
  • Remove widgets
  • Pin widgets
  • Rearrange pinned widgets
  • Customize certain widgets

I recommend pinning only the things you genuinely check throughout the day.

For example, I would rather have Weather, Calendar, Battery, Reminders, or Home controls immediately available than fill Smart Stack with widgets I rarely open.

4. Try the new dynamic app grid

This is one of the biggest navigation changes in watchOS 27.

Press the Digital Crown to open the Home Screen.

Instead of simply treating the app grid as a static collection of icons, watchOS 27 now uses a dynamic app grid that highlights Siri-suggested apps, including apps you use frequently and recently. The Siri app remains in the center.

This makes the Home Screen feel less like a tiny iPhone and more like a launcher that adapts to how I use my watch.

You can still touch and hold an app to rearrange it.

5. Use Siri AI for more than timers and weather

For years, I mostly used Siri on Apple Watch for simple commands like “Set a timer,” “What’s the weather?” or “Start a workout.”

Siri AI in watchOS 27 makes the assistant considerably more interesting. On supported devices, Siri AI can understand more natural requests, use personal context, answer broader questions, and take actions in supported apps.

You can ask things such as:

  • “What’s on my calendar today?”
  • “Set my Move goal to 600 calories.”
  • “Find the information about my flight.”
  • “Start directions home.”
  • “Play the music I was listening to earlier.”

Siri AI is still marked as a beta feature, and availability depends on your Apple Watch, paired iPhone, language, and region.

6. Revisit previous Siri conversations

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app where you can view previous conversations, continue them, or start a new one. That makes Siri feel less like a one-question-at-a-time assistant.

If you started something on another Apple device, the conversation can also be available across devices when the relevant iCloud features are enabled.

For someone who uses Siri frequently, this is much more useful than having every interaction disappear as soon as the answer is given.

7. Get useful information while you’re on a business call

watchOS 27 introduces Call Context, which can surface relevant information from your apps while you’re calling a business.

Imagine calling an airline. Instead of switching between apps to find your reservation or confirmation code, your Apple Watch can surface relevant information from Mail when appropriate.

It’s a small feature, but this is exactly where I think a smartwatch makes sense: giving me information at the moment I need it without making me dig through my phone.

8. Use Live Activities from your wrist

Live Activities can now make the Apple Watch more useful for ongoing events.

The Smart Stack can show real-time information for supported activities such as:

  • Workouts
  • Timers
  • Other supported app activities

Instead of repeatedly opening an app to check what’s happening, you can glance at the Live Activity or tap it for more information.

If you don’t want Live Activities appearing automatically, you can manage them from: Settings → Smart Stack → Live Activities

9. Customize Control Center properly

The Control Center on your Apple Watch gives you quick access to certain functions, such as activating silent mode, toggling on Airplane mode and more. While the default Control Center does its job pretty well, you can customize it by rearranging, adding, or removing the control icons.

  1. Press the side button to open Control Center.
  2. Scroll to the bottom → tap Edit.
  3. Now you can:
    • Rearrange controls
    • Add controls
    • Remove controls

You can also add supported controls from apps such as Home, Notes, Reminders, and Shortcuts.

Tip: Don’t organize Control Center according to Apple’s default layout. I put the things I actually use most, such as Ping iPhone, Flashlight, Battery, Focus, and Water Lock, where I can reach them quickly. That saves me from opening an app just to perform a two-second action.

10. Turn on Water Lock before swimming

This is one of those features I knew about but didn’t fully appreciate until I actually needed it.

When you’re swimming or doing a water-based workout, turn on Water Lock. You can access it through Control Center.

Water Lock prevents accidental screen interactions while you’re in the water.

When you’re finished, press and hold the Digital Crown to unlock the watch. Your Apple Watch will play sounds to help eject water from the speaker.

11. Use the wrist flick when your hands are full

This is another watchOS gesture that quickly became one of my favorites.

Quickly turn your wrist away from you and back.

Depending on what you’re doing, the Wrist Flick gesture can:

  • Dismiss notifications
  • Silence an incoming call
  • Stop a timer
  • Return to the watch face
  • Dismiss other alerts

It’s especially useful when I’m carrying something and don’t have a free hand.

12. Cover the display to mute an alert

If you don’t want to use Wrist Flick, there’s an older trick that’s still incredibly handy.

When your Apple Watch starts ringing or making an alert sound, simply place the palm of your other hand over the display. The watch will mute the alert.

You can check the setting under: Settings → Gestures → Cover to Mute

I like this because it feels almost instinctive when I’m in a meeting.

13. Double Tap can do much more than answer calls

If you have a compatible Apple Watch, the Double Tap gesture lets you tap your index finger and thumb together twice to perform supported actions.

Depending on the situation, you can use it to:

  • Answer or end calls
  • Reply to messages
  • Scroll through supported apps
  • Scroll through Smart Stack
  • Snooze an alarm
  • Stop a timer
  • Control media
  • Take a photo using Camera Remote
  • Record a voice memo
  • Pause or resume a stopwatch

However, note that Double Tap and Single Tap aren’t the same thing. Double Tap handles common actions, while Single Tap can select a Smart Stack widget.

14. Make your watch face work harder

I used to choose watch faces based mostly on how they looked. Now I choose them based on how much information they can give me without opening an app.

Touch and hold your current watch face → swipe left or right → tap Add to choose another face. When customizing it, think carefully about your complications.

I prefer complications for things I check frequently:

  • Weather
  • Calendar
  • Battery
  • Activity
  • Workout
  • Music
  • Timers
  • Reminders
  • Maps

A good watch face should reduce the number of times you need to open an app.

15. Try the Siri Modular watch face

watchOS 27 also introduces the Siri Modular watch face.

It is designed around quick access to Siri and includes a large complication area that can surface information from Smart Stack.

If you use Siri regularly, this is one of the watch faces I’d try instead of simply sticking with whichever face you have always used.

16. Make the Always On display work for you

If your Apple Watch supports Always On, you don’t have to choose between keeping it enabled and showing everything while your wrist is down.

  1. Go to Settings → Display & Brightness → Always On.
  2. You can manage which information is visible when the display is dimmed, including complications, notifications, and Live Activities, depending on your model and settings.

I prefer customizing this rather than automatically switching Always On off.

17. Quickly switch between your last two apps

This remains one of the fastest Apple Watch shortcuts.

  1. Double-click the Digital Crown.
  2. Your watch switches between the current app and the previous app.

It’s particularly useful when you’re bouncing between two apps, for example, Messages and Music or Workout and another app.

If you need the full App Switcher rather than simply jumping between two apps, double-click the Digital Crown to open it. From there, you can browse your recently used apps and tap the one you need. It’s much quicker than going back to the Home Screen every time.

18. Remove apps you never use

Most people don’t need every compatible iPhone app sitting on their Apple Watch.

  1. Press the Digital Crown.
  2. Find the app and touch and hold it.
  3. Tap the Delete button when available.

You can also delete apps through the Watch app on your iPhone. Go to Watch app → My Watch. Then manage which apps appear on your watch.

I prefer keeping only the apps that make sense on a small screen.

19. Use the Digital Crown to view the time discreetly

Let’s say you are in a dark environment, like a movie theatre or during meetings, where you don’t want to disturb others with a bright screen when checking the time.

In such cases, you can slowly rotate the Digital Crown upwards while your watch is in sleep mode, and the screen will gradually brighten, showing the time without fully illuminating.

Stop rotating the Digital Crown once the screen is illuminated enough to check the time. Leave the Digital Crown, and the display will automatically dim, or rotate the Digital Crown downwards to dim it manually.

20. Increase the text size when reading feels uncomfortable

If the text on your Apple Watch feels too small, don’t just squint at it.

  1. Go to Settings → Display & Brightness → Text Size
  2. Adjust the slider until the text feels comfortable.

You can also use the Watch app on iPhone to manage display-related settings.

21. Have Apple Watch announce the time

Wake the display and place two fingers on the watch face. The Apple Watch can announce the time aloud.

If it doesn’t work, check Settings → Clock → Speak Time. Alternatively, you can use a tap to hear the time.

I particularly like this when I’m cooking or working and don’t want to stop what I’m doing just to look at the screen.

22. Get a gentle chime every 15, 30, or 60 minutes

If you like having a subtle reminder of time passing, Apple Watch can play a chime at regular intervals.

  1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Chimes.
  2. Turn on Chimes.
  3. Then choose a schedule such as:
    • Every 15 minutes
    • Every 30 minutes
    • Every hour
  4. You can also choose the sound.

I wouldn’t recommend this for everyone, but if you work in timed blocks or simply like a periodic reminder, it’s surprisingly useful.

23. Keep two time zones on your wrist

This is one of the Apple Watch features I think more people should know about.

If you regularly deal with people in another country, travel frequently, or simply need to keep an eye on another time zone, use the GMT watch face.

  1. On your iPhone: Watch app → Face Gallery → GMT
  2. Add it to your Apple Watch.
  3. The inner portion shows your local time, while the outer ring can show another time zone.

You can rotate the Digital Crown to change the selected city.

To add a city of your choice, go to the World Clock section of the iPhone Clock app. Now add the city here. After that, it will appear in the list of cities added to the GMT watch face.

I find this particularly useful when working with people in another country. I can glance at my wrist before sending a message instead of doing the time-zone calculation in my head.

24. Set your Apple Watch a few minutes ahead

I actually like setting a traditional watch five minutes ahead, and the Apple Watch lets me do the same.

  1. Go to Settings → Clock → +0 min.
  2. Tap +0 min and increase it by 1 to 59 minutes, as desired.
  3. Finally, tap Set.

The important part is that this changes the displayed time, not the actual system time.

So if I set it five minutes ahead, the watch face might show 10:05 when the actual time is 10:00, but alarms, notifications, and other time-based functions continue using the actual time.

25. Use the Apple Watch keyboard when you need to type

On compatible Apple Watch models, you can type directly on the display using the built-in keyboard.

Open an app such as Messages or Mail and tap a text field.

You can:

  • Tap individual letters
  • Swipe across letters using QuickPath
  • Use dictation
  • Add emoji

For anything longer than a sentence, I still prefer dictation. But for short replies, the keyboard is much more useful than I expected. You can also send a Tapback and share/forward the message from your watch.

26. Dictate messages instead of typing them

If typing on the small screen isn’t your thing, tap the microphone and dictate your response.

Depending on the app and message interface, you can send the transcription as text or use an audio message.

I use dictation when I’m walking or when the keyboard feels like more effort than the message itself.

27. Take a screenshot of your Apple Watch

Need to capture what’s on your Apple Watch display? You can quickly take a screenshot on the Apple Watch.

  1. Press the Digital Crown and side button simultaneously.
  2. The screenshot is saved to the Photos app on your paired iPhone.

If screenshots aren’t working, check Settings → General → Screenshots and make sure the screenshot feature is enabled.

This is particularly useful when you’re writing a tutorial or want to share a particular watch screen with someone.

28. Use Apple Watch as a flashlight

Many of you might not know that your Apple Watch’s screen can function as a Flashlight when needed.

  1. Press the side button and tap Flashlight.
  2. The display becomes bright white.
  3. You can swipe to access different modes, including a red light mode.

It won’t replace your iPhone flashlight for serious illumination, but it’s excellent for finding something beside the bed or walking through a dark room.

29. Find your iPhone from your wrist

If you’ve misplaced your iPhone, you can use your Apple Watch to locate it using the Ping My iPhone feature.

  1. Open Control Center and tap Ping iPhone.
  2. Your iPhone will make a sound so you can find it.

 If you own an iPhone 15 and Apple Watch Series 9 or a later model, you can also view the exact distance between the two devices.

30. Find people, devices, and AirTags from one app

watchOS 27 consolidates Find Devices, Find People, and Find Items into the Find My app.

Open Find My on your Apple Watch to access the things you need to locate. The new map-focused experience makes it easier to see where people, devices, and items are.

This is a nice example of a watchOS 27 change that isn’t flashy but makes the Apple Watch feel more coherent.

31. Check your AirPods battery from your wrist

If your AirPods are connected, you can check their battery from your Apple Watch.

  1. Open Control Center and tap the battery percentage.
  2. Depending on your connected devices, you’ll see additional battery information.

I use this before leaving the house because it’s much easier than opening the iPhone just to check whether my earbuds have enough charge.

Also read: How to check iPhone battery percentage on Apple Watch

32. Use Apple Watch as an iPhone camera remote

This is one of my favorite practical Apple Watch features.

Open Camera Remote on your Apple Watch. Your iPhone camera opens, and the watch gives you a preview and shutter control.

It’s great for:

  • Group photos
  • Selfies
  • Trip photos
  • Long-distance shots
  • Photos where you want the iPhone completely steady

The best part is that you don’t need to run back to the phone after setting up the shot.

33. Transfer an Apple Watch call to your iPhone

Sometimes answering a call on the Apple Watch is convenient.

But a five-minute call can suddenly become a 30-minute conversation. When that happens, transfer the call to your iPhone rather than holding your wrist next to your face.

Answer the call on your Apple Watch, then use the option to transfer the audio to your iPhone.

It’s one of those features that makes more sense once you’ve actually been stuck in a long call on your wrist.

34. Use Workout Buddy during your workouts

Workout Buddy is one of the more interesting Apple Intelligence additions to Apple Watch.

It can provide motivational feedback and insights based on your workout, including information about:

  • Pace
  • Distance
  • Workout duration
  • Progress

On supported setups, Workout Buddy can also work when your paired iPhone isn’t nearby, as long as your Apple Watch has Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.

For runners, this is one of the watchOS features worth trying.

35. Get better treadmill distance tracking

If you’ve ever looked down at your Apple Watch after a treadmill workout and wondered why the distance doesn’t match the treadmill, watchOS 27 has a useful improvement.

Apple has updated its distance calculations for treadmill walking and running. The Workout app can now calculate indoor distance more accurately from the beginning of a workout.

So if you regularly run indoors, make sure you’re running the latest watchOS before assuming the watch’s distance estimates are hopelessly inaccurate.

36. Use Apple Watch for transit and payments

Apple Watch can be used for Apple Pay wherever supported.

In supported cities, you can also use eligible transit cards and payment methods for public transportation, such as metro, train, and bus rides. The real convenience comes from not having to pull your iPhone out of your pocket every time you need to tap.

Availability depends on your country, transit system, card, and bank.

37. Keep track of your sleep automatically

Apple Watch can track sleep and help you establish a consistent sleep routine.

The important part is setting up your sleep schedule properly and wearing the watch to bed.

Once configured, the watch can automatically collect your sleep information instead of requiring you to manually start tracking every night.

I think this is one of the Apple Watch features where consistency matters much more than constantly checking the data.

38. Use the Apple Watch for directions

The traveler, hiker, or biker in you will love this little feature. Apple Watch has the Compass app, which allows you to see directions straight on your wrist. Furthermore, you can even get cycling directions on your Apple Watch using Apple Maps.

39. Unlock your Mac with your Apple Watch

If you use both a Mac and Apple Watch, you can enable automatic unlocking.

Once configured, your Mac can recognize your nearby Apple Watch and authenticate you without requiring you to type your password every time. It can also help with authentication for supported macOS actions, such as approving payments.

This is one of those features I barely notice when it’s working, and immediately miss when I use a Mac without it.

40. Use Apple Watch as a tiny second screen for your iPhone

The Apple Watch isn’t supposed to replace your iPhone. It’s supposed to save you from reaching for it.

Use the watch for the things that benefit from being immediate:

  • Check a notification
  • Start or stop a workout
  • Check the weather
  • Find your iPhone
  • Check a boarding pass
  • Control music
  • Check a timer
  • See a Live Activity
  • Answer a short message
  • Ask Siri something
  • Control your smart home
  • Take a photo remotely
  • Find an AirTag
  • Check another time zone

The more I use it this way, the less I feel the need to turn the Apple Watch into a miniature iPhone.

Bottom line

The Apple Watch can do much more than show notifications, track workouts, and tell the time. With watchOS 27, there are even more small features and shortcuts that can make it more useful in everyday life.

I’d suggest trying a few of these tips and keeping the ones that fit into your routine. You don’t need to use every feature; just finding a few shortcuts that save you time can make a big difference.

Which Apple Watch trick did you discover for the first time while reading this list?

mainEntity.name: Does hiding the Caller ID hide my number from everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It prevents your number from being displayed through normal Caller ID, but your carrier still knows which number placed the call. Certain emergency or specialized services may also handle caller information differently.

mainEntity.name: Will text messages show my number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Caller ID hiding only affects voice calls, not SMS or iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Does hiding Caller ID work with FaceTime?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. FaceTime has separate Caller ID controls. You can choose whether your phone number or Apple Account email address is used for FaceTime Caller ID in Settings > Apps > FaceTime.

mainEntity.name: Is this supported worldwide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most countries support Caller ID blocking, but availability varies by carrier.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the editing tool isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Try force-quitting the Photos app or restarting your iPhone. It can help eliminate any software bug that could be causing trouble when trying to access or use the editing tool in the Photos app.

mainEntity.name: Can I revert my edited photos back to their original version?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can. Go to the Photos app, open the edited photo, tap the three-dot button, and select Revert to Original.

title.rendered: OpenAI launches Dots, always-on AI agents in ChatGPT

content.rendered:
OpenAI has launched Dots, personal AI agents that keep working on ongoing goals between conversations. They use GPT-6 Astra, have their own cloud computer and browser, and can connect to more than 4,000 apps through plugins.

Announced on September 29, Dots are rolling out to Pro, Business Premium, and eligible Enterprise workspaces. You can name your primary dot, give it responsibilities, and return later to review its work or change direction.

Dots keep track of work between conversations

A dot retains project context and learns from feedback, so you do not have to repeat the same instructions each time. It can coordinate tasks using Codex and connected tools, building on ChatGPT Work and the earlier ChatGPT Agent.

OpenAI’s examples include turning interview transcripts into show notes and draft social posts, updating presentations when new figures arrive, and preparing tested software fixes from customer feedback. One early tester’s dot noticed an unsent invoice, prepared it, and sent it after approval.

You can also ask for reminders or recurring checks and follow activity from the dot’s profile. These are intended capabilities, and results still need review.

Who gets Dots, and what does it cost?

Access depends on your plan and region. The initial rollout covers:

  • Pro: Markets outside the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK.
  • Business Premium: All supported ChatGPT regions.
  • Enterprise, including Edu and Healthcare: Beta access when an administrator enables it; off by default.

Free, Go, Plus, and Business Standard are not included in the announced initial rollout. Dots are unavailable to users under 18, and eligible accounts may take several days to receive access. India is not among the listed Pro exclusions.

Your first dot is included in Pro or Business Premium at no extra cost. Individual Pro plans currently cost $100, $200, or $500 per month, with different usage allowances.

Conversations with a dot do not count toward ChatGPT usage limits. Tasks it starts or manages in Codex or ChatGPT Work use the usual allowances. OpenAI is extending deeper-work limits for the first month; always-on access does not mean unlimited tasks.

How to set up and reach your dot

Create your dot in the ChatGPT desktop app or a desktop browser, name it, connect the apps it needs, and describe your goal. Include boundaries such as asking before sharing a document or sending an email.

After setup, you can message it in the ChatGPT mobile app when mobile access is available. You cannot currently create a dot on mobile, and mobile web is unsupported.

Dots can carry context across ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams, where available. Texting is planned more broadly, with a limited beta already listed for some US Pro users. That beta is unavailable in Business and Enterprise workspaces. Dots cannot initiate calls or have their own standalone email address at launch.

What it can access and do on its own

Your dot’s cloud computer is separate from your laptop. Local computer access starts turned off; you must connect it before the dot can work with local files and tools.

App permissions are shared across Dots, ChatGPT, Work, and Codex, so review existing connections too. For supported website logins, secure sign-in keeps passwords outside the model’s conversation.

Background proactive research uses read-only tools. Those tools cannot directly send messages, edit connected apps, or control a browser or desktop. Follow-up actions must pass the usual permissions and safety checks.

Custom Rules let you set action boundaries. Auto-review checks certain actions against your instructions, while sensitive steps such as changing a password stay with you. You can inspect progress, redirect work, or pause the dot from its profile.

Memory, privacy, and enterprise controls

Dots can retain context from conversations, ChatGPT memories, and connected apps. Disconnecting an app stops new access but does not erase retained information. Individual dot memories cannot currently be viewed or edited; deleting the dot removes its own context, while separately stored files and ChatGPT memories need their own controls.

Business, Enterprise, and Edu data is excluded from model training by default. Personal users can control eligible use through Improve the model for everyone.

Enterprise admins can manage app, messaging, and computer capabilities. Only a dot’s owner can direct it; another person’s mention does not start work. OpenAI is also piloting specialist dots with dedicated organizational responsibilities and working on Microsoft Agent 365 integration.

Teams of dots, broader access, and options for more work capacity are planned. For now, users start with a primary dot and should review consequential work before relying on it.

title.rendered: Apple Pay launches in India with Axis Bank credit cards

content.rendered:
Apple Pay is officially available in India, starting with Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards. Customers can add an eligible card to Wallet and use their iPhone or Apple Watch for contactless payments, with in-app and web checkout also available on iPhone and iPad.

Apple announced the launch on September 30, following earlier reports of a September or October rollout. Mac support is coming soon.

Which cards and devices are supported?

The initial rollout covers Axis Bank Visa and Mastercard credit cards. Apple has not announced support for Axis debit cards, RuPay cards, other Indian banks, or UPI in this release. Having an Axis account alone is not enough; your credit card must be eligible.

Apple lists these requirements for India:

  • iPhone: iPhone XR or later, running iOS 18 or later.
  • Apple Watch: Series 6 or later, running watchOS 11 or later, paired with iPhone XR or later.
  • iPad: Supported for in-app and web payments. The announcement does not specify a separate India model list.

You need an Apple Account signed in on the device and a passcode set up. Keep your software updated and enable two-factor authentication for your Apple Account.

How to add your Axis Bank card and pay

You can add a supported card through the latest Axis Bank app or directly in Wallet:

  1. Open Wallet and tap the plus button.
  2. Select Debit or Credit Card, then Continue.
  3. Scan your card or enter its details manually.
  4. Complete the bank’s verification prompts.

For Apple Watch, use Watch app → My Watch → Wallet & Apple Pay → Add Card on your paired iPhone. On iPad, use Settings → Wallet & Apple Pay → Add Card.

At a contactless terminal, double-click your iPhone’s side button, authenticate with Face ID or your passcode, and hold the top of the phone near the reader until Done appears. Supported Touch ID devices use the Home button. On Apple Watch, double-click the side button and hold the display near the reader.

Online or in apps, select Apple Pay, review the payment and shipping details, and authenticate. Our Apple Pay setup guide explains the general process.

Where it works, fees, and UPI limits

Launch merchants include Apple Stores, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato. Apple has worked with payment providers including Cashfree, Juspay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline.

Look for contactless acceptance in stores or an Apple Pay button at checkout. The merchant must also accept your card and its payment network.

Apple charges no fee for using the service. Your issuer’s usual card charges still apply, and existing rewards and benefits continue. Overseas purchases remain subject to your bank’s international usage rules and fees.

In-store payments on iPhone and Apple Watch work without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Transaction history may refresh after you reconnect.

The launch does not include UPI integration, so ordinary UPI QR payments and bank transfers still need your UPI app. Participating websites may offer an Apple Pay QR checkout, but that is a separate payment flow. Apple Cash remains US-only.

Security, refunds, and card errors

Apple Pay uses a device-specific payment number and a unique transaction security code instead of sharing your actual card number with merchants. If your device goes missing, Find My’s Lost Mode suspends Apple Pay.

Refunds follow the merchant’s policy and return to your payment card. Some merchants need the last four digits of the Apple Pay card number, which differs from your physical card number. Find it under Wallet → your card → More → Card Number.

If Wallet shows Could Not Add Card, Invalid Card, or Card Device Limit, check your card eligibility, device software, and account security, then contact Axis Bank. The bank approves cards for Apple Pay; Apple does not.

Apple has not announced when more Indian banks or card types will join the service.

title.rendered: Fortnite x FNAF collab: All skins and cosmetics revealed so far

content.rendered:
Five Nights At Freddy’s (FNAF) is arriving in Fortnite in an influential way, with a wide range of skins, related cosmetics, and gameplay updates in the pipeline for October 1. It is the first major IP collaboration confirmed by Epic’s highly popular multiplayer game for their forthcoming Halloween event titled ‘Fortnitemares‘.

Over the past few weeks, rumors and speculation surrounding an imminent Fortnite x FNAF collab had been running strong in the community. This was finally confirmed when the game’s official social channels teased such a partnership.

Since then, several leaks have followed and given Fortnite players a good look at what to expect. The following article lists all such confirmed and leaked FNAF-inspired content that has surfaced so far.

Fortnite x FNAF crossover skins

One recent teaser video posted by Fortnite showed Five Nights at Freddy’s antagonists, namely Freddy Fazbear, Chica the Chicken, Bonnie the Bunny, and Foxy the Pirate Fox, in action. Notably, these characters were also depicted in the clip from the player character’s camera view, which strongly suggested their inclusion as character skins.

It’s worth mentioning that Freddy, Chica, and Bonnie are also seen stalking and chasing the player, which might point at a few of these characters being available as an in-game boss. However, this interpretation is highly speculative.

Other leaked FNAF cosmetics coming to Fortnite

As noted by popular leaker HYPEX, a combination of Fortnite cosmetic items themed around certain FNAF characters are on their way to Fortnite. These respective sets of in-game extras are as follows:

  • Freddy: Back bling and kicks
  • Chica: Back bling
  • Bonnie: Back bling

In addition to these, new FNAF-oriented emotes and musical instruments were leaked as part of the collab by the source. The music playing during the aforementioned video was also identified as Five Nights at Freddy’s 1 Song by The Living Tombstone. What this could hint at is the song being rolled into the game as a jam track.

FNAF location arriving in Fortnite map

Among the other confirmed inclusions in Fortnite are Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria, a clear nod to Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza, which is the main setting for the Five Nights at Freddy’s game. It is yet to be known where exactly on the Fortnite map this location might appear once the Fortnitemares update kicks in.

Must Read: FNAF Bonnie locations in Fortnite: Where to find and beat him

Fortnitemares and other confirmed IP collabs

tricks n treats 4 u https://t.co/wrpsNnThN6

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) September 28, 2026

The Fortnite x FNAF collab is already attracting a lot of attention, even before its release, with the X post announcing the same quickly becoming one of the most liked posts by the game’s official channel. But that isn’t the only franchise coming to Fortnite this October.

With the Fortnitemares event now excitingly close, Fortnite has unveiled several more franchises that will appear in the game during this period. Besides Five Nights at Freddy’s, the IPs and recognizable names prominently featured in the forthcoming event are A Nightmare on Elm Street, Beetlejuice, Slender Man, Obsession, The Purge, and Black Clover. It will be interesting to see the kind of cosmetic items that these other brands inspire in the game.

Read more:

  • How to get the Champion Focus FNCS skin in Fortnite
  • How to get the Madison Beer skin in Fortnite
  • Universal Monsters skins return to Fortnite: How to get them
  • How to get the Dollie skin in Fortnite
