title.rendered: WhatsApp now lets Apple Watch users react with any emoji

content.rendered:
You can finally react to WhatsApp messages on your Apple Watch with any emoji, not just six presets.

WhatsApp has started rolling out full emoji reactions on watchOS, as reported by WABetaInfo. Reactions from the Watch now look just like reactions from your iPhone.

What changed

When WhatsApp launched its full Apple Watch app in November 2025, the Watch finally got proper support for reading chats, sending voice messages, and seeing call notifications without relying on plain system notifications. Emoji reactions came with it, but you were limited to six choices. Anything else meant pulling out your iPhone.

Now that limit is gone. If you long-press a message on the Watch, you’ll still see those six quick reactions first. But there’s now a button to open the complete picker.

That picker shows:

  • your recently used emoji at the top
  • the full watchOS emoji library split into categories
  • a scrollable list designed for the small screen

WABetaInfo says WhatsApp organizes the library into 8 categories: Smileys, Nature, Food, Activity, Travel, Objects, Symbols, and Flags. Tap a category to expand it, pick anything, and the reaction appears in the chat the same way it does from an iPhone.

On iPhone you tap the + in the reaction tray to get every emoji. The Watch version brings the same flexibility, just with a vertical scroll instead of tabs.

Rolling out now, but not to everyone yet

WABetaInfo notes this is a gradual rollout. Even though the feature is officially live, it may take a few weeks before you see the category button on your Watch. WhatsApp hasn’t listed it in the App Store changelog yet, which is normal for its staged releases.

If you don’t see it, make sure your iPhone and Watch apps are updated and check again later. There’s nothing to enable in Settings, it appears automatically when your account gets it.

For anyone who lives on the Watch for quick replies, this closes a small but annoying gap. Reactions are the fastest way to acknowledge a message without typing, and on a tiny screen knowing how to use WhatsApp on Apple Watch properly matters more than on the phone. The same long-press to react flow you use on iPhone now carries over to your wrist without compromise.

title.rendered: iOS 27.2 beta 2 reveals more about iPhone’s Anti-Snatching feature

content.rendered:
Apple is still building an iPhone feature that can lock your phone automatically if someone snatches it from your hand, and code in the latest beta shows how careful it is trying to be about false alarms.

New references spotted in iOS 27.2 beta 2 point to an internal system called “AutoLock” that watches for signals a theft may have just happened. Apple hasn’t announced the feature, and it isn’t turned on for users in this beta.

The new beta adds more detail about what triggers it and what stops it from firing by mistake.

What iOS 27.2 beta 2 reveals

AutoLock can look at several signals together to decide an iPhone may have been taken:

  • a sharp acceleration consistent with being snatched
  • a paired Apple Watch becoming unreachable or losing connectivity
  • prolonged loss of network connectivity
  • the device staying unlocked beyond a set interval

None of these alone locks the phone. The code describes a voting system: theft signals can request a lock, but safeguards can veto it.

Those veto signals are meant to avoid false positives:

  • a successful Face ID or Touch ID check after the motion
  • certain foreground app activities that look like theft motion but aren’t, like gaming or workout apps
  • being in a familiar location or on a familiar Wi-Fi network, similar to how Stolen Device Protection relaxes restrictions at home or work
  • a backoff mechanism that temporarily suppresses extra locks after repeated triggers

That familiar-place check is already familiar to iPhone owners. If you have Stolen Device Protection enabled, your iPhone already adds extra steps when you’re away from trusted places, and AutoLock appears to reuse that same idea.

Still in testing, not live yet

Apple has enabled the underlying AutoLock service in the background in iOS 27.2 beta 2, but the component that would actually lock the display is still disabled. That lets Apple test behavior without accidentally locking testers’ phones.

It also means you won’t find a toggle for this in Settings yet. The references only show progress, not a launch date. Apple could still change how it works, rename it, or hold it for a later iOS 27.x update.

The need is clear. Apple’s current protections like Find My, Activation Lock, and Stolen Device Protection help after a theft, but they don’t help much if a thief grabs an already-unlocked iPhone. Android already has a Theft Detection Lock that uses motion to lock the screen for the same reason. Apple’s version, if it ships, would aim for the same moment: the seconds right after a grab.

For now, the best available protection remains what shipped with iOS 27’s existing security features, and Apple hasn’t said when AutoLock will become user-facing.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

title.rendered: Bitrig adds iPhone Duo support with Interactive 3D simulator

content.rendered:
Bitrig now lets you build and test apps for Apple’s upcoming foldable right inside its AI coding platform, with a 3D simulator you can fold, tilt, and rotate like the real phone.

The update arrived on September 19, just a week after Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 with iPhone Duo support. Bitrig detailed the changes on its official blog.

What Bitrig’s 3D simulator does

Standard iPhone simulators show a flat device. Bitrig’s take is interactive. You can grab the virtual iPhone Duo, fold it closed, open it flat, leave it half-folded, turn it around, and set it down in different poses. Your app responds in real time as you move it.

That matters because Duo has more than one way to be used. Bitrig says the phone can sit like a laptop on a table, stand like a tent on a nightstand, or work folded shut on its outer display. Developers need to see how layouts break in each position.

How developers can use the new Duo features

Bitrig points to four specific SwiftUI tools Apple introduced for the foldable:

  • Try every pose. Test open, closed, and partially folded in both portrait and landscape. The 3D view lets you drag and rotate to check adaptive layouts.
  • Respond to the hinge. Use onHingeChange to trigger animations as the phone folds, like Apple’s window-like unfold effect on the outer display. Bitrig streams live hinge data as you fold.
  • Build hands-free experiences. Use ArrangementView to put video on the top half and controls on the bottom when Duo is propped on a table. Bitrig also reminds developers to support landscape for outer-display use.
  • Use both displays at once. Add CameraCaptureAccessory to show useful content on the outer screen while the inner screen handles the main camera view.

For most native SwiftUI apps, Bitrig says standard navigation and toolbars already adapt to Duo, but the new APIs help take advantage of the extra space.

From vibe-coding app to full Xcode workflow

Bitrig started in 2025 as an iPhone app that turned text or voice prompts into SwiftUI apps running inside Bitrig itself. Since then it added a Mac app with full Xcode toolchain access, an integrated simulator, on-device testing, and export to Xcode or TestFlight and the App Store.

With this Duo update, Bitrig also helps manage multiple Xcode versions. You can build against the Xcode 27.1 beta to prepare a Duo-ready app and switch back to Xcode 27 for regular updates.

Apple’s iPhone Duo doesn’t ship until October 23, with preorders starting October 16 and pricing from $1,999, but the developer tools are already live. Bitrig is also hosting a Bitrig Hacks: iPhone Duo Edition meetup in San Francisco on September 26 to get developers experimenting early.

If you’re curious what the hardware actually offers, Apple’s first foldable packs a 7.6-inch inner OLED and a 5.4-inch outer display with an A20 Pro chip and the same A20 Pro driving the iPhone 18 Pro lineup.

title.rendered: How to get Pac-Man sidekick in Fortnite

content.rendered:
After years of anticipation, Pac-Man has finally made his way into Fortnite. However, instead of arriving as a skin, the iconic arcade character is joining the game as a Sidekick! This means that Pac-Man will follow you around during matches and react to everything happening around you. With that said, let’s take a look at how you can get the Pac-Man Sidekick in Fortnite.

Here’s how to unlock the Pac-Man sidekick in Fortnite

The Pac-Man Sidekick arrived in Fortnite after the Item Shop reset on September 18, 2026, as part of the Pac-Man Bundle. Here’s a complete step-by-step guide on how to unlock the Pac-Man Sidekick in Fortnite –

  1. Open Fortnite on your console, mobile, or PC
  2. Head to the Item Shop tab
  3. Choose the Pac-Man Sidekick (1,500 V-Bucks)
  4. Hold the purchase button until the progress circle fills up

Once you’ve completed the purchase, head to the Fortnite Locker and equip Pac-Man as your Sidekick. The Sidekick features the character’s classic bright yellow design with red boots and brown gloves, which makes it a fun addition to any collection. You can also earn additional rewards by building up enough Sidekick Points while using Pac-Man Sidekick.

All Pac-Man Cosmetics Available in Fortnite

While you can purchase the Pac-Man Sidekick separately, it’s actually a part of the Pac-Man Bundle, which costs 2,200 V-Bucks. Although it’s the more expensive option, the bundle includes tons of Pac-Man-themed cosmetics that are worth checking out, especially if you’re a die-hard fan of the iconic arcade character. Let’s take a look at all the cosmetics included in the bundle –

The Pac-Man Bundle will be available to purchase in the Item Shop until September 25, 2026, at 8 PM ET. However, before spending your V-Bucks, keep in mind that the Lil Wayne skin is also available in Fortnite, so choose your purchase accordingly.

title.rendered: Siri AI is finally here in iOS 27, but there’s a catch you need to know

content.rendered:
For years, I felt Siri was becoming the forgotten assistant on my iPhone. I could use it to set an alarm, send messages, or get the weather, but the second I needed something more than that, I would use ChatGPT or any other AI tool.

That changes with iOS 27. Apple has finally delivered its long-awaited Siri AI, transforming Siri from a traditional voice assistant into a much more capable AI assistant that can understand personal context, search the web, see what’s on your screen, work across apps, and maintain conversations.

Here’s everything you need to know about Siri AI in iOS 27.

Siri AI is finally here, but it’s still a beta

Apple released iOS 27 to the public on September 14, 2026. The update is compatible with iPhone 11 and newer, but Siri AI has more demanding hardware requirements.

You need an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone, starting with the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 16 series, and later models. It’s also available on compatible iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, CarPlay, and Vision Pro models.

And if you’ve installed iOS 27 but can’t find the new Siri, don’t assume something is broken. Apple is using a waitlist-based rollout.

To enable Siri AI on your iPhone:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Siri.
  3. Select Try Siri AI (Beta).
  4. Tap Join Waitlist > Continue.

Access isn’t necessarily immediate. Some users have received Siri AI within minutes, while others have reported waiting hours or even days.

What makes Siri AI different?

The public release of iOS 27 makes Siri AI much broader than the earlier Siri preview suggested. Using the latest Apple Intelligence, Apple has rebuilt Siri around three major capabilities:

  • Personal Context Understanding
  • Broad World Knowledge
  • Onscreen Awareness

These capabilities work together rather than functioning as isolated features. Let’s understand in detail.

1. Siri can finally understand your personal context

One of the biggest changes is Siri’s ability to understand information stored across your Apple apps.

Apple has rebuilt the search system behind Siri using a semantic index. Instead of simply matching keywords, Siri can understand the meaning of information found in apps such as:

  • Mail
  • Messages
  • Photos
  • Notes
  • Reminders
  • Calendar
  • Files

That means you can ask questions in a much more natural way. For example: “What was that movie my brother told me to watch last week?” or “What’s the confirmation number for my upcoming flight?”

I have also tried asking Siri to find photos from a particular event, locate information from an old email, or figure out what I need to do tomorrow based on information stored across my apps. This is what it’s like to have an assistant who knows everything about your digital life.

2. Siri now has broader world knowledge

Siri isn’t limited to information stored on your iPhone. The new assistant can search the web to answer questions that require current or broader knowledge.

You can ask it about recipes, travel planning, homework, gardening, DIY projects, calculations, local business information, and other everyday research tasks.

The important difference is that Siri can combine this broader knowledge with information from your device. So instead of asking one assistant for information and then manually giving another assistant your personal details, Siri is designed to bring those pieces together.

3. Siri can understand what’s on your screen

Siri AI also gains on-screen awareness. If you’re looking at an image, webpage, document, or selected piece of text, you can ask Siri about it without copying the information into another app.

For example, you can:

  • Summarize an article.
  • Explain selected text.
  • Translate something you’re looking at.
  • Ask about an image.
  • Analyze information in a document.
  • Ask follow-up questions about selected content.

This works across supported apps, making Siri considerably more useful when you’re already doing something on your iPhone.

The new Search or Ask Siri interface

Apple has also changed how Siri looks and feels on iPhone.

The new Search or Ask interface replaces the traditional Spotlight search experience and is accessible by swiping down from the middle of the display.

You can:

  • Type your request.
  • Speak to Siri.
  • Use the side button.
  • Say “Siri” or “Hey Siri.”
  • Upload an image or document.
  • Continue an existing conversation.

When Siri is processing a request, a new animation appears around the interface. Responses can appear as concise information in the Dynamic Island area.

If you need more information, you can swipe down on the response and continue the conversation. There’s also a + button that lets you attach files and images to a conversation.

Some responses also use rich information cards. For example, weather and Calendar requests can display information in a more visual format rather than returning only a block of text.

Siri finally gets its own app

For the first time, Siri has a dedicated app. The Siri app gives you a place to start new conversations and revisit previous ones.

It includes a card-based history of recent Siri conversations, along with options to:

  • Search previous conversations.
  • Pin conversations.
  • Continue an earlier discussion.
  • Access conversations across compatible Apple devices.

I like that Siri conversations can sync across Apple’s ecosystem, meaning I can start something on one device and revisit it elsewhere. This is a major departure from the old Siri experience, where most interactions felt temporary.

Write with Siri is much more powerful

Apple has also integrated Siri deeply into text editing.

Write with Siri works anywhere you can type.

You can ask Siri to:

  • Write something from scratch.
  • Rewrite text.
  • Change the tone.
  • Shorten text.
  • Expand an idea.
  • Turn bullet points into paragraphs.
  • Proofread grammar.
  • Fix spelling.
  • Give feedback on your writing.

For example: “Make this email sound more professional.” or “Turn these bullet points into a paragraph.” I tried asking: “How does this email sound?” Siri then provided feedback on my writing.

The interesting part is that Siri can even adapt my writing style when generating text in Mail and Messages, making its suggestions feel more personalized. Apple has also added automatic proofreading for spelling and grammar as you type.

Must read: How to Rewrite Existing Text with Siri AI

Visual Intelligence and Siri now work together

Apple has made a major change to Visual Intelligence in iOS 27.

Instead of treating it primarily as a Camera Control feature, Apple has moved Visual Intelligence into the Camera app through a new Siri Mode. You can swipe to Siri Mode, point your camera at something, take a picture, and ask Siri about what you’re seeing.

Camera Control can still be used to access Visual Intelligence on supported iPhones. The integration with Siri makes Visual Intelligence considerably more useful because Siri can now search the web and answer follow-up questions directly.

What can Visual Intelligence do?

Apple has added several new capabilities.

  • Get nutritional information: Point your camera at food, and Siri can provide nutritional insights and information about what you’re eating.
  • Split a restaurant bill: In supported regions, you can photograph a restaurant bill and ask Siri to work out what each person owes.
  • Import multiple Calendar events: Photograph a schedule or list and Siri can identify multiple events and add them to Calendar or Reminders.
  • Import contacts: Take a picture of a business card and Siri can extract the information and create a contact.
  • Add membership cards to Wallet: A photo of a barcode from a supported membership card or pass can be converted into a Wallet pass.
  • Read labels and ingredients: You can click laundry-care labels and ask Siri to explain the instructions. Siri can also read ingredient lists and help identify potential allergens.
  • Understand confusing signs: You can photograph a parking sign and ask Siri to explain what it means.

This is where Siri AI starts to feel much closer to the multimodal AI assistants that have become popular over the last few years.

Siri gets a new voice on newer iPhones

Siri’s voice is also getting an upgrade, but this feature depends on newer hardware.

The iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air have Apple’s more powerful on-device Apple Intelligence model.

On these devices, you can customize Siri’s voice emotions.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on Siri and select Voice.
  3. Change the Pace slider to control how fast or slow Siri talks.
  4. Adjust the Expressivity slider to change the emotional tone and personality.

The newer on-device model can also improve system-wide dictation. Apple says Siri’s improved natural-language understanding makes dictation better at handling spelling, punctuation, capitalization, and transcription accuracy.

Because dictation is built into the keyboard, these

Privacy remains a major part of Siri AI

Siri AI uses a combination of on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute. When a request requires more processing power, Apple can send the necessary workload to Private Cloud Compute rather than processing everything directly on the iPhone.

Apple says data sent to Private Cloud Compute isn’t accessible to Apple or third parties.

The company has also expanded Private Cloud Compute infrastructure, including Apple Intelligence workloads running on Google Cloud using NVIDIA hardware.

iOS 27.2 expands Siri AI to five new languages

Apple has already started expanding Siri AI beyond English.

The first iOS 27.2 beta, released on September 16, adds Siri AI support for:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

Apple had previously indicated that these additional languages would arrive around October, so the iOS 27.2 beta provides an early look at the expansion.

Siri AI availability varies by region

At the launch of iOS 27, Siri AI supports English in:

  • Australia
  • Canada
  • Ireland
  • India
  • New Zealand
  • South Africa
  • United Kingdom
  • United States

Apple is expanding language support through subsequent updates.

There are also regional restrictions. Siri AI and the new Apple Intelligence features are not available in China, while Siri AI was not initially available on iPhone and iPad in the European Union.

The future of Siri has finally arrived

Siri’s biggest problem was that it struggled with requests that required context, reasoning, multiple steps, or information from several sources.

iOS 27 addresses those weaknesses with Personal Context Understanding, Broad World Knowledge, Onscreen Awareness, App Actions, Visual Intelligence, Write with Siri, a dedicated Siri app, and a completely redesigned Siri interface.

And Apple is already moving beyond the initial release. The iOS 27.2 beta’s expansion shows that Siri AI’s rollout is only beginning. The question is how quickly Apple and third-party developers can turn this new Siri foundation into an assistant that people genuinely rely on every day.

Have you joined the Siri AI waitlist yet? Which new Siri feature are you most excited to try? Let me know in the comments.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Crash Bandicoot Sprite in Fortnite: What it does and how to find it

content.rendered:
Crash Bandicoot Sprite has recently landed in Fortnite, joining six other sprites in the game that are also heavily inspired by fan-favorite video game characters. At the time of writing, the list now spans across Sonic Sprite, Tails Sprite, Shadow Sprite, Mega Man Sprite, Jackrabbit Sprite, and Blinky Sprite.

The Crash Bandicoot IP has emerged as a key collaborator of Fortnite during the ongoing Chapter 7 Season 4 titled Override, which has a strong focus on video game franchises. As a result, so far, we have already seen Crash Bandicoot cosmetics arrive, in tandem with Spyro-inspired items, in the Item Shop.

The recent addition of the Crash Bandicoot Sprite should further give Fortnite players, especially those who are also fans of the long-running franchise, more reasons to be excited. Below, you can learn more about what this sprite does and how you can grab one for your own.

Crash Bandicoot Sprite: Abilities and level-up buffs

First introduced in inaugural Crash Bandicoot game for the original PlayStation, the spin attack or whirlwind attack is one of the most popular moves of the titular hero. Thanks to the Crash Bandicoot Sprite, you can finally execute the same against opponents in Fortnite.

This sprite is a Legendary-tier item and can be equipped to do a whirlwind attack when you press the jump button again while in mid-air. Doing so inflicts damage on nearby enemies and also pushes them back, creating some breathing room for the player. This move could prove particularly useful when you are surrounded or overwhelmed in a close-range fight.

As you level up the Crash Bandicoot Sprite, by performing actions such as eliminating enemies and opening chests, the whirlwind attack’s damage effect increases, whereas the cooldown time before you can use this attack again decreases.

How to get Crash Bandicoot Sprite in Fortnite

Given that the Crash Bandicoot Sprite belongs to the Legendary tier, it won’t be easy to find him in your in-game surroundings during a Battle Royale match. However, there are still some ways that you can go down in order to maximize your chances of securing the desired sprite.

1. Use Legendary Cheat Codes

The most reliable way of getting a Crash Bandicoot Sprite is through the use of a Legendary Cheat Code if you can find one. These look like any other cheat codes but sport a distinct golden color. Even if you can’t find one of this particular tier, you can also try the Epic Cheat Codes, marked in purple, as those also have a small but existent chance of giving sprites of a higher tier.

Instead of manually keeping an eye out for such Cheat Codes, you can use the gizmo known as Cheat Code Locator to mark nearby cheat codes on the map. To obtain this item, you can either purchase it using Sprite Dust at an Extraction Site or punch in one of the relevant admin panel codes in Fortnite, such as “ChatFindMeAnotherCode,” that offer the same for free.

2. Open Rare Chests

Chests are still a traditional way of finding new sprites and loot in the game. While standard chests may have extremely low chances of spawning high-tier sprites, the blue-colored ones, aka Rare Chests, have a good likelihood of containing sprites like the Crash Bandicoot Sprite.

Since Rare Chests themselves are not ubiquitous in the Fortnite Battle Royale map, it helps to know where to look for them in advance. So, for that matter, the map locations with the most Rare Chests are the islands in the shape of Pac-Man, Blinky, and Pink, along with places such as The Battlewoods and Stone Sanctum.

3. Borrow it from a friend

Another straightforward way of getting the Crash Bandicoot Sprite is from someone who already has it and is willing to share. You can find such resourceful Fortnite players on the game’s official Discord server.

For this method, you and the player sharing his sprite need to join two matches together. In the first one, the latter would drop the desired sprite for you to pick it up and extract. Once you do that, the game will register that particular sprite into your collection. Then, in the second match, you have to do the same and return the item to its original owner. Afterwards, you can recall the sprite using Sprite Dust from the Sprites section in the Override tab.

Rounding up

The advent of more iconic video game characters into the sprite portfolio of Fortnite is a welcome trend, no doubt. Besides adding more weight to Fortnite Override’s gaming-oriented theme, it also brings some memorable moves and power-ups into the online multiplayer title.

With sprites inspired by figures from Sonic the Hedgehog, Mega Man, Crash Bandicoot, and more already in the game, it will be interesting to see which other gaming icons Fortnite devs next incorporate into their game. Because of this, it should be worth keeping up with the weekly updates that bring such new changes for the players to discover.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

title.rendered: Pond Sprite in Fortnite: What it does and how to find it

content.rendered:
With yet another Fortnite update comes a new community-made sprite called the Pond Sprite. It follows after the Onigiri Sprite and the X-Ray Sprite, which were also sprites conceived by the players themselves.

Created by X user @matsubokiri, Pond Sprite is one of the five fan entries that were selected for being added into Fortnite in August. After the arrival of this sprite, the only ones from the bunch yet to join the in-game lineup are Honey Sprite and Dumpster Dive Sprite.

In this guide, you can learn more about the benefits of using the Pond Sprite in Fortnite. In addition, you can also check out the different methods you can get your hands on it.

Pond Sprite: Abilities and level-up bonuses

Pond Sprite is a community-made sprite of Epic rarity. By equipping it, you can press jump again after landing to do a bigger jump aka Super Jump, given that a charge (generates over time) is available for use. This ability should come in handy when trying to escape an early-match skirmish or when trying to quickly race outside of the Storm.

Upon ranking up the Pond Sprite, the strength of your Super Jump increases, whereas the cooldown time for using the ability decreases. Hence, for those who prioritize quick traversal and evasion during Fortnite matches, leveling up this sprite is a recommended move.

How to get Pond Sprite in Fortnite

Among the three sprites added on September 17, Pond Sprite is the easiest to grab, given it’s of the Epic tier while the other two are Legendary-tier sprites. Hence, once you start following the ways below, it shouldn’t take you too long before you end up with a Pond Sprite in your collection.

1. Through Rare Cheat Codes or Epic Cheat Codes

Cheat codes can reasonably be considered the primary source of sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4. Since Pond Sprite is an Epic item, you could easily get it by using Epic Cheat Codes (purple) or even Rare Cheat Codes (blue). But, as obvious, the former has a much higher probability of offering this particular sprite than the latter.

When you are going on a search for cheat codes, it’s important to first look in the areas where they are highly concentrated. In the current Battle Royale map, Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast, and Shaken Sanctuary are the locations leading in this aspect.

Moreover, you can easily locate nearby cheat codes using the Cheat Code Locator, which can be exchanged with Sprite Dust at any of the Extraction Sites or by using relevant lobby hacks in Fortnite.

2. Through blue-colored chests aka Rare Chests

Chests are another way of getting sprites, even though they may usually just spawn loot. For boosting your chances of finding a sprite in them, you must target special chests such as the Rare Chests (the blue-colored kind).

You can find these blue chests in certain key locations on the island, including Pac-Man islands (shaped in the form of Pac-Man, Blinky, and Pinky), The Battlewoods, and Stone Sanctum.

3. Use the help of another player

If you can find a willing player, from places such as Fortnite’s official Discord, the lowest-effort way to get the Pond Sprite should be borrowing it from someone else. To do this, the two players involved have to join a match, where the owner of the sprite lets the other player take it from him and then extract the same. To return the sprite, they once again have to join a match together and repeat the aforementioned step in the opposite direction this time.

After this, the player who returned the sprite can easily recall the item through the Override tab’s Sprites section. However, it’s worth noting that a nominal amount of Sprite Dust will be needed for this to work.

Rounding up

So far, the community-created sprites have been quite an interesting addition in Fortnite. While the Onigiri Sprite may not be a gamechanger, the X-Ray Sprite certainly holds up its weight and then some when it comes to utility. The latter sprite is, hence, popular and widely sought-after by the players.

In the coming weeks, it will be intriguing to see how the devs spread out the remaining two community-made sprites across the rest of the Fortnite Override season. Another thing that should be worth noting is whether any of the forthcoming player-conceived sprites can replace the X-Ray Sprite in terms of its importance in gameplay.

title.rendered: iOS 27 camera features: What’s new on iPhone

content.rendered:
iOS 27 makes the Camera app easier to customize and much more useful when you point it at something you don’t recognize. The update also gives iPhone 18 Pro owners the manual controls photographers have wanted for years.

The catch is that iOS 27 does not give every iPhone the same camera experience. Siri mode and AI editing need an Apple Intelligence-compatible model, while Pro controls and Reference mode are exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

Which iPhones get which camera feature?

Use this quick split before looking for a setting that may not exist on your iPhone.

Siri mode turns the Camera into a visual assistant

Siri mode joins Photo and Video in the Camera mode picker. Point your iPhone at a plant, a strange gadget, a menu, or a bill, and Siri can identify it, answer questions, search for similar images, or suggest an action.

For example, a restaurant bill can trigger a split-bill action, while a printed card can be turned into a Wallet pass. You can also ask a follow-up question without leaving the Camera interface.

To use it, open Camera and tap Siri, then point the viewfinder at something. Tap the Siri button for a quick answer, Ask to type a specific question, or Search to find similar images. If your iPhone has Camera Control, you can also click and hold it while the iPhone is locked to enter Siri mode. Apple’s instructions cover the available actions.

This is the camera feature most people will notice first, but it is limited to Apple Intelligence devices such as the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, and iPhone 16 models or later. Siri AI is still in beta, starts in English, and is not initially available on iOS in the EU. For a deeper look at what it can recognize and do, see what’s new in Visual Intelligence in iOS 27.

Put your favorite camera controls above the viewfinder

Apple has finally made the Camera controls less rigid. The Flash and Live Photo buttons can stay above the frame, and you can add or remove other tools so the settings you actually use are one tap away.

Open Camera, tap the Camera Controls button, and choose Edit. Add tools such as Timer, Exposure, Styles, Aspect, or Depth, then drag them into the order you want. You can also return to Apple’s default layout with Reset to Essentials.

This is a small change with a real payoff. If you often lower exposure, use a timer, or switch Photographic Styles, you no longer need to open the controls drawer every time. The available tools still depend on your iPhone and the mode you are using. If you use an iPhone 16, you can also adjust settings from the side button with Camera Control.

iPhone 18 Pro gets real manual camera controls

The iPhone 18 Pro is where the hardware changes the Camera app. In Photo, Video, Cinematic, Slo-mo, and Time-lapse modes, you can manually adjust the lens aperture, shutter speed, and white balance. A histogram lets you check whether the scene is too dark or too bright before you capture it.

The 48MP Main camera also has a variable aperture that moves between f/1.48 and f/4.0. Use a wider aperture for more light and stronger background blur. Use a narrower aperture when you want more of a group or landscape to stay sharp. Shutter speed is the more useful control for moving subjects, since it lets you freeze action or create intentional motion blur.

The iPhone 18 Pro camera system adds smart focus tracking, too. Tap a subject twice to track it as it moves closer, farther away, or briefly leaves the frame. Photographic Styles also gain texture and film grain controls, so you can soften skin or add a film-like finish before or after shooting.

If you do not have an iPhone 18 Pro, the built-in Camera app still handles most everyday shooting well. For manual shutter speed, white balance, and RAW controls on older models, these iPhone camera apps are the more practical route.

Reference mode helps verify an iPhone 18 Pro photo

Reference mode is aimed at photographers, journalists, sellers, and anyone who needs to show that a photo came from an iPhone 18 Pro camera. The Main camera records signed sensor data alongside the photo. Photos can then develop and display a reference image that you can compare with the edited version.

It is opt-in. Go to Settings > Camera > Reference Image > Add Reference Mode, then swipe to Reference in Camera when you want to capture one. Apple’s Reference Image instructions cover the supported regions and capture process. It can help verify the capture and whether the photo was altered, but it cannot prove that the scene itself was unstaged or truthful.

Photos can rescue a weak frame after you shoot it

iOS 27 also gives the Photos app three useful AI editing tools. They are not camera modes, but they change what you can do with a photo after pressing the shutter:

  • Clean Up: Remove larger or more complicated distractions with more natural-looking results.
  • Extend: Add content beyond the original edges when a photo is too tightly cropped or needs a different aspect ratio.
  • Reframe: Drag the image to adjust its perspective and improve the composition after capture.

Open a photo in Photos, tap Edit, and choose the tool you need. These features require Apple Intelligence, and Apple applies the same device, language, region, and usage-limit restrictions as its other AI tools. For the basic Clean Up workflow, see how to remove unwanted objects from iPhone photos. You can also read the full iOS 27 Photos breakdown for more examples.

The practical takeaway

For most people, the best iOS 27 camera upgrade is the customizable control row. Put Exposure, Timer, or Styles where you can reach them and the redesigned Camera app becomes quicker to use. If you have an Apple Intelligence iPhone, Siri mode is worth trying next.

The manual controls, smart tracking, texture and grain options, and Reference mode belong to the iPhone 18 Pro generation. They are hardware features delivered alongside iOS 27, not upgrades every compatible iPhone receives.

Whether you’re customizing your iPhone, troubleshooting your Android, or tweaking Chrome OS settings, my goal is to help you get more out of your tech.

title.rendered: Apple Home Hub will be the intelligent center of your home: Report

content.rendered:
Apple’s long-rumored Home Hub will be the "intelligent center" of the home, the home equivalent of what the iPhone is for your pocket, according to Bloomberg.

Mark Gurman reports in his Power On newsletter that the device, codenamed J490, is now being tested widely inside Apple employees’ homes and will serve as the anchor for controls, video calls and media, tying together an "intelligent personal hub" strategy that CEO John Ternus laid out at the September 9 event.

Ternus called the iPhone the ideal intelligent personal hub for mobile life. Gurman says Apple wants a second hub for the household, a central place where Siri AI can pull personal context, device state and media together without asking you to dig out your phone in every room.

What J490 looks like

Gurman describes a roughly square display, about 7 inches, with thin bezels and rounded corners, smaller than an iPad mini and closer to an Amazon Echo Show in concept, but more restrained.

There are two expected forms: a tabletop version with the screen perched on a half-dome base that looks like a HomePod mini cut in half, and a wall-mounted version that attaches with magnets. Both run a new operating system built around Siri AI, previously reported as "Charismatic," that blends iOS, tvOS and watchOS ideas. It includes a home screen, widgets and clock faces, with StandBy-like glanceability on the iPhone Duo as a reference point. Setup syncs with an iPhone.

Facial recognition is part of personalization, but not Face ID as you know it. Gurman says the Hub identifies who is nearby with a standard camera rather than a TrueDepth sensor array, then tailors what it shows, calendar, photos, suggested media, to that person. If that approach works reliably in a kitchen-lighting reality, he notes it could even inform how Apple adds similar recognition to a future iPhone Duo without the depth-camera bulk. That’s reported possibility, not promise.

Siri is the point

The Hub is being built for next-generation Siri AI, the personal-context assistant Apple has tied to App Intents and Private Cloud Compute. Gurman says on the Hub, Siri can surface information across your devices and accounts, find a podcast or song someone sent weeks ago, display a relevant photo, and carry out more precise tasks in Notes, Reminders and Calendar, plus run complex searches within Apple apps. That same Siri AI push is already rolling out with the iPhone 18 Pro, which gives a sense of what Apple wants the voice experience to feel like before the home hardware arrives.

That Siri foundation is also why the product has slipped before. Gurman previously noted the Hub was originally planned for March 2025 and then pushed because the Siri features it needs, personal data reasoning and app control, weren’t ready for iOS 18.4. Those delays explain why a hardware-ready display sat in employee homes long before launch.

When it might arrive

Gurman has not given a firm date, but the latest note places the Hub as one of the most anticipated launches of Ternus’s early tenure, alongside the iPhone Duo and a touch-screen MacBook. A summary of the same newsletter puts the window as early as next month, with broader reporting pointing to fall 2026.

Apple has not confirmed timing. Earlier background from Gurman still expects refreshed Apple TV and HomePod mini models with faster chips to support Siri AI around the same period, plus a more ambitious tabletop robot with a 9-inch arm-mounted display down the road. For now, the home Hub plus those living-room updates are the expected first wave.

If you already live with an iPhone, Apple Watch and HomePods in most rooms, Gurman suggests the Hub’s value will still come down to one question: can a fixed screen with better voice handle the home stuff faster than pulling a phone from your pocket? Apple thinks the answer is yes, provided Siri AI actually feels personal, not just vocal.

title.rendered: iFixit iPhone 18 Pro teardown shows battery sizes and new variable aperture

content.rendered:
iFixit has torn down the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max and the inside tells the same story Apple did on stage, plus a few caveats, according to the iFixit teardown published September 20.

The teardown confirms battery sizes for the eSIM-only models sold in the U.S. and several other countries, gets close to the new variable aperture camera, and flags a repairability issue iFixit hasn’t seen this badly before.

Battery capacities are official for eSIM models

iFixit read the labels directly:

  • iPhone 18 Pro (eSIM): 4,288 mAh, 16.76 Wh, up 0.8% from 4,252 mAh on iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max (eSIM): 5,567 mAh, 21.751 Wh, up 9.4% from 5,088 mAh on iPhone 17 Pro Max

Those numbers apply to eSIM-only units sold in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and Kuwait. Models with a physical SIM tray in other regions have smaller cells, as earlier filings suggested. The iPhone 18 Pro still relies on Apple’s own playback claims for real-world battery life, so capacity alone doesn’t tell you how long it lasts.

Once you get past the display, the battery is actually a bright spot. Apple kept the screwed-in metal battery tray from last year. You remove the tray and battery together with 13 screws and no wrestling with strong adhesive. The cell itself uses electrically releasable adhesive, about 90 seconds at 12 volts, and lifts cleanly.

The variable aperture is tiny, precise, and not really fixable

Apple’s biggest camera change this year is a mechanical variable aperture on the main 48MP camera. iFixit found six polymer-composite blades, each about as thin as a human hair and barely more than a millimeter at the tip, driven by electromagnets independent of optical image stabilization.

One blade flew across the room while iFixit pried the lens stack open. That says a lot about repairability. The blades pivot and slide on pins with almost no tolerance, and the glues are gummy. iFixit calls component-level repair as close to impossible as it gets, if the aperture sticks, you’ll be replacing the entire main camera assembly. The module itself is modular and easy to swap, but Apple hasn’t posted parts pricing yet. The iPhone 17 Pro camera assembly was $249, so expect more this year.

For photographers, iFixit is also skeptical about the benefit. On a 1/1.3-inch-type sensor with a 6.8mm focal length, the four presets, f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8 and f/4.0, give you about 7.3x more light at the widest versus f/4.0, but not the big background blur you’d get from a full-frame camera at the same f-number. Their test shots show legible background even at f/1.48. It’s real control, but subtle on a phone sensor.

A better cooling system, with a trade-off

The A20 Pro has moved to the outside of the dual-layer logic board, sitting directly against a vapor chamber Apple says is three times larger by surface area than before. A spongy thermal interface pad helps conduct heat evenly, and the chamber spreads it across the body. That move should help sustained performance for gaming and on-device AI.

It comes with a cost. The NAND storage now sits inside the board sandwich, so any storage-level or deep board repair starts with separating the layers, more heat, more labor, and more risk before you even reach the fault. Data recovery is also harder because the data is encrypted to that NAND.

The display frame cracked and iFixit is not sure why yet

Here’s the surprise. The plastic frame around the display cracked or pulled away on three of the four phones iFixit opened. The phones still worked, but a damaged frame won’t sit flush after reassembly and could compromise water resistance.

iFixit is cautious here. The same frame has been used since iPhone 15 Pro without this much trouble, and other teardowns haven’t reported the same damage. Four phones is too few to call it a trend. Adhesive strength, heating time, iFixit heated one intact unit for 25 minutes at 70-72°C, technique, or a change in plastic could all be factors. The larger vapor chamber may also be pulling heat away from the seam, making the adhesive harder to soften.

The teardown is otherwise front-entry only. The rear glass opens, but there’s nothing serviceable inside aside from the wireless charging coil. The USB-C port is a separate part but buried under screws and adhesive, a step back from the more accessible layout on the iPhone 16 Pro.

iFixit gives both phones a provisional 7 out of 10 for repairability. The score credits the tray-mounted battery and modular camera, but docks points because almost every repair still goes through that glued display. For now, the display frame issue doesn’t drag the score down further, iFixit wants more data.

One last modem oddity

All versions now carry Apple’s C2 modem except the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max, which still uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80. iFixit notes this is likely the tail end of Apple’s prior agreement to use Qualcomm chips through 2026. Apple put it in the model with the largest battery, so extra power draw is less noticeable. This will likely be the last iPhone to ship with a Qualcomm modem.

excerpt.rendered: iFixit’s iPhone 18 Pro teardown confirms eSIM battery sizes, shows the 6-blade variable aperture up close, larger vapor chamber cooling, and a new display-frame cracking flag.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

title.rendered: Apple scrapped a shorter Apple Pencil for iPhone Duo before launch: Report

content.rendered:
Apple built a smaller Apple Pencil specifically for the iPhone Duo and then dropped it before mass production, according to Bloomberg.

Mark Gurman reports in his Power On newsletter that the Duo was supposed to launch with a shorter, stubbier Pencil designed to magnetically attach to the hinge side of the foldable. The project ran into technical problems ahead of mass production, so Apple scrapped it.

Instead, Apple said at its September 9 event that the iPhone Duo will support the existing USB-C Apple Pencil later this year, but not at launch.

That delay is not just marketing. Gurman notes getting the iPad Pencil to work on the Duo is not as simple as flipping a switch. Apple still has to ship new software and run extensive internal testing to make the Pencil work on both the 5.4-inch outer display and the 7.6-inch inner display. He expects the update to arrive fairly late in 2026.

The shift is notable because Gurman had flagged the stubby prototype weeks before the event, while also saying it was unlikely to ship. That call turned out to be right.

Why Apple had to fall back to USB-C

The Duo was designed from the start to support Pencil input, but the plan changed from a bespoke accessory to compatibility with hardware people already own. The USB-C model is the lowest-cost Pencil in the lineup and charges over USB-C, not by magnetic attachment.

Apple’s own pages for the iPhone Duo confirm the October launch window, with preorders starting October 16 and availability on October 23, and no Pencil included in the box. Pencil support is listed as coming later this year.

Code spotted in iOS 27 also points to hover support for the foldable, suggesting Apple wants the experience to feel like it does on iPad, where the tip is tracked just above the display.

What this means if you planned to draw on Duo

You won’t need to buy a new Pencil if you already own the USB-C version. You will, however, have to wait. Apple hasn’t given an exact date, and Gurman’s reporting suggests you should treat "later this year" as December rather than October.

If you don’t already own a Pencil, there’s little reason to buy one now just for Duo until Apple confirms which models are supported, Gurman specifically names USB-C, not Apple Pencil Pro or Apple Pencil (2nd generation).

A dedicated hinge-mounted Pencil would have been tidier for a pocketable foldable, but Apple is betting that software compatibility beats another accessory to carry and charge. Whether that feels like a compromise will depend on how well the full-size Pencil handles on a phone that folds. For now, the practical way to plan is to consider only the accessories that actually fit the Duo’s hinge rather than waiting for a custom Pencil.

title.rendered: How to update your iPhone to iOS 27 (Step-by-step guide)

content.rendered:
Key takeaways:

  • Latest version: iOS 27.2, released on October 26, 2026. It adds Siri AI upgrades, Suggested Actions in Messages, Apple TV profiles and more than 160 security fixes.
  • iPhone models supporting iOS 27: iPhone 11 and newer, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation and later).
  • Preparation before updating: Back up your iPhone, free up storage, and stay plugged into power on Wi-Fi to avoid failed updates.
  • Ways to install: Update over the air, turn on Automatic Updates, or use a Mac or Windows PC if your iPhone is short on storage.

Apple released iOS 27 on September 14, 2026, and the latest version is now iOS 27.2, which arrived on October 26, 2026. iOS 27 introduced Apple’s next-generation Siri AI, more Apple Intelligence features, Liquid Glass customization and redesigned experiences across several apps. iOS 27.2 builds on that with smarter Siri, new app features and important security fixes.

iOS 27 comes pre-installed on Apple’s latest iPhones, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo. Owners of compatible older iPhones can download and install it for free, and anyone already on iOS 27 can update to iOS 27.2 the same way.

First, make sure your iPhone supports iOS 27. If it does, take care of a few things in advance for a smooth upgrade. Here’s everything you need to know about updating your iPhone to iOS 27.2.

What’s new in iOS 27.2?

iOS 27.2 is the second major point update to iOS 27. Here are the highlights:

  • Smarter Siri AI: Siri can recall past conversations and draw on more context, including photos in Messages, Calendar attendees, voicemails and your Safari history. You can also copy part of a Siri response, and a redesigned Excluded Apps setting controls which apps Siri can use. Siri AI now supports French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
  • Suggested Actions in Messages: Tappable shortcuts, such as tracking a package or adding an invite to Calendar, based on your conversations.
  • Photos: Shared Albums let you edit captions and comments, avoid duplicate photos and get a reminder before an album expires.
  • Apple TV profiles: Create profiles for people in your household. Child profiles default to PG content.
  • FaceTime: Dual Capture now works in Group FaceTime, and you can add a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call.
  • Other changes: A new black-and-white Apple Music icon, refreshed Podcasts and Games tabs, Multiview for live sports, new Shortcuts automations, and Apple Pencil (USB-C) support on iPhone Duo.
  • Security: Fixes for more than 160 vulnerabilities, so it’s worth installing even if you don’t need the new features.

Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later and isn’t available in the EU or mainland China. The redesigned Health app isn’t part of iOS 27.2; Apple is expected to release it later this year.

Does your iPhone support iOS 27?

The good news is that Apple didn’t drop any iPhone models from the iOS 27 compatibility list. Every iPhone that runs iOS 27 can also install iOS 27.2.

Just like iOS 26, iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and newer, along with the iPhone SE (2nd generation and later). Apple’s official compatibility list includes both older models and the latest 2026 iPhones.

This means iOS 18 remains the last major iOS update for the iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max and iPhone XR, which Apple launched in 2018.

Complete list of iPhones that support iOS 27:

  • iPhone SE (2nd & 3rd generation)
  • iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, iPhone 11 Pro Max
  • iPhone 12, iPhone 12 mini, iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 12 Pro Max
  • iPhone 13, iPhone 13 mini, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Plus, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max

If your iPhone isn’t on this list, it can’t be updated to iOS 27 or iOS 27.2.

iOS 27 vs Apple Intelligence: There’s an important difference

Before you update, there’s one important distinction worth knowing.

Supporting iOS 27 doesn’t automatically mean your iPhone supports Apple Intelligence. Apple’s AI features, including the new Siri AI and the Siri upgrades in iOS 27.2, require newer hardware.

Apple Intelligence in iOS 27 is available on:

  • iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16 series, including iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 17 series, including iPhone 17e
  • iPhone Air
  • iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • iPhone Duo

So, an iPhone 11 can run iOS 27.2 but can’t use Apple Intelligence or Siri AI.

How to prepare your iPhone for iOS 27.2

Before you start the update, take a few minutes to make sure you don’t lose any data or get interrupted midway.

Here’s what you should do before installing iOS 27.2:

1. Back up your iPhone

This is the single most important step. Although an iOS update normally preserves your apps, photos, messages and settings, a recent backup lets you recover your information if something goes wrong.

To back up with iCloud:

  1. Go to Settings → iCloud → iCloud Backup.
  2. Tap Back Up Now.

To back up with a Mac:

  1. Connect your iPhone with a cable.
  2. Open Finder and select your iPhone in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Back Up Now.

Wait until the backup finishes before starting the installation.

2. Free up enough space

An iOS update needs several gigabytes of free space to download and temporarily unpack. If your iPhone is nearly full, the update may fail or freeze. To clear space on your iPhone, try:

  • Deleting unused apps
  • Removing downloaded movies or TV shows
  • Deleting large video files you no longer need
  • Clearing old message attachments
  • Moving photos and videos to another storage service
  • Removing offline music or podcast downloads

Once done, check your available space by going to Settings → General → iPhone Storage.

3. Plug in and connect to Wi-Fi

It’s best to download iOS 27.2 over a reliable Wi-Fi connection. A stable connection reduces the chance of the download being interrupted and avoids using a large amount of cellular data.

Also, plug your iPhone into a charger before you start. This prevents the battery from running out mid-installation, which can leave the update incomplete.

3 ways to install iOS 27.2 on your iPhone

Whether you’re coming from iOS 26 or an earlier iOS 27 release, there are three ways to download and install iOS 27.2 on your iPhone.

1. Manually install iOS 27.2 over the air (OTA)

Installing the latest iOS directly on your iPhone takes just a few taps:

  1. Open Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Wait for your iPhone to check for the iOS 27.2 update.
  3. Tap Update Now or Download and Install once the update appears.
  4. Enter your iPhone passcode if prompted.
  5. Agree to Apple’s terms and conditions.
  6. Wait for the download to finish. Your iPhone will restart and complete the installation.
Note If you’re still on iOS 26, you may see both iOS 26 security updates and iOS 27 listed under Software Update. Tap the iOS 27 option under Also Available or Upgrade to iOS 27 to get the latest version. If Automatic Updates already downloaded the update, you may see Update Tonight instead.

The process can take a while depending on your internet connection, iPhone model and Apple’s server load.

If iOS 27.2 doesn’t appear, restart your iPhone and check again.

2. Make your iPhone install updates automatically

You can also set your iPhone to download new updates like iOS 27.2 as soon as they’re available and install them overnight, so you wake up on the latest version.

Here’s how:

  1. Open Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Tap Automatic Updates.
  3. Toggle on the options to automatically download and install iOS updates.
  4. You can also toggle on Security Responses & System Files to install important security fixes automatically.

Your iPhone will now install new updates overnight while it’s charging and connected to Wi-Fi. Apple notifies you before an update is installed.

3. Install the latest iOS using a Mac or PC (Optional)

If you can’t free up enough space on your iPhone for the over-the-air update, connect it to a computer instead. An OTA update has to download and unpack the installer on your iPhone’s internal storage, which can take several gigabytes of free space.

Updating through Finder lets your Mac download and unpack the update on its own storage, then install it directly on your iPhone.

Here’s how:

  1. Connect your iPhone to your Mac using an MFi-certified cable.
  2. Open Finder and select your iPhone in the left sidebar.
  3. Go to the General tab and click Check for Update. Your Mac will look for the iOS 27.2 update.
  4. When the update appears, click Download and Update and follow the on-screen instructions.

On a Windows PC, use the Apple Devices app (or iTunes on older versions of Windows) and follow the same steps. Macs running macOS Mojave or earlier use iTunes instead of Finder.

Enjoy the new features in iOS 27.2

That’s it. Follow any of the methods above, and your iPhone will be running the latest iOS in no time. Updating is exciting, but it’s even better when it goes smoothly.

So back up your data, free up space and stay plugged in, and you’ll be ready to enjoy everything iOS 27.2 has to offer, from the smarter Siri AI to the latest security fixes.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

keyPoints.title: iPhone Models Supporting iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Only iPhone 11 and newer models support iOS 26, while older models like iPhone XS, XS Max, and first-generation iPhone SE are supported up to iOS 18.

keyPoints.title: Preparation Before Installing iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Before updating, ensure your iPhone is backed up, has enough free storage space, and is connected to power and a stable Wi-Fi network to prevent disruptions.

keyPoints.title: Methods to Install iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: You can install iOS 26 via over-the-air update, automatic updates, or using a Mac with Finder if storage space is limited.

keyPoints.title: Supporting Devices List
keyPoints.explanation: Supported devices include iPhone SE (2nd & 3rd gen), iPhone 11 to 17 series, and Pro models, among others, with support finally returning to a pattern of more recent models.

keyPoints.title: Ensuring Smooth Update Experience
keyPoints.explanation: Follow recommended steps such as backing up data, freeing up space, and connecting to power to ensure a smooth installation of iOS 26 and enjoy its new features.

title.rendered: 10 Things you can do in GTA 6 that you couldn’t do in GTA 5

content.rendered:
We’re just weeks away from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the hype surrounding Rockstar Games’ next magnum opus is off the charts. Over the past couple of weeks, the developer has revealed plenty of new GTA 6 details about what players can expect from Vice City and the state of Leonida. From a more immersive world to new activities and mechanics, it’s clear that the game will take the series to a completely new level compared to its predecessor.

So, if you’re wondering what GTA 6 will let you do that GTA 5 didn’t, here are some of the biggest features you should look forward to.

1. Manage a full-blown relationship

One of the things you can do in GTA 6 that you couldn’t do in GTA 5 is managing the relationship between our protagonists, Jason and Lucia. How close they become and whether their relationship stands the test of time will come down to your actions.

You will be able to take them shopping, go on drives, commit robberies, and participate in various other activities to strengthen their bond. Neglecting their relationship could cause it to fall apart over time, which will have a direct impact on certain missions and story elements.

Unlike GTA 5, where Michael, Trevor, and Franklin did have a dynamic that was out of your control, GTA 6 seems to give players a much bigger say over how its protagonists interact and shape the story. It’s a much deeper system that adds RPG-like elements to the game.

2. Stop at gas stations to refuel

Gas stations in GTA 5 didn’t really serve much of a purpose, but Rockstar is changing that in GTA 6. This time around, we’re going to see functional gas stations where players can refuel and even repair their vehicles. That’s not all, as electric vehicles will also get access to dedicated charging stations around the game.

Whenever you decide to refuel or recharge your vehicle, a cutscene lasting around 10 seconds will play. Rockstar has stated that it doesn’t want fuel management to become a burden for players, which is why fuel consumption has been deliberately slowed down across all vehicles. Whether you like this feature or not, there’s no denying that it adds another layer of realism to the game.

3. Build a reputation as a criminal

GTA 6 will allow you to build your reputation as a criminal in Leonida with the new Criminal Profile system. It’s somewhat akin to the Honor system we saw in Red Dead Redemption 2, but it works a bit differently. The system will track what sort of criminal you end up being.

If you manage to de-escalate situations without causing chaos, you’ll be a professional. However, if you choose to take everyone out and cause destruction, your Criminal Profile will reflect that.

There are four different Criminal Profile states in the game: Professional, Aggressive, Violent, and Psycho. However, if you commit serious crimes, your profile will go beyond Psycho, and this change will be irreversible for the playthrough. Both Jason and Lucia will have their own individual Criminal Profiles.

4. Use your vehicle to store weapons

Say goodbye to the days of GTA 5, where you could carry infinite weapons and switch between them using the weapon wheel. With GTA 6, Rockstar is taking a realistic approach by requiring players to use their vehicles to store their weapons in the trunk. Every personal vehicle in the game will be able to carry your selected loadout as well.

This seems like a negative change on paper, but it’s going to completely change how vehicles are used and how missions are tackled. Instead of scrolling through the weapon wheel to find the right weapon for the situation, you’ll now have to think ahead about which vehicle to take and what weapons you want to bring along to deal with your targets.

5. Hit the gym to stay in shape

If you’re fond of staying fit and hitting the gym in real life, you’ll be able to do the same in GTA 6. Both Jason and Lucia will physically change depending on how much you play and what you eat. If you eat too much, for example, you can expect both protagonists to gain weight and look bigger.

This can be dealt with by hitting the gym. Players will be able to work out and exercise their characters to lose weight, and even build muscles. This means staying in shape will become another aspect of managing Jason and Lucia throughout the game.

It’s not just working out either, as other aspects of their lifestyle, such as getting enough sleep, can also affect the characters. This is a major change from GTA 5, where working out and maintaining your character’s fitness affected their hidden stats rather than their actual physical appearance in the game.

6. Explore a variety of new activities in leonida

Side activities aren’t exactly new to the GTA franchise, as previous games have featured tons of them. However, GTA 6 is amping up things by offering tons of new ones for players to enjoy.

What are we talking about? Well, for instance, the GTA 6 Extended Look revealed that players will be able to use VR headsets, watch in-game shows and commercials on their TVs, participate in car and bike races on dedicated tracks, try wrestling, read newspapers, go base jumping, hit clubs, take part in shooting ranges, go fishing, and even participate in backyard wrestling.

The activities we’ve mentioned above are just scratching the surface. Some activities that are worth looking out for are scuba diving and kayaking. With so much to do across Leonida, you won’t have to always focus on the main story missions.

7. Turn dirty money Into clean cash

GTA 6 will feature three different types of money: funds stored in your bank account, physical cash, and money kept in your duffel bag. Any money deposited in your bank account will be safe, just like in previous games. However, carrying cash comes with risks, as you’ll lose it if you die before depositing it at an ATM.

What’s interesting is how the game handles the money stored in your duffel bag. You’ll need to take it to a fence, essentially a black-market middleman who will take the stolen goods off your hands and pay you in return. This means money earned through robberies won’t be instantly credited to your account. You’ll need to take steps to turn your stolen loot into usable funds.

8. Reach a six-star wanted level

GTA 6 will bring back the franchise’s iconic wanted system, allowing players to cause chaos across Leonida, attracting different levels of police attention. The more trouble you cause, the more wanted stars you’ll earn, which will bring more forces after you. However, Rockstar is bringing several changes to make the system more immersive, such as NPC witnesses and police officers remembering your face, vehicle, and other details.

One of the biggest changes is the return of the six-star wanted level. This GTA 6 feature isn’t new, as it was present in older games but was removed in GTA 5. It’s currently unclear what kind of law enforcement response players can expect after reaching six stars, but one thing’s for certain: escaping the police at that level won’t be an easy task.

9. Dual-Wield your weapons

<insert image named “GTA6Weapons” >

Based on all the screenshots and leaks surrounding GTA 6, it seems like dual-wielding weapons is another potential feature that could make its way to the game. As the name suggests, this would allow players to wield two weapons at the same time, such as pistols or even shotguns, and fire them at the same time.

However, it’s crucial to remember that Rockstar Games hasn’t officially confirmed dual-wielding in GTA 6. There’s always a chance that the feature could be scrapped before the game’s final release.

10. Keep up with leonida on social media

Social media has become a huge part of our everyday lives, and GTA 6 looks set to bring that same influence to the game. Players will be able to access social media platforms through their phones, where they can watch short-form videos of people partying, pulling off stunts, and getting into all kinds of situations across Leonida. You will also be able to watch influencers and follow their accounts.

However, social media won’t be just about entertainment. It will also allow players to discover what’s happening across the state. You could come across livestreams of ongoing events and then travel to the location yourself to see what’s happening or even get involved.

Wrapping up

GTA 6 is shaping up to be a much more immersive experience than GTA 5, with Rockstar introducing several new mechanics and activities that could change how players interact with the world. From managing Jason and Lucia’s relationship and keeping them in shape to refuelling vehicles, storing weapons, and building a criminal profile, there’s plenty to explore beyond the main story.

With a more detailed world, expanded activities, social media, and a revamped wanted system, Leonida looks set to offer plenty of reasons to keep exploring even after completing missions. While some features, such as dual-wielding, remain unconfirmed, everything Rockstar has shown so far points toward a significantly deeper open-world experience than its predecessor.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

mainEntity.name: What are Race Rerolls in The Veil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Race Rerolls allow you to switch your character's race and roll for different stats. They allow you to create a character that works for your playstyle.

mainEntity.name: How to redeem codes in The Veil?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the game and look for the shop tab below the Health and Sanity bars. Choose codes and paste a working code.

mainEntity.name: Is The Veil a PvP or PvE game?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Veil brings both PvP and PvE aspects. Not only can you find hordes of enemies, but you can also face off against other players.
