title.rendered: 4K Video Downloader Plus review: A clean way to save online videos

content.rendered:
Saving one online video is easy enough. Keeping high-quality videos, playlists, subtitles, and audio organised is where browser tools start to feel clumsy. 4K Video Downloader Plus moves the whole job into a desktop app, with more control and fewer questionable download buttons.

It is available for Mac, Windows, and Linux, and the permanent free version covers occasional downloads. Unlike a platform-specific tool, it combines video, audio, subtitle, playlist, and file-management options in one place.

You can download 4K Video Downloader Plus for free and upgrade only if its daily limits or premium feature restrictions get in your way.

4K Video Downloader Plus review: Pros, cons, and key details

4K Video Downloader Plus suits people who save online videos regularly and care about file quality, formats, subtitles, or larger collections. It offers much more control than a basic web downloader while keeping the first download approachable.

Pros

  • Clean interface with a quick copy-and-paste workflow
  • Downloads in resolutions up to 4K and 8K when available
  • Useful format, audio, subtitle, playlist, and channel controls
  • Smart Mode removes repetitive setup
  • Permanent free tier is enough for occasional use

Cons

  • Free downloads have daily quantity limits
  • AI processing, automatic subscriptions, and other advanced tools require higher plans
  • Supported-site reliability can change when platforms update

4K Video Downloader Plus interface and download experience

The main window revolves around one obvious action: copy a video link and select Paste Link. The app analyses it, presents the available quality and format choices, and lets you choose where the file should go. It is a familiar workflow, but putting it inside a proper desktop app makes it feel safer and more predictable than jumping between web downloaders.

The interface does not force every setting into view. A casual user can accept the recommended options and move on, while someone building an offline collection can choose the resolution, format, audio track, subtitles, frame rate, and destination folder.

Supported websites, video quality, and file formats

4K Video Downloader Plus handles media from services such as YouTube, X (Twitter), Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Vimeo, Twitch, SoundCloud, and more. This broad coverage is useful if your saved media comes from several sites rather than one streaming platform.

4K Video Downloader Plus can save videos in MP4 or MKV at resolutions ranging from standard HD to 4K and 8K. The source still sets the limit; a 1080p upload will not become 4K, but the app preserves the best quality that is actually available.

It also covers the details that become important after the first few downloads:

  • Audio-only downloads: Extract audio as MP3, M4A, or OGG instead of keeping the full video.
  • Subtitles: Save available subtitles as SRT files, including multiple languages where provided.
  • Playlists and channels: Queue larger collections instead of feeding the app one link at a time.
  • Multiple audio tracks: Keep original or dubbed tracks when the source provides them.
  • Special video formats: Download supported 3D and 360-degree videos for offline playback.

What are the best features of 4K Video Downloader Plus?

Choosing the same format, resolution, subtitle language, and folder for every file gets old fast. Smart Mode lets you save those preferences once and apply them automatically to future downloads.

Smart Mode is the feature worth turning on first. Set MP4, your preferred quality, and a destination folder, and later downloads can start with little more than a pasted link.

The built-in browser lets you find media and start downloads without constantly switching between the app and a separate browser. Eligible paid plans also let you sign in to supported services for private or protected media that your account already has permission to view.

Users who follow regularly updated channels or playlists can subscribe to them in the app and automatically save new uploads. The built-in proxy can also help when a supported service is blocked by a network or unavailable in a region. These features require an appropriate premium plan, and availability and local rules still apply.

Version 26.1 also added AI audio processing. From the same workspace, Pro users can remove background noise or echo, isolate vocals or speech, and strip music from a downloaded file. These tools will not replace a full audio editor, but they are handy for cleaning up an interview, preparing a voice track, or making a quick karaoke version.

Download performance and file management

Download speed depends on the source website, resolution, connection, and file size. The practical performance advantage comes from the workflow: the app analyses links, queues downloads, and keeps completed files in one manageable list.

You can sort and filter downloads, control individual items or groups, and import or export download records. This matters once you move beyond occasional clips and start handling playlists, courses, reference videos, or several audio files at once.

Skip 8K unless you genuinely need it because the files can consume storage surprisingly quickly. Platform support can also break temporarily when video services change how they deliver or protect media, so keeping the app updated is important.

4K Video Downloader Plus free vs paid plans

The Starter tier is permanently free, with no payment details or short trial countdown. Its main restriction is a daily quantity limit, making it best for occasional use rather than large libraries.

The current premium options are straightforward:

Prices and promotions can change, so check the final purchase page before paying. For most people, the free plan is the right starting point. Personal offers better long-term value once the daily limits become annoying, while Pro makes sense only if you need its automation, AI processing, or commercial license.

The current desktop release requires macOS 12 or later, Windows 11 or later, or 64-bit Ubuntu 22.04 with GNOME or later. Native Apple Silicon and Intel installers are available for Mac.

Is 4K Video Downloader Plus worth it?

Yes, if saving online media is something you do regularly. 4K Video Downloader Plus brings quality controls, audio extraction, subtitles, playlists, repeat-download presets, and file management into one clean desktop app. It feels like a proper utility rather than a website you visit only when every other option fails.

Occasional users should stay with the free tier. You can use it to download YouTube videos one at a time, download full playlists, save a Facebook video, or extract Instagram Reel audio. The desktop app earns its place when you want consistent quality, repeatable settings, and organised downloads.

The main limitation is outside the app’s control: video platforms change frequently, and support can occasionally break until an update arrives. You should also download only content you own, have permission to save, or are otherwise authorised to use.

Verdict: 4.5/5.

4K Video Downloader Plus combines a friendly interface with enough depth for demanding downloads. The free version is genuinely useful, and the paid plans add convenience without turning the basic experience into a demo.

title.rendered: Apple A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: 7 biggest upgrades you need to know

content.rendered:
I have come to a stage where Apple’s yearly chip upgrades are difficult to judge by the name alone. An A20 Pro seems like a straightforward successor to the A19 Pro, but once I got to know about the actual improvements, I realised Apple has got much more under the hood.

The A20 Pro is the first 2nm iPhone chip, featuring a 7-core GPU, wide memory bandwidth, a dual Neural Engine, and new CPU cores. This makes it one of the greatest improvements Apple has made to its mobile silicon in recent times.

So, how big is the change that you will experience? I have analysed the A20 Pro vs A19 Pro across performance, gaming, AI, memory, efficiency, and thermal performance to see what has really changed and whether the A20 Pro is a good enough reason to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Specs at a glance

Before getting into the interesting stuff, here’s how the two Apple Silicon generations compare.

The interesting part is that Apple didn’t simply increase the CPU core count. Both chips have six CPU cores. However, in order to improve performance, Apple decided to redesign the CPU cores, push up clock speeds, and redesign many elements around them.

And that is only the beginning.

2nm vs 3nm: The biggest A20 Pro upgrade

When it comes to choosing just one upgrade for the A20 Pro, then it has to be the move from 3nm to 2nm.

The A19 Pro was manufactured using a 3nm-class process, while the A20 Pro moves to TSMC’s N2 2nm process. This lets Apple fit more transistors into a similar die area while providing 18% faster performance and 30% lower power consumption, compared to the A19 Pro.

Besides that, M-class packaging design puts memory and the silicon die in a side-by-side position. This leads to an improvement in the heat dissipation capabilities of the A20 Pro.

Why does 2nm matter on an iPhone?

This is because smartphone CPUs have an inconvenient challenge: They require desktop-level performance without desktop-class cooling.

I can mount a huge cooler on a desktop processor. Apple won’t be able to put it into their iPhone. That’s why efficiency is so important.

The A20 Pro’s 2nm foundation gives Apple more room to increase performance without increasing power draw and overheating. And Apple has used that extra headroom across the CPU, GPU, memory subsystem, and AI hardware. Ultimately, you get better battery life and speed.

CPU performance: How much faster is it?

The A20 Pro retains a six-core CPU, but Apple has introduced two new Super cores and four new efficiency cores. The Super cores can reach up to 4.93GHz, compared with roughly 4.26GHz on the A19 Pro’s Everest performance cores. Apple describes the new cores as desktop-class and says they are up to 20% faster.

And the benchmark numbers back up the idea that this isn’t a minor CPU refresh.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Benchmark Comparison

An early Geekbench 7 result represented improvements of about 23.3% in single-core and 27.1% in multi-core in that particular comparison.

The A20 Pro also has a clear edge over Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in CPU performance, particularly in single-core workloads. In Geekbench 6, the latter typically scores around 3,588 and 10,207, respectively. That puts Apple ahead by roughly 50% in single-core and 29% in multi-core, according to these reported results.

What about real-world performance?

Having owned an A19 Pro iPhone before, I would not expect the A20 Pro to instantly give me a 25% improvement in basic operations. The A19 Pro is already very fast.

But the difference will be much more noticeable if the workload makes the CPU work for a longer period of time:

  • Video editing
  • Photo processing
  • 3D applications
  • AI workloads
  • Gaming
  • Large file processing
  • Heavy multitasking

So yes, the A20 Pro CPU performance has improved substantially. But I think that the more interesting part is how Apple will use the additional performance over a longer period.

GPU and gaming performance

The A19 Pro has already received a major GPU upgrade, with Neural Accelerators built into each GPU core and a larger 32 MB cache. This improved hardware ray tracing and graphics performance and enabled direct handling of complex on-device AI workloads.

The A20 Pro gets a meaningful graphics upgrade on this.

Apple has moved from the A19 Pro’s 6-core GPU to a 7-core GPU. The new GPU also includes Neural Accelerators designed to accelerate AI-related workloads, while Apple claims the A20 Pro delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance than the A19 Pro.

This makes the A20 Pro very appealing for gaming purposes.

But I wouldn’t judge the GPU upgrade solely by a short benchmark. A smartphone can render a very high frame rate for just a few minutes, after which it starts to struggle because of overheating. This is why I believe the A20 Pro’s GPU update looks even more exciting when combined with its thermal architecture.

For demanding games, the improvements should matter most in:

  • Higher and more stable frame rates
  • Better ray-tracing performance
  • More demanding graphics settings
  • Longer gaming sessions
  • Reduced performance degradation from heat
  • Better handling of graphics-heavy AI features

Early Geekbench graphics results also show a performance gain of approximately 38-40% for the A20 Pro’s full 7-core GPU, although such tests shouldn’t be considered a general benchmark of gaming performance.

If I were buying an iPhone to play demanding games, I’d pick the A20 Pro without any doubts. Though the A19 Pro itself has some good capabilities, its successor has more graphics hardware and sustainability.

Memory: A20 Pro gets a wider highway

This is probably the A20 Pro upgrade that most people will overlook. Both generations can have 12GB of LPDDR5X-9600 memory; hence, the impression is that there is not much change from the earlier version.

But the memory interface is wider. The A19 Pro uses a 64-bit memory interface, reaching up to 76.8 Gb/s bandwidth. The A20 Pro reportedly moves to a 96-bit interface, thus supporting 115.2 Gb/s memory bandwidth, which is 50% better.

I like to think of memory bandwidth as a highway. The amount of RAM is roughly how much cargo I can keep available, whereas Memory bandwidth is how quickly I can move that cargo around. Adding more lanes becomes useful when I start moving huge amounts of data, especially for GPU, AI, and graphics workloads.

That’s why this upgrade matters for:

  • AI processing
  • Graphics rendering
  • Gaming
  • Video editing
  • Large image processing
  • Multitasking
  • On-device machine learning

And it helps explain why Apple can improve performance without simply throwing more CPU cores into the chip.

Neural Engine and AI performance

AI is no longer just an additional feature at Apple, and the A20 Pro is a clear example of this.

While the A19 Pro features a 16-core Neural Engine, the A20 Pro comes with two Neural Engines, which results in 32 Neural Engine cores. Moreover, the A20 Pro has Neural Accelerators in the GPU system.

According to Apple, these Neural Accelerators will provide 2x faster performance in FP8 operations. This matters because Apple is now focusing more on executing AI on the device itself.

Instead of sending every AI request to a cloud server, more processing can happen locally using Apple’s new Foundation Models. That can improve responsiveness and privacy while reducing the need for a constant internet connection.

The A20 Pro’s AI hardware should therefore be useful for:

  • Apple Intelligence
  • Generative AI
  • Image generation
  • AI-assisted photo editing
  • Voice processing
  • On-device language models
  • Real-time image and video processing

In my view, it looks like the A20 Pro has been built to handle not only the Apple Intelligence features the current iPhone has, but also future features Apple might want to introduce.

Thermal performance: Where A20 Pro could make the biggest real-world difference

This is my favourite A20 Pro upgrade because it addresses a genuine problem: heat.

The A20 Pro also changes how Apple packages the chip for sustained performance. Unlike past Apple processors, which used PoP (Package-On-Package), the A20 Pro will have WMCM (Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module) packaging, placing the memory beside the main chip instead.

This will make sure that the heat can now have a clear route out of the CPU and GPU and not get trapped around the hottest part of the chip. In practice, that should help the A20 Pro reduce thermal throttling and maintain higher performance for longer.

Apart from that, Apple has also upgraded the iPhone 18 Pro by including a vapour chamber three times the size of its predecessor. The wider surface area distributes heat and helps it dissipate faster. With all of these, the A20 Pro is able to give 40% better sustained performance compared to the A19 Pro.

This could benefit:

  • Long gaming sessions
  • 4K and high-resolution video editing
  • ProRes workflows
  • 3D rendering
  • AI processing
  • Photography processing
  • Other sustained workloads

And this is where I think the A20 Pro could feel more different from the A19 Pro than the raw benchmark numbers suggest.

Modem and connectivity improvements

The A20 Pro generation also changes what’s happening beyond the processor itself.

The iPhone 18 Pro generation introduces Apple’s C2 modem to the Pro lineup, replacing the Snapdragon X80 modem used in the previous Pro generation. According to Apple, the C2 is capable of delivering 50% faster uploads and 15% lower power consumption and uses mmWave 5G (only in the USA).

The A20 Pro generation also continues Apple’s move toward in-house connectivity hardware. The N1 wireless chip handles technologies including Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread.

For me, the important part isn’t simply that Apple has replaced one modem with another. It’s the possibility of tighter integration of Apple’s own silicon for better power consumption, connectivity, and system-level performance.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: Should you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro?

After analysing all the aspects, it was clear that the A20 Pro is really a great upgrade.

However, this does not necessarily mean everyone owning an A19 Pro must go out and get an iPhone 18 Pro. If you already own an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone 17 Pro Max, I wouldn’t upgrade just for everyday speed.

The A19 Pro is already ridiculously fast. If you utilise your iPhone 18 Pro primarily for messaging, web-browsing, social media interaction, photography, and media streaming, you will hardly notice any difference.

I’d consider the upgrade much more seriously if I:

  • Play demanding games regularly
  • Edit videos on my iPhone
  • Use AI-intensive features
  • Want the best possible graphics performance
  • Keep my iPhone for four or five years
  • Care about sustained performance
  • Want Apple’s latest modem and connectivity hardware

For someone buying a new Pro iPhone anyway, though, I’d take the A20 Pro over the A19 Pro every time.

Final thoughts

The A20 Pro is more than just a faster version of the A19 Pro. Apple has practically upgraded every single aspect of the performance equation. Here you have 2nm process, new CPU architecture, larger GPU, increased memory bandwidth, improved AI architecture, and even better thermal management.

For me, the biggest advantage is that Apple isn’t just chasing higher peak performance; it is trying to keep the A20 Pro running fast for longer and able to sustain it.

Is the A20 Pro’s extra power enough to make you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro? Let me know in the comments below!

title.rendered: Build and Kill Zombies codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Build and Kill Zombies Codes on October 05, 2026

Build and Kill Zombies is a Roblox game where you build your own vehicles and then do whatever it takes to mow down hordes of zombies. However, building the best vehicles in the game requires the right weapons, seats, Hacker Tones, tanks, and plenty of cash. Luckily, the developers have released several codes that let you get your hands on these items for free! So, let’s take a look at all the active Build and Kill Zombies codes and help you build the ultimate zombie-destroying machine.

All working Build and Kill Zombies codes

  • ZEUS: 50 Lightning Tokens
  • IAMPRO: 5,000 Cash
  • COMMUNITY: 1k Cash 1 Small Engine 1 Small Tank
  • CashDrop: 500 Cash
  • MOREFRIENDS: 2 Passenger Seats

Expired or unverified Build and Kill Zombies codes

1X1X1X1, HACKER

How to redeem Build and Kill Zombies codes

The next question you might be wondering is: how do you redeem Build and Kill Zombies codes? Well, it’s quite a simple process –

  1. Fire up Build and Kill Zombies on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Tap on the Shop button.
  4. Paste a working code in the community codes section.
  5. Click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed a code, the rewards will automatically be added to your inventory in the game.

Where to find more Build and Kill Zombies codes

Build and Kill Zombies doesn’t have a fixed timeline when it comes to dropping reward codes. So, if you’re looking to grab more items, it’s a good idea to keep an eye on the official Build and Kill Zombies Discord server.

The developers can release new codes alongside new updates, events, or milestones, which you can track through the Build and Kill Zombies game page.

Be sure to bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated with the latest codes as they’re released. If you’re into shooting games and want more free rewards, check out the latest Beat the Anime Boss codes, Gym League Codes, Command An Army codes and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

title.rendered: Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude

content.rendered:
Anthropic is folding Claude Cowork into the main Claude chat experience. In its September 16 announcement, the company says users will be able to ask a quick question or hand over a larger task from the same conversation, without first choosing between Chat and Cowork.

The change is rolling out to Pro and Max subscribers over the next few weeks on Claude’s web, desktop, and mobile apps. Team and Free plans will follow, while Enterprise administrators will receive at least 30 days’ notice before their organizations move over.

One conversation can handle quick questions and bigger tasks

The new experience lets Claude decide what a request needs. A conversation can stay short, or turn into research, a report, a spreadsheet, or a presentation that Claude works on after you step away.

Anthropic’s Help Center guide says existing chats, tasks, projects, artifacts, connectors, and skills come with the account when it moves to the new experience. Once the change reaches an account, users cannot switch back to separate Chat and Cowork options.

Docs, Slides, and Design move into the conversation

Anthropic is also adding Claude Docs and Claude Slides, while Claude Design can now work inside regular conversations. The company says all three are in beta on paid plans. Users can edit the results, share them by link, or export a presentation as a PowerPoint or PDF.

The useful part is the handoff. Someone can start with a question, ask Claude to gather information, and finish with a document or slide deck in the same thread. The app can also use connected services such as Google Drive, Gmail, Microsoft 365, and Slack while it works.

What happens during the rollout

There is no switch to turn on. If your message box still shows separate Chat and Cowork choices, Anthropic says your account has not moved yet. If a task runs in the cloud, it can continue after you close your laptop. Tasks that need local files or computer apps still require Claude Desktop to remain open.

The change also makes Claude Cowork’s iPhone and web access more central, since users can check progress or answer questions from a phone while a task continues. Claude Code remains a separate coding environment, including workflows covered in Claude Code’s iOS Simulator support on Mac.

The practical shift is simple: users no longer need to decide where a task belongs before they start typing. The new unified experience is arriving gradually, and the older Chat and Cowork choices will disappear only when Anthropic moves each account over.

title.rendered: iOS 27.2 beta 1 adds a redesigned Health app, FaceTime Dual Capture, and an EU privacy update

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 27.2 developer beta 1, build 24B5084k. Apple’s developer release listing dates the seed to September 16, 2026. The beta brings a redesigned Health app and Group FaceTime Dual Capture, while Apple’s release notes add a privacy-related change for users in the European Union.

Developers with beta access can install the update from Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates, then choose iOS 27 Developer Beta. It is still pre-release software, so the feature list can change as Apple continues testing.

Health app and FaceTime changes lead the beta

The redesigned Health app Apple previewed earlier this month is now active in the beta. The official Health announcement describes a new Insights tab, a Longevity tab, and Apple Intelligence-powered health guidance. The beta gives developers an early look at that redesign, although Apple has not said that every part of the final experience is locked.

Group FaceTime also gains Dual Capture. On supported iPhones, it can show the front and rear camera views at the same time, keeping your face in a small window while you show the other person what is in front of you. Apple’s FaceTime camera guide says the feature is available on iPhone 17 or later.

The wider release includes far more than this beta. Our iOS 27 features guide covers the Siri AI, Liquid Glass, Photos, Wallet, and child-safety changes Apple announced for iOS 27.

Apple’s release notes add an EU tracking prompt change

Apple’s iOS 27.2 beta release notes say AppTrackingTransparency now supports an alternative expanded prompt and yearly re-prompting for users in the EU. Apple says the alternative prompt is required in France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Romania.

The same notes list two known issues: personalized summaries may not generate as expected in the Health app’s Insights tab, and the Describe a Shortcut feature may return an error. Those are useful warnings if you are installing the beta to try the new Health experience.

The first iOS 27.2 seed arrives after the late iOS 27.0 testing cycle, including iOS 27 beta 7 coverage. Apple has not announced a public release date for iOS 27.2, so the current build is best treated as an early look at the next round of changes.

title.rendered: WhatsApp may soon let iPhone users add a third account

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is preparing to raise the iPhone’s in-app account limit from two to three, according to WABetaInfo’s September 15 report. The feature was spotted in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.37.10.15, but it is still under development and is not available to beta testers yet.

The change would build on WhatsApp’s recent two-account rollout for iPhone. Meta’s March announcement gave iPhone users a way to keep work and personal numbers in the same app without logging out or carrying two phones.

The third account would use the same account list

WABetaInfo says users would see an "Add account" option even after two profiles are already active. The third number could be added from the account list in Settings or through the Switch accounts option.

Each account would keep its own chat history, notifications, privacy settings, backup, and media. App Lock would also work separately for each profile, so securing one account would not automatically change the others. The account selector would continue to show a profile name, photo, and phone number, with a checkmark beside the active account.

Three accounts would help people with three phone numbers

Two slots cover the usual work-and-personal setup. A third slot could help people who keep a separate number for a business, side project, family, or another role. It could also reduce the need to use WhatsApp Business as a workaround or keep a second phone nearby.

The idea follows WhatsApp’s move to two accounts on one iPhone. If you need the current two-account setup, our updated guide to using two WhatsApp accounts on iPhone covers the available options.

The third account is not available yet

WABetaInfo says the feature was found in the 26.37.10.15 beta, but the three-account option itself is not ready for testing. Installing that build will not guarantee access, and WhatsApp has not shared a public release timeline.

For now, iPhone users can officially manage up to two accounts inside WhatsApp. The third slot is a planned expansion, not a feature you can turn on today.

mainEntity.name: Can I get the Lucy skin in Fortnite for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

title.rendered: Fortnite x Kingdom Hearts collab: Here’s when the Sora skin will arrive

content.rendered:
Sora, the protagonist of the popular long-running RPG series called Kingdom Hearts, is finally coming to Fortnite later this week. The iconic video game character was one of the major faces displayed in the promotional material at the beginning of Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4.

Ever since Fortnite Override rolled out, Sora has been a highly anticipated addition to the multiplayer game’s skins catalogue. For nearly a month, players have been speculating when such Kingdom Hearts-inspired cosmetics may hit the Shop.

Thanks to some recent posts shared by Fortnite’s official channels, we now not only have a confirmed date for the Fortnite x Kingdom Hearts content drop but also have fresh glimpses of the same.

Sora Fortnite skin release date and time

The Kingdom Hearts collab, including the Sora skin, is scheduled to land in Fortnite on Thursday, September 17, with the exact time expected to be 5 PM PT. Below, you can check the timings, as per your time zone, for when this collab content will go live in the Item Shop.

All Fortnite x Kingdom Hearts skins revealed so far

Recently, Fortnite has been teasing the arrival of the Kingdom Hearts content drop in the Item Shop, with each passing day. In the same vein, the highly popular online game has confirmed that Sora isn’t the only character from the Square Enix-developed franchise to enter the fray, with more fan-favourite figures set to join alongside him.

Through a new trailer, Fortnite confirmed that the following characters from Kingdom Hearts will also appear in the Shop on the same day.

Sora

Sora, the main protagonist of Kingdom Hearts, is finally making his Fortnite debut as part of the crossover. The iconic Keyblade wielder brings his recognisable look to the game, along with Kingdom Hearts-inspired cosmetics. His arrival has been one of the most anticipated parts of the crossover.

Roxas

Roxas, one of the most recognisable characters from the Kingdom Hearts series, is also joining Fortnite alongside Sora. Known for wielding dual Keyblades and his connection to Sora, Roxas brings another major character from the franchise to the Item Shop. His inclusion gives Kingdom Hearts fans another familiar face to add to their collection.

Kairi

Kairi is another key Kingdom Hearts character, making her Fortnite debut with the crossover. As one of the series’ central characters, she joins Sora and Roxas in bringing the world of Kingdom Hearts to Fortnite. Her arrival rounds out the lineup with another fan-favourite character from the franchise.

Riku

Riku, Sora’s longtime friend and rival, is also part of the Fortnite x Kingdom Hearts crossover. His journey throughout the Kingdom Hearts series makes him one of its most important recurring characters. With Riku joining the lineup, Fortnite players can bring another iconic member of the series into their matches.

Wrapping up

With Sora on his way to join the Fortnite skins catalogue soon, it brings to a close another period of anticipation and speculation for fans. However, since Joker from the Persona series is another highly anticipated character confirmed to arrive during the Fortnite Override season, it may now be time for the community’s focus to shift to him.

While the arrival of Sora in itself is exciting, the fact that more key Kingdom Hearts characters such as Kairi, Roxas, and Riku are also being thrown into the mix makes it even more exciting for fans of the Japanese IP. It will be interesting to see how prevalent the Sora skin gets in Fortnite lobbies in the coming days—and if it reaches the levels of the Sonic The Hedgehog skin in that aspect.

FAQs

Is Sora Fortnite skin free?

No, the Sora skin in Fortnite is set to be added to the Item Shop, where it will only be available for purchase using V-Bucks. However, there are multiple reports of the skin also being available as a reward for placing high enough in a forthcoming event called Kingdom Hearts Cup.

Which other video game franchises are yet to release collab content for Fortnite Override?

Some other video game IPs that are confirmed to arrive later in the season include Persona, 99 Nights In The Forest (Roblox game), Peak, among others.

Which other video game protagonists have appeared in Fortnite before?

In the past, popular gaming protagonists such as Master Chief, Kratos, Crash Bandicoot, Lara Croft, and Marcus Fenix have been released as Fortnite skins.

title.rendered: Does the iPhone Duo have MagSafe? Here’s what Apple actually says

content.rendered:
When Apple announced the iPhone Duo, one question immediately caught my attention: does it have MagSafe? That might sound small, but I think it is one of the more important questions to answer before buying one.

Many of us have already invested in MagSafe chargers, battery packs, wallets, stands, and car mounts. The last thing I would want is to discover that my new iPhone technically supports MagSafe but makes half of my accessories useless.

The good news is that the iPhone Duo does have MagSafe. However, there is a catch: not every existing MagSafe accessory will work properly with the foldable iPhone Duo. Here’s what Apple says and what you need to know before the phone goes on sale on October 23.

Does the iPhone Duo Have MagSafe?

Yes. The iPhone Duo has MagSafe built-in.

Apple’s technical specifications list:

  • MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W
  • Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W
  • A magnet array
  • An alignment magnet
  • Accessory Identification NFC
  • Magnetometer

That second part is particularly important.

The magnet array and an alignment magnet in the iPhone Duo make MagSafe accessories snap into position. That means the phone isn’t relying solely on the charging coil to work with a MagSafe charger.

How fast is MagSafe charging on the iPhone Duo?

The iPhone Duo supports MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W.

Apple says the phone can reach up to 50% charge in around 30 minutes when using a MagSafe Charger paired with a 35W adapter or higher.

For comparison, wired USB-C charging is faster, reaching up to 50% in around 20 minutes when connected to a 60W-capable adapter or higher.

So I wouldn’t buy the iPhone Duo expecting MagSafe to replace wired charging when I need the fastest possible top-up. Instead, I see MagSafe as the convenience option.

Can I use existing MagSafe chargers with the iPhone Duo?

Yes, the iPhone Duo is designed to work with MagSafe chargers.

So if you already own Apple’s MagSafe Charger, you don’t need to buy another charger for the iPhone Duo.

However, MagSafe charging compatibility isn’t the same as accessory compatibility. A MagSafe charger only needs to align with the charging area. Other MagSafe accessories can have very different physical requirements.

For example, a battery pack needs enough usable space around the magnetic attachment area. But the Duo’s dimensions and camera bump can cause problems with larger MagSafe power banks.

What about MagSafe cases for the iPhone Duo?

Apple has released the iPhone Duo Case, a two-part protective case designed specifically for the foldable phone.

It is compatible with:

  • MagSafe
  • Qi2 at 25W
  • Qi-certified chargers

The case also has built-in magnets designed to align with the iPhone Duo. Apple’s iPhone Duo Folio is another option. It includes an integrated kickstand and is also designed around the Duo’s foldable form factor.

There are already several third-party iPhone Duo cases with magnetic charging support, including options from Spigen, Ridge, FNTCASE, and others. However, the design of each case matters because the hinge and folding mechanism can affect how some MagSafe accessories attach to the phone.

If you’re still deciding which case to buy, I’ve put together a separate list of the best iPhone Duo cases, including Apple’s official case, rugged options, slim cases, and more affordable alternatives.

Do MagSafe accessories work while the iPhone Duo is folded?

The iPhone Duo has a completely different shape from a regular iPhone. It folds in half, has a hinge, and has a different camera layout.

That means an accessory can magnetically attach to the phone and still be awkward to use. Some existing batteries don’t have enough usable space around the magnetic attachment area, while others could extend beyond the bottom of the Duo.

Moreover, the camera bump and the Duo’s dimensions make the standard MagSafe wallet arrangement problematic. That’s a big deal if you were expecting to take your existing MagSafe wallet from your current iPhone and simply slap it onto the Duo.

You should also consider MagSafe car mounts and stands. These accessories were generally designed around the dimensions of traditional iPhones, so their size and positioning can matter just as much as the magnets themselves.

I’ve rounded up the accessories I’d actually consider buying in my guide to the best iPhone Duo accessories, including MagSafe-compatible cases, a 65W adapter, a Qi2 wireless charger, power banks, and magnetic car mounts. They are specifically designed around the Duo’s unusual dimensions.

Does iPhone Duo support Qi2?

Yes, the iPhone Duo supports Qi2 wireless charging at up to 25W, which is the same maximum charging speed Apple lists for MagSafe.

I think this is good news because Qi2 gives you more freedom when shopping for wireless chargers and magnetic accessories. Qi2 uses magnetic alignment similar to MagSafe, but it is an industry-wide wireless charging standard rather than an Apple-only system.

There is one thing I would watch out for, though: “magnetic” doesn’t automatically mean Qi2. A charger can use magnets to hold your iPhone Duo in place without being Qi2-certified. Likewise, seeing “MagSafe compatible” on a product doesn’t necessarily mean it will deliver the full 25W charging speed.

So, when I’m shopping for a charger, I wouldn’t rely on the word “magnetic” alone. I’d look for the product listing to explicitly mention Qi2 25W or MagSafe 25W support for full-speed charging.

Final thoughts

After looking through Apple’s specifications, I think the MagSafe situation on the iPhone Duo is actually pretty straightforward, but only if we separate charging from accessories.

The iPhone Duo has the magnets required for MagSafe and supports 25W MagSafe and Qi2 charging. However, not every MagSafe accessory will work perfectly with the Duo. Its foldable design changes the way accessories fit, so I’d always check for iPhone Duo compatibility before buying one.

With the iPhone Duo launching on October 23, will you be keeping your old MagSafe accessories or starting fresh with Duo-specific ones?

title.rendered: Beat the Anime Boss codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Beat the Anime Boss codes on October 16, 2026

Beat the Anime is a Roblox game where you’ll take on the fight against powerful anime-inspired bosses. However, taking down these enemies is no joke, as you’ll need to progress your character by upgrading their stats and collecting various items.

Luckily, the developers regularly release codes that can give you free rewards, including Mutation Crystals, Potions, Luck Potions, Cash, and more! So, let’s take a look at all the Beast the Anime boss codes and how you can use these freebies to dominate your enemies.

All working Beat the Anime Boss codes

  • SPOOKYUPDATE: Cash
  • TRICKORTREAT: 30 Candies
  • HAPPYHALLOWEEN: Potions
  • PRIMORDIAL: Potions
  • RAIDKEYS: 3 Raid Keys
  • TRADINGPLAZA: Gems
  • LUCKY161: Potions
  • GIGANTICUPDATE: Potions and Cash
  • JANTSISNOTCOOL: Potions and Cash
  • WOW!ARTIFACT: Death Note
  • BESTGUILDS: Gems
  • PUBLICTRADING: Gems
  • 6.7MVISITS: Potion
  • 67KLIKES: Potions

Expired or unverified Beat the Anime Boss codes

As of now, all the Beat the Anime codes we’ve mentioned above are still active. We’ll make to sure update this list whenever any of the codes expire, so you can safely redeem them without having to worry.

How to redeem Beat the Anime Boss codes

The next obvious question is: how do you redeem Beat the Anime Boss codes? Well, it’s quite a simple process –

  1. Fire up Beat the Anime Boss on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Select the ‘codes‘ icon from the menu on the left.
  4. Paste a working code.
  5. Click Redeem to claim your reward.

Once you’ve redeemed a code, the rewards will automatically be added to your inventory in the game.

Where to find more Beat the Anime Boss codes

Beat the Anime Boss doesn’t have a fixed schedule when it comes to releasing codes. So, if you’re looking to grab more free rewards, it’s a good idea to keep an eye on the official Beat the Anime Discord server.

The developers can release new codes alongside new updates, events, or milestones, which you can track through the Beat the Anime Boss game page.

Be sure to bookmark this page, as we’ll keep it updated with the latest codes as they’re released. If you’re into shooting games and want more free rewards, check out the latest Stay Hard Run codes, Gym League Codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

Missed this? Check It out:

  • Prehistoric Farm codes

title.rendered: MSP360 Backup review: Flexible cloud backup without storage lock-in

content.rendered:
Most backup apps sell the software and cloud space as one package. MSP360 Backup lets you choose where your data goes, including Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, a NAS, or a local drive.

That freedom is the reason to use MSP360 Cloud Backup software. It is also the catch. You get more control over storage, security, and cost, but setup takes more thought than signing into a service such as Backblaze and letting it run.

MSP360 Cloud Backup review at a glance

MSP360 works best for people and small teams that already have cloud storage in mind or want to avoid tying years of backups to one provider. Mac users get capable file backup, while Windows users can add full-system images and bare-metal recovery.

Pros

  • Works with a wide choice of cloud and local storage
  • Useful free edition for personal computers
  • Detailed schedules, retention rules, versioning, and file restore
  • Paid plans add encryption, compression, and immutable backups
  • Managed Backup can control many computers from one web console

Cons

  • Cloud storage is billed separately
  • Setup is less friendly than an all-in-one backup subscription
  • macOS and Linux support file backup only
  • The free Mac edition has no client-side encryption or compression
  • Product editions and storage costs take time to compare

A guided setup with one extra job

MSP360 organises backup around plans. You add a storage destination, choose the files or drives to protect, set a schedule and retention policy, then save the plan. The wizard breaks those decisions into manageable screens instead of dropping every option into one settings window.

The extra job is connecting storage. A local drive is straightforward, but cloud backup may require an account, bucket, region, and access credentials from the storage provider. That is normal for IT tools. It feels like work if you expected one email sign-in and an unlimited storage button.

Once the first plan is ready, MSP360 becomes much less demanding. It can run backups on a schedule, resume missed jobs, send email reports, keep older file versions, and remove old restore points according to your retention rules.

Storage choice is MSP360’s strongest feature

MSP360 supports major providers such as Amazon S3, Microsoft Azure, Backblaze B2, Google Cloud, IDrive e2, Wasabi, MinIO, Impossible Cloud, and other S3-compatible services. It can also write to external drives, network shares, and NAS storage.

This is more useful than a long compatibility list suggests. You can keep a fast local copy for quick restores and a cloud copy away from your computer. You can also move to a provider whose price, region, or retention rules suit you better without changing backup software.

The downside is a less predictable bill. MSP360’s license does not include cloud capacity. The storage provider may charge for stored data, requests, retrieval, and downloads. Cheap archive tiers look attractive until you need a large restore quickly, so check recovery fees and waiting periods before choosing one.

If you mainly want files synced across devices, a regular cloud storage service for Mac will be easier. MSP360 is for versioned backup and recovery, not everyday file sharing.

Mac backup is useful but file-only

The platform difference matters more than the feature count. On Windows, MSP360 Cloud Backup software can back up selected files or create an image of the system, including the operating system, apps, settings, and data. Eligible Windows editions can restore that image to a repaired computer, new hardware, or a virtual machine.

On macOS and Linux, MSP360 backs up files and folders only. You can protect Documents, Photos libraries, project folders, external drives, and selected network data, but you cannot create a bootable or full-system Mac image with it.

That makes MSP360 a companion to Time Machine rather than a replacement. Time Machine remains the simpler way to back up an entire Mac to an external drive. MSP360 earns its place when you want selected files copied to cloud storage you control, with more precise schedules and retention.

The current Mac app supports Intel and Apple silicon. The native Apple silicon build requires macOS 13 Ventura or later and 8 GB RAM. The Intel build supports macOS 10.12 or later, with 4 GB RAM as the minimum.

Security is strong when you configure it properly

MSP360 Pro can encrypt backup data before it leaves the computer with AES-128, AES-192, or AES-256 encryption. This client-side approach matters because the storage provider receives encrypted data rather than the original files.

Keep the encryption password somewhere safe. MSP360 does not store it, and there is no reset link that can unlock an encrypted backup. Lose the password and the backup is useless.

Paid editions also support Object Lock with compatible Amazon S3, Wasabi, and Backblaze B2 storage. Object Lock keeps backup data from being changed or deleted during a chosen period, which gives ransomware less opportunity to damage the recovery copy.

The free edition is less reassuring on Mac. It has versioning and the storage provider’s own transport security, but the Mac edition comparison shows that client-side encryption and compression require Pro. Free is fine for a local test or low-risk files. I would pay for Pro before sending private documents or family photos to third-party cloud storage.

Scheduling and restores offer real control

Backup plans can run manually, once at a set time, or on a recurring schedule. You can filter file types, skip folders, limit bandwidth, keep a set number of versions, retain backups for a chosen period, and receive an email when a job finishes or fails.

The restore wizard mirrors the backup process. Choose the storage account and backup plan, select a restore point, pick the files, then restore them to their original location or another folder. You can recover the latest copy or go back to an older version before a bad edit, deletion, or corruption.

This part is practical, but it deserves a test before you trust it. Run a small backup, delete or move a harmless file, and restore it to a temporary folder. A green backup report proves that data was uploaded. A successful restore proves that you can get it back.

Large restores still depend on the storage provider and your connection. A local drive will usually be faster than cloud storage, while archive tiers may take hours to prepare data and charge a retrieval fee.

MSP360 Free, Pro, or Managed Backup?

The three editions suit different levels of control. The current prices below cover the software license. Cloud storage costs are separate.

The Free edition is generous. It has no time limit, supports local and cloud destinations, allows one network share, and protects up to 5 TB. Start there if you want to understand the workflow before paying.

MSP360 Pro pricing is low for the backup software itself. Pro is the better choice for cloud backups of private files because it adds encryption and compression. Each license covers one computer, though, so the savings shrink as you add devices.

Managed Backup is for a different problem. It adds central monitoring, alerts, remote administration, and a web console for multiple endpoints. A small company with five or more computers should compare it with buying and checking several standalone Pro licenses. A home user does not need it.

Who should skip MSP360 Backup?

Skip MSP360 if you want one subscription with storage included and almost no setup. An all-in-one service will be easier to understand, even if it gives you less control. The best Mac backup software includes simpler options for continuous personal backup.

Mac users who want full-system recovery should also keep Time Machine or another disk-level Mac tool. MSP360 protects Mac files well, but it cannot rebuild the entire Mac from an image.

It is also a poor fit if you do not want to learn how your storage provider charges for retrieval and downloads. The lowest price per terabyte is not always the cheapest backup once recovery begins.

Is MSP360 Backup worth it?

Yes, if storage control matters more to you than a one-click setup. MSP360 combines local backup, broad cloud support, flexible schedules, version recovery, encryption, and immutable storage without forcing your data into one company’s cloud.

The Free edition is a good way to test the workflow. Pro is worth the modest annual cost for encryption and compression, especially on a Mac. Managed Backup makes sense only when several computers need central oversight.

The rough edge is not the backup engine. It is the buying decision. You must choose an edition, a storage provider, a storage class, and a sensible retention policy. Get those choices right, and MSP360 is a capable backup tool that can grow from one computer to a managed fleet.

Verdict: 4.2/5. MSP360 Backup offers excellent storage freedom and detailed recovery controls at a fair software price. Separate cloud billing, a more technical setup, and file-only Mac backup keep it from being the easiest recommendation for everyone.

Try MSP360 Backup

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which flagship is better?

content.rendered:
Apple has launched its next Pro model, the iPhone 18 Pro, bringing a new A20 Pro chip, camera upgrades, iOS 27, and several other improvements. But it enters a market where Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra is already one of the most feature-packed flagship phones available.

So, how does Apple’s latest Pro iPhone compare with Samsung’s Ultra flagship? I’m putting the iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra side by side to see how they compare in design, display, performance, cameras, battery life, AI features, software, and pricing and which one deserves your money.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Specs comparison

Before getting into the experience of using these phones, here’s a quick comparison.

On the surface, Samsung appears to throw more hardware at me. But I wouldn’t make a buying decision from this table alone.

Design and build quality: Which feels more premium?

The first thing I’d notice switching between these phones is the size.

The iPhone 18 Pro is the easier phone to live with physically. Its 6.3-inch display makes it considerably more manageable than Samsung’s 6.9-inch Ultra. I can see myself comfortably using it one-handed, slipping it into a pocket and forgetting I’m carrying a Pro-level phone.

Apple offers the iPhone 18 Pro in black, silver, glacier, and the new burgundy finish. Galaxy S26 Ultra comes in four colours: Cobalt Violet, Sky Blue, White, and Black, along with two online exclusives: Shadow Silver and Pink Gold.

Another thing that caught my attention is the difference in thickness and weight. The Galaxy S26 Ultra measures just 7.9mm thick and weighs 214g, while the iPhone 18 Pro is 8.75mm thick and weighs 211g. In other words, the Samsung flagship is 0.85 mm thinner, but it’s just 3 g heavier than Apple’s smaller Pro model.

When it comes to protection, both phones use premium glass. The iPhone 18 Pro uses Ceramic Shield, which Apple designed to improve durability and help protect the phone from everyday drops and scratches. As for the Samsung flagship, the back of the phone is made from Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2.

My verdict: iPhone 18 Pro for comfort. Galaxy S26 Ultra for its slimmer design and larger form factor.

Display: Is bigger really better?

The display is one of the first things I notice when switching between two flagship phones, and both Apple and Samsung have opted for premium panels here. However, they take very different approaches.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a 6.3-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate. Its compact size is actually what I like about the device. The display is brighter, and the adaptive refresh rate makes scrolling and animations feel smooth. And it’s also easier to hold while typing or handling the device with just one hand.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra, on the other hand, is the one I’d pick for watching movies, gaming, browsing, or getting work done. Its 6.9-inch QHD+ display gives me noticeably more screen space, and Samsung’s Dynamic AMOLED 2X panel delivers the kind of punchy colours and deep blacks I expect from an Ultra phone.

Samsung also has another interesting advantage: Privacy Display. It can make the screen harder for people around me to see from an angle, which could be genuinely useful when I’m checking private messages or working on sensitive information in a crowded place.

My display verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins.

Performance: A20 Pro vs Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5

This is the section where I would tell readers not to get obsessed with benchmark charts.

The iPhone 18 Pro is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro, while Samsung uses the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy.

The A20 Pro is particularly interesting because it is built using a 2nm process. It has a 6-core CPU with two new Super cores and four efficiency cores, along with a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators. Compared to the A19 Pro, the new Super cores can be up to 20% faster, while the GPU can deliver up to 40% faster graphics performance.

Apple has also given the A20 Pro a Dual 16-core Neural Engine to handle demanding on-device AI tasks and computational photography. What I find more interesting is that Apple isn’t only chasing peak performance. The iPhone 18 Pro has a new vapour-chamber cooling system to keep the A20 Pro running at high performance for longer periods.

Unlike Apple’s 6-core CPU, Snapdragon uses an octa-core CPU, with two high-performance Oryon cores and six performance cores. It is built on a 3nm process and is paired with Qualcomm’s Adreno 840 GPU.

Samsung has also tuned the chip specifically for the Galaxy S26 Ultra to deliver up to a 19% CPU performance improvement, 24% greater graphics processing and 39% faster NPU performance compared with the previous generation. I also like that Samsung gives the S26 Ultra up to 16GB of RAM,

That combination makes the S26 Ultra particularly interesting for gaming, multitasking and AI-heavy workloads.

The early benchmark results give the A20 Pro a clear lead in CPU performance.

The difference is particularly noticeable in single-core performance, where the A20 Pro is roughly 25% ahead of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy based on these results. Multi-core performance is much closer, but the iPhone still has the lead.

Which one feels faster?

I wouldn’t say one is simply “faster.”

The A20 Pro benefits from Apple’s tight control over the hardware and software stack. That matters for things such as:

  • Video editing
  • Gaming optimization
  • Camera processing
  • AI workloads
  • App performance
  • Sustained performance

My verdict: I would choose the A20 Pro for optimised performance and Apple’s ecosystem.

Camera comparison

This is where the iPhone 18 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra comparison gets really interesting.

Samsung is still playing the hardware and versatility game. Apple is taking a more computational and creator-focused approach.

The iPhone 18 Pro gets a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, which is one of the biggest camera changes Apple has made in years. The aperture can move between f/1.48 and f/4.0, giving the camera more control over light and depth of field. The phone also gets new Pro camera controls.

The system includes:

  • 48MP Fusion Main
  • 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide
  • 48MP Fusion Telephoto
  • 4x optical and up to 8x optical-quality zoom

I particularly like the variable-aperture approach because it gives the camera a physical control that smartphone photography has largely avoided.

Samsung takes the “give me everything” approach.

The S26 Ultra includes:

  • 200MP main camera
  • 50MP ultrawide
  • 10MP 3x telephoto
  • 50MP 5x telephoto
  • Digital zoom up to 100x

And this is where Samsung has the advantage for me. If I’m travelling, shooting a concert, photographing architecture from a distance, or simply want more flexibility when framing a subject, those dedicated zoom cameras matter.

The 3x and 5x telephoto cameras give me options that a single telephoto system can’t replicate as effectively. However, more megapixels do not automatically mean better photos.

  • For zoom and versatility, I’d pick the Galaxy S26 Ultra.
  • For video, I’d lean toward the iPhone 18 Pro for its Dolby Vision recording, Smart Focus Tracking, and Audio Mix.
  • For everyday photography, I’d want to compare identical real-world shots before declaring a winner because both companies process images very differently.

Battery life and charging

Samsung S26 Ultra has the obvious hardware advantage here with a 5,000mAh battery. It also supports up to 60W wired charging and reverse wireless charging, which can be useful for topping up Galaxy Buds or another compatible device.

Apple takes a different approach. Rather than competing directly on battery capacity, it combines its silicon, operating system, and battery architecture to maximise efficiency.

The iPhone 18 Pro delivers major battery-life improvements, with the A20 Pro and updated battery design working together to deliver up to 36 hours of video playback. However, Samsung lists only up to 31 hours of video playback for the S26 Ultra.

My verdict: If I’m gaming for hours, navigating with GPS, recording lots of video and streaming content, I’d be more comfortable choosing the iPhone 18 Pro.

Software and ecosystem: iOS 27 vs One UI

When you are buying a $1,200-plus smartphone, you are often buying into an ecosystem, not just buying a phone.

The iPhone 18 Pro ships with iOS 27, which brings the new generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. One feature I find particularly interesting is Siri mode in the Camera app. I can point the camera at something, ask Siri about what I’m seeing, and get information or take an action based on it.

But for me, Apple’s biggest advantage remains the ecosystem.

If you already own:

  • MacBook
  • iPad
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods
  • Apple TV

Then an iPhone is just a more intuitive and sensible choice. AirDrop, Handoff, iCloud, Messages, FaceTime, and cross-device continuity create an experience that’s difficult for Samsung to duplicate. This is the very reason why I would recommend this device to existing Apple users.

Samsung takes the opposite approach. One UI is designed for people who want more control.

I can:

  • Customise the interface
  • Run multiple apps in split-screen
  • Use Samsung DeX
  • Take handwritten notes with S Pen
  • Share images directly with contacts using Quick Share.
  • Customise more aspects of the phone
  • Broadcast audio or even my voice to compatible nearby LE Audio devices using Auracast

Samsung has also committed to seven years of OS and security updates for the Galaxy S26 series.

My verdict: iOS 27 wins for simplicity and ecosystem integration. One UI wins for customisation and power users.

AI features: Apple Intelligence vs Galaxy AI

AI has become one of the biggest selling points of flagship phones, but I think this is one area where buyers should be careful. I don’t care how many AI features appear in a launch presentation. I care whether I actually use them.

Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence, including a new Siri AI designed to understand personal context, recognise what’s on screen and perform actions across apps. Apple is also emphasising privacy through on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute.

Other meaningful additions include:

  • Dedicated Siri app: Revisit previous Siri conversations and continue them across Apple devices using iCloud.
  • Write with Siri: Describe what you want to write and have Siri create or refine a draft.
  • New AI photo editing: Spatial Reframing, Extend, and an upgraded Clean Up tool give me more ways to edit photos after taking them.
  • Image Playground improvements: Create more realistic AI-generated images.

Samsung’s Galaxy AI is more aggressively integrated into the phone’s everyday workflows.

The S26 Ultra brings the new Bixby as a more conversational device agent. Instead of remembering the exact name of a setting, I can describe what I want in normal language, and Bixby can identify the appropriate setting or action. It can also search the web for up-to-date information directly within Bixby.

Also, Photo Assist lets you make multiple AI-powered photo edits without saving each version individually; you can then review the editing history and choose which versions to keep.

Samsung is also leaning heavily into AI-powered productivity and cross-app actions and integrating services such as Gemini and Perplexity. And that’s where I give Samsung the edge.

My verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins for breadth and practical AI tools.

Connectivity and extra features

At this price, both phones have everything I expect from a modern flagship.

Both offer:

  • 5G
  • Wi-Fi 7
  • Bluetooth
  • NFC
  • USB-C
  • UWB

But the extras are where Samsung starts pulling away.

The S26 Ultra gives me:

  • S Pen
  • Samsung DeX
  • Privacy Display
  • Reverse wireless charging
  • Ultrasonic fingerprint scanner
  • Extensive multitasking
  • Android customization

The S Pen is still one of Samsung’s biggest differentiators. This allows me to take down my handwritten notes, edit my photos, annotate documents, and navigate precisely. I don’t have to buy a separate accessory and remember to carry it.

Apple’s biggest extras are ecosystem-related:

  • Face ID
  • MagSafe
  • AirDrop
  • Apple Watch integration
  • Mac continuity
  • Advanced camera controls
  • LiDAR
  • Apple’s satellite and emergency features where supported

So I see the difference this way: Samsung gives me more features on the phone itself, whereas Apple gives me a better-connected collection of devices.

My verdict: Galaxy S26 Ultra wins for individual features. iPhone wins if I already live inside Apple’s ecosystem.

Price and value for money

The iPhone 18 Pro begins at $1,199 for 256 GB in the US. Apple also provides promotional offers from eligible carriers, trade-in credits, and its Apple Upgrade leasing option. Eligible carrier deals can provide up to $1,200 in credits for certain iPhone 14 or newer trade-ins, depending on eligibility.

Samsung’s regular U.S. pricing starts at $1,299.99 for the 256GB Galaxy S26 Ultra, with 512GB and 1TB versions going higher. Samsung is also advertising trade-in incentives.

The iPhone 18 Pro is cheaper at standard pricing. But the Galaxy S26 Ultra becomes compelling once discounts are applied.

iPhone 18 Pro vs Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which one should you buy?

After looking at the two phones category by category, I don’t think there is a universal winner. And that’s actually a good thing. These phones are aimed at slightly different people.

I’d buy the iPhone 18 Pro if I:

  • Already own a MacBook or iPad.
  • Wear an Apple Watch or use AirPods.
  • Want a smaller flagship.
  • Care heavily about video recording.
  • Prefer iOS.
  • Want the new variable-aperture camera.
  • Want up to 2TB of storage.
  • Don’t need a built-in stylus.

The iPhone 18 Pro is the phone I’d recommend to someone who says, “I want a Pro iPhone, but I don’t want a giant phone.” That’s where Apple’s strategy makes perfect sense.

You should buy the Galaxy S26 Ultra if you:

  • Want the biggest display possible.
  • Take lots of zoom photos.
  • Want the S Pen.
  • Multitask heavily and want Samsung DeX.
  • Like Android customisation.
  • Want a large battery.
  • Use a Windows PC more than a Mac.
  • Want Samsung’s broader AI toolkit.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra is the phone I’d recommend to someone who wants a powerhouse.

My final verdict

If I had to spend my own money today, I’d pick the Galaxy S26 Ultra as the better overall flagship. It gives me a larger and more versatile display, more flexible camera hardware, S Pen, stronger productivity features, a large battery, and an extensive set of AI tools.

But I wouldn’t call the iPhone 18 Pro a worse phone. I’d call it the better choice for a specific kind of buyer.

If you already owned a MacBook, Apple Watch, and AirPods, the iPhone 18 Pro would be my pick. The ecosystem advantage is too significant to ignore. Buy the iPhone 18 Pro if you want a compact Pro iPhone, excellent video capabilities, and seamless Apple ecosystem integration.

The most important takeaway from this comparison: the best flagship isn’t necessarily the phone with the most impressive spec sheet. It’s the phone that fits the way I already live.

title.rendered: Apple Car Key code hints at support for Lincoln, Freelander, and Lucid

content.rendered:
Apple may be preparing to expand Car Key support to Lincoln, Freelander, and Lucid. Aaron Perris spotted the three automakers in Apple’s backend code, but the discovery does not include a release date, compatible vehicle list, or confirmation from Apple.

It is also not a first-time support announcement for every brand. Apple’s current public vehicle list already shows Car Key support for certain Lincoln and Lucid models, while Freelander does not appear on the list. The code may point to additional models, markets, or a staged rollout.

What the code discovery shows

The names appeared in a September 15 post from Aaron Perris. Similar backend references have preceded other Car Key additions, but code alone cannot tell us when a feature will launch or which vehicles will support it.

The discovery follows earlier references to GWM Tank and Haval. Our previous report on Volkswagen’s planned Apple Wallet car key support explains why these backend findings can be useful clues while still falling short of an announcement.

Apple’s public compatibility list currently marks selected Lincoln vehicles and Lucid entries as supporting car keys. Freelander is not listed there. That leaves several possibilities: Apple could be preparing more models from an already supported brand, adding support in another market, or getting the backend ready before an official rollout.

How Apple Car Key works

Car Key lives in the Wallet app. With a compatible vehicle, an iPhone or Apple Watch can lock, unlock, and start the car. Depending on the automaker and model, it can also support passive entry, remote locking, trunk controls, or sharing a key with another person.

Apple says setup usually begins in the automaker’s app, an email, or the vehicle’s display. After the key is added to Wallet, Express Mode may let you use it without opening the app or authenticating every time. The exact behavior depends on the vehicle.

Apple Support lists an iPhone XS or later, or an iPhone SE (2nd generation) or later, and a compatible Apple Watch as the usual device requirements. The phone and watch need to be signed in to the Apple Account associated with the key. Apple also says some functions vary by region and manufacturer, so a supported brand does not automatically mean every trim supports every feature.

When could the new support arrive?

There is no confirmed launch date for Lincoln, Freelander, or Lucid based on this code discovery. Apple and the automakers would still need to announce supported vehicles and make the feature available through software, vehicle systems, or an automaker app.

For now, owners should check Apple’s available vehicle list and the automaker’s instructions rather than assuming a particular car will work. The backend references are a sign that more Car Key support may be on the way, not a promise that it is ready to use.

For a broader look at Apple’s Wallet updates, see our guide to new iOS 26 Wallet app features.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, not anymore. However, till September 19, the Lucy skin could have been unlocked by ranking high in the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Cup in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Besides Lucy, which other Cyberpunk characters are there in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apart from Lucy, you have a choice among V, Johnny Silverhand, and Adam Smasher.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Fortnite bundle that contains both Cyberpunk 2077 and Cyberpunk Edgerunners characters?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of now, no such combined bundles exist. There is the Night City Denizens Bundle, which features Cyberpunk 2077-inspired characters exclusively (minus Adam Smasher), whereas the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Bundle only packs items inspired by the namesake series.

title.rendered: Apple explains how iPhone 18 Pro’s Reference Image mode verifies photos

content.rendered:
Apple has explained the security system behind Apple Reference Image, an opt-in camera mode on iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. It is designed to preserve evidence of the pixels the camera sensor captured, even as synthetic and edited images become harder to distinguish from originals.

Reference Image can help verify a photo’s capture history. It cannot prove that the scene itself was real or that the subject in front of the camera was genuine.

The camera signs the pixels immediately

In a technical post from Apple’s Security Research team, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro’s main camera sensor boots into a specialized Reference Image mode. The sensor cryptographically signs the pixel data immediately after capture and prevents firmware from changing it first.

The sensor metadata is signed too. The Secure Enclave Processor adds its own signature to device-generated information, such as the focal length and the boundaries used for digital zoom. Together, those records form a protected digital negative containing the pixels, sensor details, and secure timestamp bounds.

Apple’s timestamp system is designed to show when the image could have been captured. The device receives a cryptographic timestamp token through an Apple Push Notification service heartbeat, then asks for another token after taking the photo. Apple says the heartbeat averages about every 15 minutes, though network conditions can change that interval.

Private Cloud Compute develops the reference image

The signed digital negative is sent to Private Cloud Compute for steps such as demosaicing, tone mapping, and compression. Apple says the service can be verified through device attestation and an append-only log, while the system is designed to keep the image data private.

Apple says the final signature combines RSA-3072 with ML-DSA-87, a post-quantum signature algorithm. That technical combination matters less to most people than the result: the finished Reference Image is tied to signed sensor data instead of being an ordinary image file that can be silently changed after capture.

In Photos, the reference version appears alongside the regular photo. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro announcement says developers can also work with the format through APIs on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27.

What Reference Image can and cannot prove

The mode can help answer whether the pixels came from a compatible iPhone sensor and whether the signed capture data has been altered. It can also expose edits that break the provenance record.

It does not establish that the scene was truthful. If you photograph an AI-generated image on another screen, Reference Image can show that your iPhone sensor captured those pixels. It cannot tell you whether the face, document, or event shown on that screen was authentic.

That distinction is important. The feature is closer to a signed digital negative than a truth detector. For ordinary photos, our guide on how to get photo metadata on an iPhone explains what information a photo can carry and how to inspect it.

How to turn it on

Reference Image is opt-in and works through the iPhone 18 Pro main camera. Apple Support lists these steps:

  1. Open Settings and tap Camera.
  2. Tap Reference Image, then Add Reference Mode.
  3. Open Camera and swipe to Reference.
  4. Take the photo.

The mode is not available in every region. Apple says capture is unavailable in the European Union and China at launch, although people in the EU can still develop and view reference images on supported Apple devices. Check Apple’s current Reference Image instructions if the setting does not appear.

For more camera and hardware context, see our iPhone 18 Pro guide. Reference Image is a useful provenance feature, but its strongest claim is narrow: it helps show what the sensor captured, not whether the world looked exactly as the image suggests.

title.rendered: Apple’s M6 and M5 Ultra benchmark scores hint at fast new Macs

content.rendered:
Fresh Geekbench 7 results offer an early look at the Apple M6 and M5 Ultra chips headed for the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. The M6 result is stronger in single-core work, while the M5 Ultra result is more than twice as fast in multi-core work.

These are individual public benchmark uploads, not Apple-confirmed retail tests. They are useful for setting expectations, but they do not tell us how either chip will perform in sustained workloads or everyday apps.

M6 beats M5 Ultra in single-core

The Apple M6 Geekbench 7 result shows 4,071 in single-core and 22,783 in multi-core. Geekbench identifies the machine as Mac18,5 with a 12-core chip and 32GB of memory.

The M5 Ultra result shows 3,774 in single-core and 52,516 in multi-core. The record identifies a Mac17,15 with a 36-core chip and 256GB of memory.

The M6 score is about 8% higher in single-core. That kind of result can point to quicker response in lightly threaded tasks, such as opening apps or handling short bursts of work. The M5 Ultra’s multi-core score is about 2.3 times higher, which is the more relevant number for heavily parallel tasks such as large video exports, 3D rendering, and some AI workloads.

The comparison is not a fair contest between equal machines. M6 is a mainstream desktop chip for the Mac mini, while M5 Ultra is a workstation-class part designed for the Mac Studio. The large difference in CPU core count explains much of the multi-core gap.

What Apple has announced

Apple says M6 is the first Apple silicon chip built using a second-generation 2-nanometer process. It has up to a 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. Apple says M5 Ultra scales to 36 CPU cores, 80 GPU cores, and up to 512GB of unified memory.

The new Mac mini and Mac Studio are scheduled to become available on September 22. If you are weighing the two products, our M6 Mac mini vs M5 Ultra Mac Studio comparison breaks down the more important differences, including size, memory, ports, and intended workloads.

The benchmark records do not show GPU scores, so they cannot tell us whether the M6 Mac mini is a better choice for graphics work or how the M5 Ultra handles demanding visual tasks. Apple’s launch claims also use different comparison points and workloads, so they should not be mixed with these Geekbench numbers as if they were one test.

Wait for independent testing before buying

Geekbench measures a short CPU workload. A public upload can show the performance of one pre-release or early system, but it cannot settle questions about fan noise, sustained speed, power use, thermals, storage, or app compatibility. It also does not show how the Mac mini and Mac Studio feel in normal use.

For now, the numbers suggest a simple split. M6 may offer excellent quick, single-core performance in a compact Mac mini. M5 Ultra is in another class when an application can use many CPU cores at once. The history of Mac processors puts that generational jump in a broader context.

The new Macs arrive September 22. Anyone buying on day one should wait for retail reviews if sustained performance, graphics, or thermals matter more than a single Geekbench result.
