title.rendered: Apple may bring back dedicated Genius Bars in major Apple Store revamp

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly preparing a broad redesign of its retail stores, including dedicated Genius Bars, new spaces for online order pickup and Today at Apple, and the removal of large video walls. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman outlined the plans in his September 13 Power On newsletter. Apple has not confirmed the changes, so the details and rollout timing remain unconfirmed.

What Apple reportedly plans

Gurman says Apple wants to accelerate store renovations over the coming years. The changes would center on the "Avenues," the sections along the sides of newer stores where Apple displays accessories and services.

The report says Apple would add two 10-foot "bays" for tasks that are usually spread across the store:

  • An online pickup bay with an all-wood build, secure drawers for orders, a subtle Apple logo, and a front table for employee handoffs.
  • A Today at Apple bay with a large display and secure drawers for instructors’ devices.

Apple could trade video walls for Genius Bars

Apple also reportedly plans to remove the giant video walls at the back of many stores. Those screens currently support Today at Apple sessions and marketing. In the planned layout, many of those spaces would become dedicated Genius Bars.

The reported bar design uses wood, two counter heights for accessibility, storage drawers, and large product posters. That would reverse part of the store concept Apple rolled out in 2016. In its official Union Square announcement, Apple described a tree-filled Genius Grove for support and a Forum built around a 6K video wall for Today at Apple.

Apple still lists those services

Apple’s current retail page still lists online order pickup, Genius Bar support, and Today at Apple sessions. The report is about moving and redesigning those functions, not ending them. If you need support now, this guide explains how to make a Genius Bar appointment.

For now, there is no official timeline, store list, or Apple confirmation for the reported changes.

title.rendered: Apple may launch two iPhone game controllers under the Beats brand

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly working on game controllers for the iPhone, with Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman saying the accessories may be released under the Beats brand. The report adds a useful detail to code references found in macOS 26.7 earlier this month, but Apple has not announced a controller.

Gurman says Beats executives are leading the project. The reported goal is to compete with the third-party gamepads already available for the iPhone, including products from Backbone, Razer, and SteelSeries.

macOS code points to two controller profiles

The code trail began with a September 4 MacRumors forum post from pdfu, who found two Game Controller profiles in the first macOS 26.7 release candidate. They use the identifiers T6502 and T1057.

Both profiles look like what Apple calls an extended gamepad. That means a familiar layout with face buttons, a D-pad, two clickable thumbsticks, shoulder buttons, analog triggers, Home, and Menu controls. Apple’s extended gamepad documentation describes the same basic profile for physical and virtual controllers.

The two profiles differ in a few useful ways:

  • T6502 is listed with Apple USB connectivity, an Options button, and no exposed motion input. Its haptic system is split between the left and right handles.
  • T1057 is listed with Apple USB, Apple Bluetooth, and Beats USB identifiers. It adds an accelerometer and gyroscope, while its haptic system uses one whole-controller actuator and drops the Options button.

The Beats USB identifier may help explain why Gurman’s report points to a Beats-branded product. It still does not prove that T1057 is a finished Beats controller. The recovered profiles were removed from the second macOS 26.7 release candidate, which leaves open the possibility that they describe test hardware or a project Apple has changed.

Apple already supports plenty of controllers

Apple would be entering a crowded market. iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV users can already pair Xbox, PlayStation, and third-party controllers, as Apple’s Game Controller documentation explains. The best game controllers for iPhone and Apple TV guide shows how many options are already available, from full-size Bluetooth pads to controllers that hold the iPhone between two grips.

That makes the Beats angle plausible, but it also raises the obvious question: what would make Apple’s controller worth buying? The code mentions standard buttons, motion input, and haptics. It says nothing about a new form factor, special iPhone features, price, or a release window.

The timing fits Apple’s wider push to make gaming easier to find and use across its devices, but the code does not reveal how Apple would distinguish its hardware from existing options.

There is no launch date yet

For now, this is a report about a product in development, backed by code that appeared briefly in a macOS beta. Apple has not confirmed the controllers, Beats branding, pricing, or release timing. Until that changes, T6502 and T1057 are clues, not products you can pre-order.

excerpt.rendered: Bloomberg reports Apple is working on iPhone game controllers that may carry the Beats brand. macOS code points to two models, but no launch is confirmed.

Update: Verified the latest Build a Blue Lock Squad Codes on October 12, 2026

If you’re trying to build a strong starting eleven, Build a Blue Lock Squad makes you roll for Blue Lock characters and improve weak slots one pull at a time. The game has more than 200 characters, so rerolls and refreshes disappear quickly when you’re chasing a specific striker. These codes give you free rerolls, refreshes, coins, and cash before you spend your own resources. Redeem the newest ones first, then test the unverified strings only if you want to take a chance on an older reward.

How to redeem Build a Blue Lock Squad codes

Join The LockerRoom Roblox community before entering a code. If you join after launching the game, rejoin a fresh server so the membership can register.

  1. Launch Build a Blue Lock Squad on Roblox.
  2. Finish the opening tutorial if the game prompts you.
  3. Click the Settings button in the lower-left corner.
  4. Paste a code into the Enter Code box.
  5. Click Redeem and check that the reward total changes.

Why your code may not work

  • You have not joined The LockerRoom community.
  • You changed the capitalization or added an extra space.
  • You already redeemed the code on that account.
  • The code expired or was replaced by a newer update batch.
  • You are in an old server. Leave and join a fresh one after an update.

Copy and paste each code exactly as shown. If the active list fails after those checks, test one code at a time so you can tell whether the issue is the code or the server.

Where to find more Build a Blue Lock Squad codes

New codes usually appear with updates, fixes, and community milestones. Check the Build a Blue Lock Squad Roblox page and The LockerRoom community for game-side notices, then watch the Build a Blue Lock Squad Discord server for faster announcements.

Bookmarking this list is easier than keeping a pile of old code strings in your notes. If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Roblox Pressure codes, Giant Simulator Reborn codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

title.rendered: Buying an iPhone in 2026: Which iPhone should you buy?

content.rendered:
Are you planning to buy a new iPhone but can’t decide which one? I get it! The 2026 iPhone lineup is more interesting than ever, which makes choosing the right model harder. You now have the powerful iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple’s first foldable iPhone Duo, the mainstream iPhone 17, and more affordable options like the iPhone 17e.

To cut through the hype and help you pick the right iPhone for your needs. In this guide, I’ll break down the best iPhone to buy in 2026, from the most powerful flagship to the best foldable, best value option, and the model worth buying if you simply want a thin and lightweight phone.

Table of Contents
  • What is the Best iPhone in 2026?
  • Best Overall: iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Best Foldable: iPhone Duo
    • Best for Most People: iPhone 17
    • Best Budget-Friendly: iPhone 17e
    • Best for Beginners: iPhone 16
    • Experience the Thinnest Smartphone with iPhone Air
  • Which iPhone Should You Buy?
  • Which iPhone Is Not Recommended?
  • Factors to Consider When Buying an iPhone
  • How We Evaluate iPhone Models
  • Signing off…

What is the Best iPhone in 2026? 

The best iPhone depends on what you prioritize, whether it’s performance, affordability, camera quality, portability, or a foldable design. Based on the latest 2026 lineup, here’s a quick list of my top picks:

  • Most powerful: iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Special highlight: iPhone Duo
  • Best for most people: iPhone 17
  • Best budget-friendly: iPhone 17e
  • Best for beginners/value: iPhone 16
  • For thinness lovers: iPhone Air

Apple has now pushed the iPhone into a new generation with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup while also entering the foldable market with iPhone Duo.

Let’s examine each iPhone model’s features so you can match them to your requirements. I’ll also share my verdict at the end. To your requirements. We will also share our verdict at the end; therefore, keep reading! 

Best Overall: iPhone 18 Pro Max 

Key specs

  • Display: 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display with ProMotion and Always-On display.
  • Processor: A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, and new Neural Accelerators.
  • Cameras: Advanced 48MP Fusion camera system with a new variable-aperture Main camera and Pro camera controls.
  • Battery: Up to 45 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models.
  • Storage & Price: Starts at 256GB for $1,299; available up to 2TB.
  • Colors: Black, Silver, Glacier, and Burgundy.
  • Other Goodies: Next-generation vapor chamber, N1 networking chip, C2 modem, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, and iOS 27.

If you want the most powerful traditional iPhone Apple currently makes, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is my clear pick.

The A20 Pro is built on a 2nm process and includes a new 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. The GPU can be up to 40% faster than the A19 Pro, while the chip has 50% more memory bandwidth. Apple has also improved sustained performance with a redesigned vapor chamber.

The camera system is an even bigger reason to choose the 18 Pro Max over the 17 Pro Max. Its 48MP Fusion Main camera now has a variable aperture, giving you control over depth of field and the amount of light entering the lens. You can manually adjust aperture, shutter speed, and white balance using the new Pro controls.

Battery life is another major advantage. The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, making it the longest-lasting iPhone in Apple’s current lineup. I also like the updated Dynamic Island, which can now display up to three Live Activities simultaneously.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max also comes with iOS 27 and the next generation of Apple Intelligence, including the new Siri AI experience. Siri can understand personal context, use onscreen awareness, and interact with what you’re doing on your iPhone.

The downside? The 18 Pro Max is still a large and expensive phone. Starting at $1,299, it is not the obvious choice for casual users. It is also heavy at 249 grams, so anyone who prefers a smaller phone should consider the iPhone 18 Pro instead.

Pros

  • Best overall performance in an iPhone 
  • A20 Pro delivers major performance and AI improvements 
  • Advanced 48MP camera system with variable aperture 
  • Excellent sustained performance with the redesigned vapor chamber 
  • Up to 45 hours of video playback 
  • Large 6.9-inch ProMotion display 
  • Up to 2TB storage 
  • Excellent choice for creators and power users 

Cons

  • Expensive, especially at higher storage tiers 
  • Large and heavy for one-handed use 
  • Overkill for casual users 
  • Some advanced camera features may not matter to everyday users 

Tip: If you want similar Pro-level performance in a smaller body, consider the iPhone 18 Pro instead. 

Best Foldable: iPhone Duo 

Key specs

  • Display: 7.6-inch inner foldable Super Retina XDR OLED display and 5.4-inch outer display.
  • Processor: A20 Pro chip.
  • Cameras: Dual 48MP rear camera system.
  • Battery: Dual-cell battery design with fast charging.
  • Storage & Price: Starts at 256GB for $1,999; available up to 2TB.
  • Colors: Night Sky and Star White.
  • Other Goodies: Titanium foldable design, Ceramic Shield 2, ProMotion up to 120Hz, Dynamic Island, Apple Pencil support, and iOS 27 optimized for the foldable form factor.

The biggest change to Apple’s iPhone lineup in 2026 isn’t just a faster processor or a better camera. It’s the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable iPhone.

When opened, its 7.6-inch display gives you a much larger canvas for watching videos, reading, gaming, and multitasking. When closed, you get a compact 5.4-inch outer display. Both support ProMotion, Always-On display, HDR, and Dynamic Island. The inner display also has a nano-texture finish designed to reduce glare.

I liked how Apple has adapted iOS 27 for the foldable design. Apps and content can respond as the device folds and unfolds, while the interface has been redesigned to make better use of the larger inner screen. Apple also supports split-screen multitasking and has optimized its own apps for the new form factor.

The Duo is powered by the same A20 Pro family used in the 18 Pro models, so you’re not sacrificing flagship-level performance simply because you’re choosing a foldable. It also supports up to 2TB of storage.

I wouldn’t recommend Duo to everyone, though. At $1,999, it is dramatically more expensive than the traditional iPhone models. At 254 grams, it is also heavier than the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

So, who should buy it? I’d recommend it primarily to people who genuinely want a foldable and will take advantage of the additional screen space. If you’re mainly looking for the fastest iPhone, the 18 Pro Max remains the better value.

Pros

  • Apple’s first foldable iPhone 
  • Huge 7.6-inch inner display 
  • Compact 5.4-inch outer display when folded 
  • A20 Pro performance 
  • ProMotion on both displays 
  • Excellent multitasking potential 
  • Apple Pencil support 
  • Up to 2TB storage 
  • iOS 27 is specifically optimized for the foldable form factor 

Cons

  • Starts at $1,999 
  • Heavier than the traditional Pro Max 
  • More expensive than any other iPhone 
  • Foldable design may be unnecessary for casual users 
  • Availability begins later than the iPhone 18 Pro lineup 

Tip: Choose iPhone Duo if the foldable experience itself is your priority. If you simply want the fastest, longest-lasting and most capable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is still the better choice. 

Best for Most People: iPhone 17

Key specs 

  • Display: 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR with 120Hz ProMotion Always-On display 
  • Processor: A19 chip with 8GB RAM. 
  • Cameras: 48MP Dual Fusion main + 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, 18MP Center Stage front cam. 
  • Battery: Up to 30 hours of video playback, fast charging with a 40W Dynamic adapter. 
  • Storage & Price: 256GB base for $899; 512GB option. 
  • Colors: Black, White, Mist Blue, Sage, Lavender 
  • Other Goodies: Ceramic Shield 2, 3000 nits peak brightness outdoors, GPU with Neural Accelerators. 

For the 80% of us who want flagship vibes without breaking the bank, the iPhone 17 is the sweet spot. It’s got that just-right size (6.3 inches) for one-handed scrolling, longer battery life, and includes many of the Pro features. When compared to the iPhone 16, you’ll notice smoother scrolling thanks to the ProMotion display with an adaptive refresh rate up to 120Hz. 

Moreover, the 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide lets you take better photos, and the camera system offers the new Dual Capture mode and landscape selfies. The front camera now also supports ultra-stabilized videos. Therefore, unless you’re shooting professional-grade video or want a bigger display, the iPhone 17 gives you nearly all the good bits with fewer compromises.

Pros

  • Great all-around performance and camera quality 
  • More pocket-friendly size and lighter weight 
  • Price is more reasonable than Pro Max
  • New ProMotion display and double storage sweeten the deal 

Cons

  • Lacks some of the zoom power and video features found in Pro Max 
  • Battery life is strong but not top-tier
  • No telephoto lens with actual optical zoom (only cropping) 

Best Budget-Friendly: iPhone 17e

Key specs 

  • Display: 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED 
  • Processor: A19 chip with 8GB RAM 
  • Cameras: Single 48MP Fusion main, 12MP TrueDepth front camera. 
  • Battery: Up to 26 hours of video playback. MagSafe & Qi2 wireless charging up to 15W. 
  • Colors: White, Black, Soft Pink 
  • Storage & Price: $699 for the 256GB base variant, up to 512GB. 
  • Other Goodies: 169g weight, USB-C fast charging, Ceramic Shield 2 glass, and Satellite features. 

If you’re looking for a value-for-money iPhone that delivers a premium Apple experience on a budget, the iPhone 17e is the perfect choice. It brings A19 chip, Apple Intelligence support, IP68 water resistance 48MP Fusion camera with 2x optical Telephoto and next-generation portraits, MagSafe charging, Apple’s C1X 5G modem, and much more.

Therefore, you will get many of the iPhone 17 features at a more affordable price. However, to keep costs down, Apple sticks with a 60Hz display, a single rear camera, and the older notch design instead of Dynamic Island. You will also miss out on the Camera Control button, ProMotion display, high-speed charging, and several camera functions.

In my view, if you’ve been holding out for an iPhone that’s budget-friendly but still powerful, the iPhone 17e is a no-brainer. It’s a step up from older SE models, with better performance, a good camera, and a sleek design, all without the premium price tag.

Pros

  • Affordable way to get flagship-level Apple features and performance
  • Compact and lightweight 
  • 48MP camera captures detailed photos and supports optical-quality 2× zoom.
  • MagSafe support enables convenient wireless charging and accessories.
  • 256GB base storage, double the previous generation.

Cons

  • 60Hz display feels outdated
  • Single rear camera, lacking ultra-wide or telephoto lenses.
  • Older notch design instead of Dynamic Island.
  • Charging speeds still relatively slow compared with many Android rivals.

Best for Beginners: iPhone 16

Key Specs

  • Display: 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR
  • Processor: A18 chip with 8GB RAM
  • Cameras: 48MP main + 12MP ultra-wide, 12MP TrueDepth front
  • Battery: Up to 22 hours of video playback
  • Colors: Ultramarine, Teal, Pink, White, Black
  • Storage & Price: 128GB base for $799. 
  • Other goodies: Camera Control and Action button, Advanced Apple Intelligence

New to iPhones or just want something straightforward and future-proof? The iPhone 16 (last year’s standard, now on sale) is your best bet. It offers a balance between high-end features and a reasonable price. The display is 6.1 inches with 2000 nits peak brightness, which can drop to 1 nit. So, you can enjoy your content in any lighting conditions.

Apple has incorporated the A18 Bionic chip made exclusively for Apple Intelligence. In terms of the camera, the 48MP Fusion primary sensor can capture high-quality images, and the 2x optical-quality Telephoto allows for zooming in. Moreover, it’s Apple’s first modern iPhone with vertical alignment to support Spatial photo and video for Vision Pro.

I personally love the iPhone 16 for its standout color options that set it apart from the latest iPhone models. However, next to the latest iPhone 17, its 60Hz display looks outdated. Also, the battery life and charging are mid. Conclusively, if you want a premium experience without splurging, the iPhone 16 is a fantastic choice.

Pros

  • Affordable entry 
  • Will continue to get updates for 6 years 
  • Solid rear camera 

Cons

  • No ProMotion and Always-On display 
  • Smaller storage in the base variant 
  • Lesser battery life 
  • No telephoto lens 

Experience the Thinnest Smartphone with iPhone Air

Key Specs 

  • Display: 6.5-inch Super Retina XDR with ProMotion display 
  • Processor: A19 Pro chip with 8GB RAM 
  • Cameras: 48MP fusion main (four-lens equivalent), 18MP Center Stage front camera with Pro features 
  • Battery: 3,149mAh, giving up to 27 hours of video playback. 
  • Colors: Sky Blue, Light Gold, Cloud White, Space Black  
  • Storage & Price: $1,099 for the 256GB variant, up to 1TB. 
  • Other Goodies: Only 165g weight, Titanium frame, N1 and C1X chip, eSIM-only. 

Okay, confession: I’m obsessed with slim gadgets, and the iPhone Air is the wafer-thin wonder I’ve been waiting for. At just 5.6mm thick, it packs all premium Apple features, ideal for minimalists who hate bulk. 

The iPhone Air is primarily designed for individuals who value portability and sleekness. It’s super thin, easy to slip into a pocket or small purse, and feels super lightweight in the hand. You still get the latest A19 Pro chip, ProMotion display with anti-reflective coating, a 48MP high-quality camera, and advanced iOS features, all wrapped in a compact form. 

That said, the trade-offs include a smaller battery (so shorter usage time), and the device is less suited for heavy gaming or prolonged camera/video use. Additionally, the eSIM-only design may complicate matters for individuals in regions that still heavily rely on physical SIM cards. Also, consider using a good case if you are always on the go.

Pros

  • Ultra-thin, lightweight, and very portable 
  • A19 Pro chip in a slim body, nice display and camera 
  • Stylish design and sleek feel 
  • Good for casual everyday use and portability 

Cons

  • A smaller battery means less runtime 
  • eSIM-only can be limiting in some regions
  • Not built for heavy video recording or extended gaming sessions 

Which iPhone Should You Buy? 

Still torn? Here’s my quick comparison table to match your needs. Prices are starting points and can vary by region. 

If I had to recommend just one iPhone for maximum capability, I’d choose the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It combines the strongest performance, most advanced traditional iPhone camera system, excellent battery life, and the largest display in the conventional iPhone lineup.

However, if you specifically want a foldable, the iPhone Duo is now the obvious choice because it is Apple’s first foldable iPhone and introduces a completely different way to use iOS.

For most people, I would still pick the iPhone 17 because it offers the best balance between price and features. Budget buyers should look at the 17e, while the iPhone Air is ideal if thinness and portability matter more than maximum performance. 

Which iPhone Is Not Recommended?

As new iPhone models are released every year, older models can quickly become outdated. So, some devices become less advisable for purchase or continued use. In 2026, several iPhone models are not recommended for various reasons, including a lack of software support, performance limitations, and overall value. Here’s the list: 

  • iPhone 13 or older 
  • iPhone SE (3rd Generation and older) 
  • iPhone X and XR 
  • iPhone 14 is okay for basics 

If you are drawn to buying an iPhone model due to its price tag, consider the refurbished iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max for access to Apple’s Intelligence features. 

Factors to Consider When Buying an iPhone

When choosing the right iPhone for you, several factors should come into play. 

  • Price and budget: Set a budget before shopping. The difference between a standard iPhone and the iPhone Duo can be enormous, so decide whether you actually need the premium features.
  • Performance needs: If you are a gamer, vlogger, or multitasker, then the A20 Pro powered iPhone 18 Pro Max/Duo is definitely the way to go. For everyday use, the A19-powered iPhone 17 is more than enough.
  • Camera quality: If photography and video are your priority, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the strongest choice. Its 48MP Fusion Main camera introduces variable aperture and advanced Pro controls.
  • Display size: Think about how you consume content. The 18 Pro Max gives you a large 6.9-inch display, while Duo goes much further with its 7.6-inch inner screen.
  • Foldable design: If you want a phone that can double as a larger screen for multitasking and media consumption, iPhone Duo is the model to consider.
  • Battery life: The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, making it the best option for users who prioritize battery life.
  • Storage capacity: If you record lots of 4K video or store large libraries locally, consider 1TB or 2TB. The 18 Pro Max and Duo both go up to 2TB.
  • Future-proofing: If you plan to keep your phone for several years, buying a newer generation generally gives you the longest runway for new features and software updates.
  • Operating system compatibility: Make sure your chosen model supports the current version of iOS and the Apple Intelligence features you want to use.

How We Evaluate iPhone Models

We carry out rigorous tests in order to offer an accurate and comprehensive guide. It examines numerous areas, such as performance, usability, and other functional attributes. The following gives us more detailed information about the testing process we have adopted: 

  • Performance testing: Each iPhone model’s general speed and responsiveness were evaluated using Geekbench or AnTuTu benchmark tools, among others. These tests measure CPU and GPU performance under varying workloads such as gaming, multitasking or launching applications. In addition, several apps were launched simultaneously during the real-life assessments to evaluate the device’s effectiveness in supporting day-to-day activities. 
  • Camera quality assessment: Our camera testing involves taking photos and videos in different lighting conditions (low light, daylight, and artificial light) to analyze image quality, color accuracy, and dynamic range. We compare the camera performance across different models, focusing on features like Night mode, Portrait mode, and video stabilization. We also assess the front-facing camera for selfies and video calls. 
  • Battery life evaluation: We conduct battery life tests by using the iPhone in various scenarios, such as video playback, web browsing, and gaming. We monitor how long the battery lasts under typical usage conditions and how quickly it charges with the included charger and wireless charging options. Additionally, we evaluate battery health over time to determine how well the device retains its capacity. 
  • Display quality analysis: We evaluate the display quality by measuring brightness, color accuracy, and viewing angles. This includes using tools to assess peak brightness levels and color reproduction. We also perform subjective assessments by comparing how the display looks in different lighting conditions and how it performs during media consumption, such as watching videos or playing games. 
  • User experience testing: We assess the overall user experience by evaluating the iOS interface, ease of navigation, and accessibility features. This includes testing the responsiveness of touch gestures, the effectiveness of Face ID or Touch ID, and the overall fluidity of the operating system. We also consider the quality of built-in apps and features, such as Siri, Apple Maps, and iMessage. 
  • Durability testing: We assess water and dust resistance based on the IP rating of the device. This helps determine how well the iPhone can withstand everyday wear and tear. 
  • Audio quality assessment: We test the audio quality of the iPhone’s speakers and microphones by playing music, making calls, and recording audio. We evaluate clarity, volume, and bass response, as well as how well the microphones pick up sound in different environments. 
  • Connectivity testing: We evaluate the performance of cellular connectivity, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. This includes testing call quality, data speeds, and connection stability in various environments. We also assess how well the iPhone connects to other devices, such as AirPods and smart home products. 

In performing these detailed tests for all iPhone models, we believe that we are able to offer an unbiased analysis. Therefore, let’s say you want to purchase an iPhone but don’t know what model suits your taste; this article will help you decide which one would be ideal for you. 

Signing off… 

We hope this guide helps you find the best iPhone to buy for yourself in 2026. Choosing the right iPhone comes down to understanding your needs and budget. With this guide, you’re equipped to make the right decision, whether you need a premium powerhouse or a budget-friendly iPhone.

FAQs

Which iPhone has the best camera? 

The iPhone 18 Pro Max features the most advanced camera system, including a 48MP Fusion main with variable aperture, 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide, and 48MP Fusion telephoto lens. You can record 4K 120fps Dolby Vision videos and apply Cinematic mode effects later. The new Pro controls let you fine-tune the camera like professionals. Moreover, the latest Photographic Styles 3 offers new texture and grain controls. So, it is the best choice for photography enthusiasts. 

How many years do iPhones typically last? 

iPhones generally receive software updates for around 5-6 years, ensuring they remain functional and secure for a long time. 

Where is the best place to buy an iPhone? 

The best places to buy an iPhone include the official Apple Store, authorized retailers, and reputable online platforms such as Best Buy, Walmart, and Amazon.

title.rendered: Roblox Pressure codes (October 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Pressure Codes on October 08, 2026

Pressure throws you into the Hadal Blacksite with a simple goal: recover the assets and make it back alive. That makes free Kroner and Revive Tokens useful, especially when one bad encounter can end a run. The current useful codes give you 2,500 Kroner and one Revive Token. One other code takes currency away, so check the reward before you redeem anything.

All working Pressure codes

  • CodeThatRemoves1000Kroner: -1,000 Kroner (NEW)
  • ModifiersAndMovies: 2.5k Kroner
  • wawa: 1 Revive Token
  • Gullible: Removes 300 Kroner

Expired or unverified Pressure codes

1YEAR!!!, 200M, 2YEARSWASTED, APOLOGYTOUR, CHRISTMAS!!!, DECAY, FRAUD, MISERABLELAUNCHONCEAGAIN, RAVEYARD, SLEDERMAN, SMILEYBOMB!!!, SUCKER, WASTEOFTIME, YOURTAKINGTOOLONG

How to redeem Pressure codes

The code box is in Settings, and you need to redeem codes from the lobby.

  1. Open Pressure on Roblox.
  2. Wait for the lobby to load.
  3. Select the wrench-and-gear Settings icon on the left.
  4. Find the Codes field and paste a working code.
  5. Select Submit.

Your Kroner or Revive count should update after a successful claim.

Why your Pressure code may not work

  • It expired: Event, milestone, and apology codes can disappear without warning.
  • The spelling is off: Pressure codes are case-sensitive, so copy ModifiersAndMovies exactly.
  • You already redeemed it: Codes are generally limited to one claim per account.
  • You are in an old server: Leave Pressure and join a fresh server before trying again.
  • You are not in the lobby: Open the code menu from the main lobby instead of during a run.

If a positive code still fails after a clean copy-paste and a fresh server, treat it as expired and move on.

Where to find more Pressure codes

Pressure does not follow a fixed code schedule. Watch the official Urbanshade Discord, the Urbanshade Roblox community, and the Pressure game page for updates, milestones, and holidays.

The fastest option is to bookmark this page and check the useful list before each new run. If you also play horror games, grab the latest DOORS codes before your next run. If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Build a Blue Lock Squad codes, Giant Simulator Reborn codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

More like this:

  • Meow Madness codes
  • My Anime Mine codes
  • Blue Lock Farm codes

title.rendered: The best iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cases I’d buy

content.rendered:
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are finally here, and if you’re planning to get one, a good case should be one of your first purchases. Apple has introduced several upgrades to its latest Pro models, so I’d want a case that protects the phone without making it feel bulky or hiding its new design.

I’ve rounded up some of the best iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cases worth considering, from clear and rugged cases to leather, silicone, wallet, and stand options. Whether you care most about protection, style, grip, or value, there’s something here for you.

How I chose the case for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max

I don’t think there is one “best” iPhone case for everyone. The right choice depends on how you use your phone.

These are the things I check before buying an iPhone 18 Pro case.

1. Exact iPhone 18 Pro compatibility

This is the first thing I check.

A case designed for an older iPhone might look almost identical to an iPhone 18 Pro case, but “almost identical” isn’t good enough. Even a small change to the camera bump, side buttons, dimensions, or magnet placement can make a case a bad fit.

2. Camera protection

The camera system is one of the biggest reasons I’d buy the Pro model in the first place. The iPhone 18 Pro introduces a 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture. That makes the camera area important to protect carefully.

I look for a raised camera lip or camera surround that prevents the lenses from touching the table when I put the phone down.

3. MagSafe support

MagSafe compatibility is almost essential on a premium iPhone. I use magnetic accessories for charging, stands, mounts, and wallets, so a case that weakens the magnetic connection defeats part of the convenience of the iPhone.

That’s why most of my recommendations here focus on MagSafe-compatible designs.

Looking for chargers, stands, and other add-ons to pair with your case? Check out our guide to the best iPhone 18 Pro accessories.

4. Button and Camera Control feel

A case shouldn’t make the physical controls feel cheap. I pay particular attention to the side buttons and Camera Control. A poorly designed case can make buttons mushy or interfere with touch-sensitive controls.

5. Grip

A case can have fantastic drop protection and still be annoying if it constantly slides around in my hand.

For a phone as large as the iPhone 18 Pro Max, grip matters even more. I prefer cases with textured edges, grippy materials, or a shape that gives my fingers something to hold.

6. Bulk

I don’t automatically equate thicker with better.

A rugged case makes sense if you regularly drop your phone, but for everyday use, I usually choose something that adds protection without completely changing the feel of the iPhone.

This simple checklist makes choosing an iPhone 18 Pro case much easier.

Top 6 iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cases I’d recommend

Before I share my shortlisted cases, here are the official options. Apple has launched a new range of cases alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The lineup includes Silicone, TechWoven, and Clear Cases.

If you want to stick with Apple’s own cases, you can check out the complete collection of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cases and covers on Apple’s website.

1. OtterBox Defender Series Pro: Best rugged iPhone 18 Pro case

If protection comes before everything else, I’d look at OtterBox. The Defender family is designed around serious impact protection, making it the best option if you’re hard on your phone or regularly use it outdoors.

The case has a three-layer rugged construction designed to handle serious drops and everyday impacts. OtterBox says it has been tested to provide 7x the military drop standard. I also like that OtterBox hasn’t completely ignored everyday usability. The case has a textured exterior for better grip, MagSafe compatibility, and port covers to avoid dust accumulation.

However, this is not the case I’d pick if my priority were keeping the iPhone 18 Pro thin. For the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max, that extra grip can also be useful, as the phone is physically larger, heavier, and harder to hold securely with one hand.

Pros

  • Secure, form-fitting design
  • Better suited to drops and rough environments
  • Good grip
  • Protective port covers help keep dust and debris out

Cons

  • Heavier than a typical silicone or clear case
  • Port covers can be slightly inconvenient if you frequently plug in wired accessories
  • Overkill for careful users

Best for: Maximum protection rather than minimum bulk.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

2. ESR Cyber Tough Case: Best protection in budget

For someone who just bought an iPhone 18 Pro and doesn’t want to spend another $50 or $60 on a case, this is the option I’ll consider first.

The appeal of ESR Cyber Tough is straightforward: rugged protection, MagSafe compatibility, and a more affordable approach. It has a triple-layer design with a rigid PC back, a flexible TPE bumper, and PORON foam, and it’s SGS-certified to withstand drops of up to 23 feet.

I also like the attention to everyday usability. The textured sides and curved edges make it easier to grip, while raised bezels, Air Guard corners, button covers, and a charging-port cover add extra protection. The built-in magnets provide up to 1,500g of holding force, making it a good fit for the MagSafe ecosystem.

Pros

  • More affordable than many premium options
  • Protective port cover
  • Practical everyday protection
  • iPhone colour-matched options

Cons

  • More rugged and bulky than slim cases
  • The inner sponge can get damaged by water

Best for: Anyone who wants protection without spending too much on the case itself.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

3. SHIELDON Genuine Leather Case for iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: For a premium look

For people who dislike the look of plastic and silicone cases, I’d go for the SHIELDON. A leather case changes the personality of an iPhone. Instead of making the phone look like rugged equipment, it gives it a more traditional, professional feel.

SHIELDON uses top-grain genuine cowhide leather, so each case has its own natural texture and should develop a richer patina as you use it. The soft leather lining also helps prevent scratches, while the outer surface offers a comfortable, anti-slip, and fingerprint-resistant grip.

It comes with a built-in magnetic ring for supporting MagSafe accessories. I also like the small details, including custom metal buttons, raised camera and screen edges, and a dedicated Camera Control button.

Pros

  • More sophisticated appearance
  • Only 0.09in thick
  • Premium metal buttons
  • Beautiful color options

Cons

  • Leather requires more care than silicone or plastic
  • More expensive than basic cases
  • Natural leather can show signs of wear over time

Best for: Anyone who wants their iPhone 18 Pro to look more refined than rugged.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

4. Luriax Signature Alcantara Case: Luxury without leather

If leather feels too familiar and silicone feels too basic, I’d look at the Luriax Signature case. Luriax wraps it in Italian Alcantara, the same material Ferrari and Lamborghini use in their interiors. Designed in Los Angeles, it feels like suede but shrugs off stains and water far better.

Luriax finishes each case by hand and uses Alcantara for both the outer wrap and the lining. A rigid inner shell takes the force of drops, while raised edges guard the screen. The camera sits on a raised plateau wrapped in the same material. You also get black aluminum buttons, MagSafe and wireless charging support, and free laser engraving.

The main trade-off is price, since this is one of the priciest cases on this list. Also, the edges where your fingers rest can pick up a little oil over time. Leather and plastic cases do this too; you just notice it more on Alcantara. A damp cloth wipes it off, and an alcohol pad plus a soft brush handles heavier buildup.

Pros

  • Soft, suede-like Alcantara inside and out
  • Resists water, stains, and heat
  • Raised camera plateau and screen edges
  • Free personalized engraving

Cons

  • One of the priciest picks here
  • Open bottom edge leaves the base less protected

Best for: Anyone who wants a luxe, non-leather case with a soft-touch feel.

Check out: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

5. FNTCASE Matte Case for iPhone 18 Pro: Built-in stand for convenience

If you want a case that does more than just protect your iPhone, the FNTCASE stands out. Its biggest feature is the 360-degree rotatable metal ring, which works as a finger grip, a hanging hook, and an adjustable stand. I can use it in either portrait or landscape mode, making it handy for watching videos, working, or taking calls.

The case also packs 38 N52 magnets, so it works with MagSafe chargers, wallets, car mounts, and stands. It includes a tempered glass screen protector, while Airbag technology, raised edges, and full camera protection help guard against drops and scratches.

The matte translucent back is another nice touch, with a smooth finish designed to resist fingerprints and everyday smudges.

Pros

  • Matte, frosted finish looks good
  • Strong MagSafe magnetic connection
  • Includes tempered glass screen protector
  • Convenient for watching content, video calls, and travel

Cons

  • Ring mechanism adds noticeable bulk
  • Heavier than a standard slim case
  • Mostly suited to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, not the smaller Pro model

Best for: Users who regularly watch videos or use their phone hands-free.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

6. Smartish Wallet Slayer V1 Case for iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max: Replace your wallet

If I could eliminate one item from my pocket, it would be the separate wallet. That’s why wallet cases still have a place in my recommendations. Smartish wallet case’s side-loading slot can hold up to four cards plus cash without switching to a bulky folio case.

Protection is another strong point. The case has been drop-tested from six feet, while flexible TPU and air-pocket corners help absorb impact, and textured sides provide a comfortable grip. I really liked its colourful options.

The biggest compromise is connectivity. It doesn’t support MagSafe or wireless charging. I’d have to use a cable to charge the phone, which may be a deal-breaker if I rely heavily on magnetic accessories.

Pros

  • Eliminates the need for a separate wallet
  • Grippy sides
  • Drop-tested design
  • Relatively slim for a folio case

Cons

  • No MagSafe support or wireless charging
  • Wallet slot adds some thickness
  • Not ideal if I frequently use magnetic accessories

Best for: Minimalists who want to carry their phone and wallet together.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

7. Miracase Silicone Magnetic Case: Soft, colourful look

If you want something simple, comfortable, grippy, and protective, I’d consider the Miracase Silicone Case. The case features a 3 mm-thick liquid silicone construction with a four-layer design to resist fingerprints, scratches, and everyday drops. I also like the added camera protection and integrated Camera Control cover.

It also supports MagSafe-style magnetic wireless charging, so I can still use compatible chargers without taking the case off. With several colour options available, I could easily keep a few cases and switch them depending on my outfit or mood.

Pros

  • Soft and comfortable silicone finish
  • Comfortable grip
  • Simple everyday design
  • Multiple colour options

Cons

  • 3mm thickness adds some bulk
  • Silicone can attract dust and lint

Best for: Everyday users who want a comfortable, uncomplicated case.

Check out on Amazon: iPhone 18 Pro | iPhone 18 Pro Max

Which iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max case would I buy?

If I were buying the case for myself, my choice would depend on how I planned to use it.

For me, the Spigen would be the most balanced everyday choice. It gives me the clear look I want, MagSafe support, camera protection, and a relatively slim profile.

If I were buying the iPhone 18 Pro Max, I’d be more tempted by an OtterBox or a case with a built-in stand, because the larger phone benefits more from added grip and hands-free support.

Final thoughts

With the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max now officially announced, it’s a good time to start thinking about protection for your new phone. Pre-orders begin September 12, while the phones will be available from September 18.

For me, the right case depends on what I need most. I’d pick Spigen for a clear everyday case, OtterBox for rugged protection, SHIELDON for a premium leather feel, and Smartish if I want to leave my wallet at home. The Miracase is a nice option if I prefer a soft, colourful silicone case.

Whichever one you choose, just make sure you select the correct iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max version before ordering.

Which case are you planning to pair with your new iPhone 18 Pro? Let me know in the comments!

title.rendered: Every song featured in Rockstar’s GTA 6 Extended Look

content.rendered:
The GTA 6 Extended Look was a treat for the fans, as it gave a deeper look at the gameplay, mechanics, and the kind of world Jason and Lucia will experience across Leonida. There’s plenty of information to take in, but Rockstar’s choice of music has undoubtedly grabbed everyone’s attention. The footage features a great mix of classic ’70s rock, pop, hip-hop, and electronic tracks from some of the biggest names in the music scene. Each song perfectly fits with the Florida-inspired vibe Rockstar is trying to recreate in GTA 6.

So, if you’re curious about which tracks play throughout the footage and where you can hear them, here’s a look at every song featured in Rockstar’s GTA 6 Extended Look.

Every song featured in GTA 6 Extended Look

If you still haven’t watched the GTA 6 Extended Look yet, we’ll recommend checking it out first so you can follow along with the songs we’re referring to. With that out of the way, here’s a complete list of all the GTA 6 songs featured in the footage, alongside the timestamps where each of them plays –

It’s important to keep in mind that this isn’t the complete list of GTA 6 songs. We’ve already seen from the GTA 6 leaks that the game will bring tons of radio stations to the mix, and each of them has its own lineup of tracks. So, you can expect plenty more music to listen to as you explore and uncover everything Leonida has to offer.

Songs from previous GTA 6 trailers

The GTA 6 songs from the Extended Look aren’t the only tracks that have already struck with the fans. Let’s not forget that Rockstar has released two trailers for the game before this, and both of them showed just how good the developer is at picking songs that perfectly match the vibe of the game. So, let’s take a look at all the songs in GTA 6 from previous trailers –

Rounding Up

The GTA 6 Extended Look gave us a better idea of the kind of music players will be able to tune into while exploring Leonida. The footage featured a total of 14 different tracks played at various points throughout the gameplay. It featured some of the most popular artists in various genres such as rock, rap, pop, and plenty more.

It’s already a known fact that the GTA 6 map is far bigger and more ambitious compared to anything we’ve seen in the franchise so far. With such a massive world to explore, having the right selection of songs playing in the background will feel just right.

  • Is GTA 6 coming to PC earlier than expected?
  • Why GTA 6 needs a first-person mode

title.rendered: Fortnite Override gets 6 new loot hacks: How to find and use them

content.rendered:
Fortnite recently rolled out its v42.10 update, headlined by a new lineup of sprites including the fan-made Onigiri Sprite and X-Ray Sprite. Besides that, another major part of the update is a new set of loot hacks, which include highly powerful weapons and other items.

Loot hacks were introduced in Fortnite on August 20, with the launch of Chapter 7 Season 4: Override. This feature enabled players to somewhat customize the kind of items they get from chests, given they first collect enough Sprite Dust to influence the loot—providing more incentive to partake in sprite-hunting.

The following article lists the new loot hacks made available in last week’s update. It also explains how you can find and use them more often during matches across Fortnite.

New loot hacks and what they do in Fortnite Override

1. Loot Hacker Sprite Variant

You can obtain sprites of the Loot Hacker variant and equip them to boost your chances of getting items from your unlocked loot hack when you open chests. In short, this loot hack item is a boost you can apply to get the other loot hack items quicker in a match.

2. Wrecker Revolver

Damage: Very high
Range: Long
Rate of fire: Slow

3. Deadeye Assault Rifle

Damage: Low
Range: Medium, long
Rate of fire: Medium
*Comes with scope attached.

4. Holo Twister Assault Rifle

Damage: Low-to-medium
Range: Short, medium, long
Rate of fire: Medium

5. Scorpion’s Kombat Kit

This is a special item inspired by Mortal Kombat’s Scorpion. While equipped, you can deal serious damage through hand-to-hand combat. Alternatively, you can use the spear to deal damage and simultaneously pull an enemy closer.

6. Caduceus Staff

The Caduceus Staff helps you restore your health and has the capacity of adding the same up to a value of 300. Besides that, you can also aim it at a squad member, even over long distances, to revive him, increase his health, or provide a temporary buff to the damage he inflicts.

How to find and use Fortnite Override loot hacks

All the aforementioned loot hack items in Fortnite Override first need to be unlocked using Sprite Dust before you can get your hands on them. You can do so by following the steps below.

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Override tab.
  2. Then, select the desired loot hack item and press and hold the Unlock button to add it to your loot pool.

Once any of these loot hacks have been acquired, you can exclusively find them by opening chests during a match in Unranked Battle Royale, Fortnite Reload, or Fortnite Creative. For boosting your chances of obtaining these items more easily, you can further level up your desired ones by using the “Upgrade” button in the loot hack tab shown above, in exchange for more Sprite Dust.

Besides shooting up the probability of getting loot hack items from chests, you can also unlock new rarity tiers for them at certain points. These upgrades make a crucial difference because the loot hack item’s power increases with each increase in rarity, with the “Legendary” level obviously offering the best version of it.

There are six different upgrade levels for each loot hack. Here’s what happens at each level for each item.

Loot Hacker Sprite Variant

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 7% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: 9% drop rate via chests
  • Level 4: 11% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 13% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: 15% drop rate via chests

Wrecker Revolver

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 5% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: Epic rarity
  • Level 4: 8% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 10% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: Legendary rarity

Deadeye Assault Rifle

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 5% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: Epic rarity
  • Level 4: 8% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 10% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: Legendary rarity

Holo Twister Assault Rifle

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 5% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: Epic rarity
  • Level 4: 8% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 10% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: Legendary rarity

Scorpion’s Kombat Kit

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 4% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: 6% drop rate via chests
  • Level 4: 8% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 10% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: Mythic rarity

Caduceus Staff Rifle

  • Level 1: Add to loot pool
  • Level 2: 4% drop rate via chests
  • Level 3: 5% drop rate via chests
  • Level 4: 6% drop rate via chests
  • Level 5: 8% drop rate via chests
  • Level 6: 10% drop rate via chests

To unlock all levels for all these items, it costs several thousand Sprite Dust. So, it is imperative to extract as many high-tier sprites during matches as you can to accrue enough of this in-game commodity. You can also get more Sprite Dust by using certain Fortnite lobby hacks, such as “Magilume”, “Chispambo”, “H0p0nVC”, among others, granted you haven’t already used these codes.

Author’s pick

Each of the loot hack items mentioned above is useful when you get it during a Fortnite match. However, certain ones are more OP and offer you the edge over those who don’t have them yet at any point during a match.

In my experience, one of the first things you should do is unlock the Loot Hacker Sprite variant. Once you extract a sprite of that type, make sure to equip it before each match where you want to make the most of your unlocked loot pool.

Among the best weapons in the current loot hack set are the Wrecker Revolver and the Caduceus Staff. While the former is a terrific choice for offense, the latter is quite a useful health item, and its high capacity to heal makes sure you can go a large part of the match relying on just this one healing item.

After these two, the Holo Twister Assault Rifle is another fun and effective tool for those who prefer striking enemies from afar, thanks to its scope. However, the same attachment can prove to be detrimental to your aim in close-range fights, so ensure you switch to another weapon when the enemy is at a close distance.

These loot hack items have quickly become a prevalent part of Fortnite matches, despite being released just around a week ago. Hence, it helps massively to unlock all of them and upgrade them to the highest level to take the upper hand in eligible online matches.

  • How to find and use the Skeleton Key in Fortnite

title.rendered: 10 key blink-and-you’ll-miss-it details in GTA 6 Extended Look

content.rendered:
As we near GTA 6’s release date, the hype surrounding it has become increasingly palpable. The community of the franchise’s longtime fans remains buzzing, as intrigued newcomers also await the roll-out. While part of it is down to the series of leaks orchestrated by Cyberleek, a bigger reason for the boosted hype is the GTA 6 Extended Look that premiered on August 27 via Netflix.

Being the big launch year, 2026 has seen a few major GTA 6 developments take place. From the pre-orders opening in June to a new batch of official screenshots and videos in August, the marketing for the forthcoming title is starting to pick up pace. The biggest piece of this promotion puzzle so far has been the aforementioned Extended Look gameplay reveal, which we have dissected below to share some important details that may have gone unnoticed.

GTA 6 Extended Look gameplay: 10 key observations you may have missed

1. Leonida has a booming wildlife, much like RDR 2’s world

Those who watched GTA 6 Extended Look and have also played Red Dead Redemption 2, another Rockstar Games title, can easily notice that the former showed a few notable gameplay features that are plucked right out of the Wild West-themed game.

In the opening segment where Jason and Lucia are making a pick-up for Boobie Ike, one of the several key GTA 6 characters, the male protagonist briefly stops to pet a dog. During that interaction, a “Study” option can also be seen, which is something straight out of RDR 2. This feature was used by Arthur Morgan in the 2018 game to add newly encountered animals to his catalog for unlocking deeper insights, such as pelt quality.

Given the sheer biodiversity in RDR 2, it may not be far-fetched to assume that GTA 6’s Leonida could also be one of the most biodiverse worlds Rockstar devs have ever created. If anything, one of the newly released screenshots depicting a green iguana might be hinting at the same.

While studying wildlife served an important purpose in RDR 2, it will be interesting to see how the same is incorporated in the GTA 6 map. Since hunting was a small but existent part of its predecessor, it will be a safe bet to think the “Study” feature might come in handy for those kinds of missions. However, how this option would be of any considerable use for pets is anyone’s guess right now.

2. GTA 6 inherits RDR 2’s Honor system

On top of biodiversity, it looks like GTA 6 has also adopted the “Honor” system introduced by Rockstar in RDR 2. A quick revision for those who may not know: it is a game mechanic that keeps a record of all the protagonist’s actions in the game and changes the in-game world based on the same, leading to a certain kind of impression among NPCs and even impacting how missions turn out.

In the same scene where Jason pets the dog, an emoji with a halo appears on the right edge of the screen. This can be seen as the game registering a positive action, and it basically confirms that the Honor system from RDR 2 is set to make its foray into the widely acclaimed open-world action franchise next. Based on what we saw of it in the Western adventure, it will be exciting to experience how Rockstar devs have tailored it to fit GTA 6’s atmosphere.

3. Grand Theft Auto has changed

Perhaps the most common crime that every player commits in each game in this series is stealing a vehicle, aka Grand Theft Auto. This very action has been significantly evolved in GTA 6 compared to any past entry in the franchise.

In the forthcoming GTA title, there’s more to stealing or hijacking a car than simply pressing a particular button when near it. If you are hijacking, you now have to win a little minigame against the NPC by repeatedly pressing a certain button until the meter is full to be able to throw out the driver and take control of the car.

On the other hand, if you are stealing an unattended car, you don’t always have to attract attention or cause damage to the vehicle by smashing its window to get in. As confirmed in the Extended Look, you can more discreetly gain access to a car by using the “Slim Jim” tool option. All this adds to the game’s realistic approach, whereas offering multiple ways to go about the same action ensures ample player freedom.

4. The new GTA Wanted System has layers

Crime and punishment in the GTA series has been quite straightforward till now. You break a law in the game’s world, you get an equivalent wanted level for it. Break more, and you get an additional star, up to a maximum of five (the maximum wanted level in GTA 5). To lose the wanted level, you basically need to escape the police’s radar and stay hidden for some time. For GTA 6, Rockstar has cranked things up a bit and added more variables into the equation.

In the middle of Jason and Brian Heder’s rooftop conversation, a highlight reel showing various store heists plays out. And, for a brief moment, a gameplay bit is also shown, which depicts a two-star wanted level and several different icons underneath it. From what we understand, these icons represent the information law enforcement has on Jason and Lucia.

Key details about the GTA 6 protagonists, such as their faces, the clothes they are wearing, the weapons they are carrying, whether or not they are operating in numbers, and whether their crime was captured on CCTVs, will now be tracked by the police. These elements comprise a layered wanted system that should present a new challenge for players, particularly those who have been rattling the men in blue’s cages through the past GTA games.

5. Improved hand-to-hand combat in GTA 6

If you manage to catch the brief glimpse of the fisticuffs that the Extended Look cuts to while Jason-Lucia are driving towards Brian and Lori’s location, you will notice the variations in Lucia’s fighting. It shows free-flowing hand-to-hand combat where she performs a dodge, a parry, and a counter-attack. While the first two actions were also there in GTA 5, parrying is something new and should enhance the combat gameplay in GTA 6.

Skip to the highlights shown after the segment with Raul Bautista, and you will see another new mechanic that could come in handy in melee fights. The jewelry store robbery in question shows Lucia enter a scuffle with an NPC and win a button-mashing contest to disarm the latter. While disarming an opponent by shooting the hands was there in GTA 4 (the same was ditched for GTA 5), doing it via hand-to-hand combat is a novelty in the series.

Additionally, right after Lucia’s fight scene, the video cuts to Jason vaulting over the hood of a car. This is a new maneuver that should prove useful while making an escape on foot. It could also make melee combat more seamless, especially when facing enemies who are a few feet away from the player character.

6. Modern-day equivalents of RDR 2 tonics are in GTA 6

In the montage immediately following the Raul Bautista section in the video, there is a split-second glimpse of the overlay menu that shows, at the bottom-left corner, what appear to be performance-enhancing drugs.

Those who have played RDR 2 should be able to recall consumables, such as tonics and tobacco, which restored crucial HUD meters in the game and thus should be able to get an idea of where things are going with the introduction of similar items in GTA 6.

7. Stamina and Focus from RDR 2 are now in GTA

Among the most fundamental mechanics that Rockstar has adapted into GTA 6 from RDR 2 are the stamina and focus/deadeye meters. These HUD elements can be observed throughout the gameplay video, specifically during the segments where either protagonist engages actively in combat by firing a weapon or throwing some punches.

In RDR 2, the stamina meter dictated actions such as how long you could sprint before slowing down, whereas the focus meter was the measure for how long you could slow down time, to aim more precisely, during a gunfight. These two uses should serve very well in GTA, where third-person shooter combat is an inalienable part of the game’s experience.

When triggering Focus in GTA 6, you can also see the fatal and non-fatal injury points on an enemy marked in red and yellow, respectively. This mechanic is briefly displayed during Jason’s gunfight at the Megamundo building. With these yellow hit zones, the game offers players a choice to subdue the enemy instead of killing him. Such calls could contribute to and influence where you stand as per the aforementioned Honor system.

8. Jason and Lucia have their own unique health meters

Speaking of HUD changes, a small but worthwhile catch is the difference between the health meters of Jason and Lucia, where the latter’s is shorter. This could either suggest that aspects such as health, stamina, and focus may permanently differ between the two protagonists. Or, it could also mean that there is room for extending the meter through in-game activities.

Another noteworthy bit from the gameplay reveal is the presence of a break near the middle of the health meter. While not much is known about its meaning, this could probably mark the point till which health automatically regenerates. This is an educated guess based on the fact that GTA 5 also offers health regeneration till about 50% of the bar.

9. New side activities in GTA 6

A GTA game isn’t just about the story missions but also the various side activities available in its sprawling world. Throughout the series, we have had several different activities and minigames, ranging from pool in GTA San Andreas to triathlons in GTA 5.

In GTA 6 though, we seem to be getting new side activities such as backyard wrestling and dirtbike racing. On the flip side, there also appear to be activities that we have seen in the series before making a return, such as backyard basketball, gymming, base jumping, street racing, and track racing. These additional in-game pastimes should provide players enough opportunities to catch a break from the missions that progress the narrative.

10. Driving in GTA 6 is more realistic than in GTA 5

If you look up the viral GTA 5 videos today, you will find tons of them show instances of driving cars and riding bikes that tend to break most laws of physics. In short, they reflect the side of the game that is more arcade-y, strongly prioritizing the fun element over realism. If the driving segments in GTA 6 Extended Look are anything to go by, the series seems to be dialing down the unrealistic handling and gravitating towards something that is closer to the real world.

In other words, the heft of the car apparently plays a more integral role in determining how easily you can take sharp turns and quick maneuvers. Also, things like getting a flipped-over car back on its wheels may not be as easy as before.

The last GTA title to take a realistic approach to driving was 2008’s GTA 4, which also split the community because of that very design choice. Although GTA 6 clips still don’t make driving look as rigid as it was in the Niko Bellic-led title, it certainly looks like this aspect of the forthcoming game sits somewhere between GTA 4 and GTA 5.

The nitty-gritties of whether the feel is closer to one game or another is something that we will only know for sure, closer to launch, when the reviews start coming out.

Author’s take

The excitement of another GTA title, the first in 13 years, rolling out in two months’ time is immense in itself. On top of that, the GTA 6 Extended Look has done the perfect job of stirring even more hype. The first generous peek at gameplay has more or less confirmed that the Rockstar Games title has done remarkably well in a few major aspects, namely graphical fidelity and open-world detail.

The American publisher’s last big project, RDR 2, was a record-shattering release and elevated the standards for the open-world action genre. Given that GTA 6 wears RDR 2’s influence on its sleeve, the hotly anticipated title should mark an upgrade over what the Western-themed title did, especially in terms of immersion. And if that happens, a whole new set of records can be expected to be broken once GTA 6 launches on November 19.

  • Every GTA protagonist, ranked from worst to best
