title.rendered: Best time to buy an iPhone in 2026: Save big with these smart tips!

content.rendered:
Buying an iPhone used to be fairly predictable: Apple launched the new models in September, older iPhones got cheaper, and Black Friday brought some of the best deals of the year. But after Apple’s September 2026 event, it is time to rethink that strategy.

This year, Apple changed its iPhone release cycle. Instead of launching a standard iPhone 18, Apple introduced only the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its September event, alongside its first foldable, the iPhone Duo. At the same time, Apple raised the starting price of every iPhone it continues to sell by $100.

That means the best time to buy an iPhone in 2026 depends more than ever on which model you want, whether you’re willing to buy an older generation, and how much storage you need.

In this guide, I’ll explain when I think you should buy an iPhone, when you should wait, and why Apple’s unusual 2026 pricing makes the usual “buy after the new iPhone launches” advice less straightforward.

Table of Contents
  • Apple's iPhone release schedule and price trends
    • iPhone prices: 2026 vs. previous pricing
  • Apple's 2026 iPhone price increases make storage more important
  • Best times to buy an iPhone
    • Right after launch (September – October)
    • Black Friday & Cyber Monday (November)
    • Holiday Sales (December – January)
    • Wait for the next iPhone release cycle (February – March)
    • Back-to-School promotions (July – August)
  • Best time to buy a certified refurbished iPhone in 2026
    • Pros and cons
  • How to ensure quality and warranty: Is a refurbished iPhone worth it?
  • When and how to find the best iPhone deals?
  • Regional considerations
  • So, when is the best time to buy an iPhone in 2026?
    • My bottom line

Apple’s iPhone release schedule and price trends

For years, Apple’s iPhone release cycle followed a simple pattern: new flagship iPhones arrived in September, followed by pre-orders and sales shortly afterward. The launch of the next generation also meant older models usually became cheaper or disappeared from Apple’s lineup.

Apple has changed that pattern in 2026.

At its Surprise and Shine event, Apple introduced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but did not launch a standard iPhone 18. Apple also introduced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone. The iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max were discontinued after the new Pro models arrived.

The result is an unusually expensive iPhone lineup.

iPhone prices: 2026 vs. previous pricing

The important thing to notice is that Apple didn’t just make the new iPhones more expensive. It also raised the prices of existing models. The iPhone 17 went from $799 to $899, while the iPhone 17e went from $599 to $699. The iPhone Air and iPhone 16 also received $100 increases.

So, unlike previous years, I wouldn’t automatically assume that September is the best time to buy an older iPhone.

Apple’s 2026 iPhone price increases make storage more important

The biggest surprise isn’t just the $100 increase at the entry level. It’s how quickly the price climbs when you add storage.

The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for 256GB, but the price rises to $1,399 for 512GB, $1,799 for 1TB, and $2,399 for 2TB.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Air, and the rest of the lineup follow the same pattern:

Apple’s 2TB option is particularly expensive. Moving from 1TB to 2TB costs an additional $600. Overall, going from the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro Max to the 2TB model adds $1,200 to the price.

That’s why I would think carefully about storage before buying this year’s iPhone. If you don’t actually need 2TB, spending hundreds of dollars on storage that you rarely use doesn’t make much sense.

Best times to buy an iPhone

The best time to buy now depends on whether you’re buying the newest iPhone, an older model, or a refurbished device.

Right after launch (September – October)

If you want Apple’s newest Pro iPhone, the period immediately after launch is one of the best times to buy because you’ll get the newest hardware without waiting for another generation. The iPhone Duo is particularly significant because it marks Apple’s move into the foldable iPhone category.

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max went up for pre-order on September 12, with availability beginning September 18, whereas iPhone Duo will be available from October 23.

However, I wouldn’t necessarily recommend buying immediately if your main goal is saving money. Apple’s new Pro models start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively, while iPhone Duo starts at a whopping $1,999, and higher storage configurations can push the price even higher.

If I were buying one, I’d compare Apple’s trade-in value with carrier promotions before paying full price. Apple says eligible iPhone 13 or later trade-ins can receive up to $885 in credit, while select carrier offers can provide up to $1,200 in credits for eligible devices.

There’s another reason I wouldn’t rush to upgrade: Apple’s unusual 2026 release cycle means the standard iPhone 18 isn’t part of the September lineup. If you don’t need the latest Pro features or the foldable design of the iPhone Duo, waiting for the rest of Apple’s iPhone 18 lineup could give you more options.

My advice: Buy in September or October if you want the latest iPhone and can take advantage of a strong trade-in or carrier promotion. Otherwise, wait.

Black Friday & Cyber Monday (November)

Black Friday and Cyber Monday remain some of the best opportunities to save on an iPhone.

The important difference in 2026 is that I would focus less on expecting Apple itself to cut the price and more on looking at retailers like Amazon, carriers, trade-in bonuses, gift cards, and accessory bundle offers.

These deals can be especially attractive for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17e because Apple has increased its official prices. A retailer discount can effectively cancel out some or all of Apple’s $100 price increase.

If you’re not interested in the newest iPhone 18 Pro, I’d make Black Friday one of my first shopping windows.

Holiday Sales (December – January)

December and January can also be good times to buy.

Retailers often use the holiday shopping period to discount existing inventory, while carriers may offer trade-in bonuses or promotional financing to attract last-minute shoppers and post-holiday buyers.

This is particularly worth watching for older iPhones. Since Apple’s official prices are now higher across its lineup, a retailer offering even a modest discount can make an older model a lot more appealing.

Wait for the next iPhone release cycle (February – March)

In a normal year, I would say September is the time to buy the previous generation because Apple launches the new model and reduces the price of the older one.

I wouldn’t follow that rule blindly in 2026.

Apple’s new release strategy means the standard iPhone 18 wasn’t part of the September launch. The company instead focused on the Pro lineup and iPhone Duo. The standard iPhone 18 is expected to follow a different release schedule, meaning buyers who don’t need a Pro model may benefit from waiting for the next stage of Apple’s 2026-27 iPhone cycle.

If you already own an iPhone 17 and aren’t impressed by the 18 Pro, I would personally wait rather than upgrade simply because a new iPhone generation has arrived.

Back-to-School promotions (July – August)

If you’re a student or buying an iPhone for a student, don’t miss the back-to-school sales. Apple and major retailers offer student discounts and education-focused deals during July and August, making it a great time to buy an iPhone or even an iPad or Mac.

These promotions often include trade-in bonuses, gift cards, or discounts on accessories, helping students and teachers save on their tech upgrades.

Best time to buy a certified refurbished iPhone in 2026

If you want an iPhone without paying Apple’s increasingly high prices, refurbished models from reputable sources deserve more attention in 2026.

The best times to shop for refurbished iPhones are still Black Friday, Cyber Monday, the holiday shopping season, and back-to-school sales.

But there’s another advantage this year: Apple’s higher prices make older-generation iPhones more valuable as refurbished purchases. For example, instead of paying $1,199 for the entry-level iPhone 18 Pro, you may find a previous-generation Pro model with similar performance for substantially less through a reputable refurbished seller.

A refurbished iPhone is a pre-owned device that has been inspected, tested, and repaired if necessary before being resold. The quality depends heavily on the seller, so I would prioritize Apple Certified Refurbished products or established retailers with clear warranty and return policies.

Pros and cons

Pros

  • Lower price than buying a new iPhone
  • Professionally tested and repaired
  • Apple Certified Refurbished devices come with a one-year warranty
  • Older Pro models can offer excellent performance for considerably less
  • More environmentally friendly than buying a brand-new device

Cons

  • Availability depends on inventory
  • Some third-party refurbished phones may have cosmetic imperfections
  • Battery condition varies by seller
  • Older models won’t receive new hardware features
  • You need to pay close attention to the warranty and return policy

How to ensure quality and warranty: Is a refurbished iPhone worth it?

Before buying a used or refurbished iPhone, I recommend checking the return policy, battery health, carrier compatibility, and whether the device is unlocked.

I would also stick to reputable sources.

  • Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store: Apple’s refurbished devices are tested and come with a one-year warranty.
  • Major carriers: Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, and other carriers sometimes sell refurbished iPhones with their own warranties and financing options.
  • Trusted third-party retailers: Retailers such as Best Buy and Amazon Renewed can offer good deals, but always check the exact condition, warranty, return period, and battery policy before ordering.

When and how to find the best iPhone deals?

With Apple’s 2026 price increases, I would use a slightly different strategy when shopping for an iPhone.

  • Don’t look only at the starting price: The cheapest configuration can look reasonable until you add the storage you actually need.
  • Compare every storage tier: On the iPhone 18 Pro Max, going from 512GB to 1TB costs $400, while moving from 1TB to 2TB costs another $600.
  • Check trade-in offers: A strong trade-in can make a $1,199 or $1,299 iPhone much more affordable.
  • Compare carrier promotions: Carrier credits can sometimes save considerably more than a direct retailer discount.
  • Don’t assume older means cheaper: Apple has increased the price of several existing iPhones by $100.
  • Shop during Black Friday: Retailers are often more aggressive with discounts during major shopping events.
  • Consider refurbished: A previous-generation Pro model can offer much better value if you don’t need the latest features.
  • Avoid unnecessary storage: If 256GB is enough for your usage, there’s little reason to spend hundreds more on 1TB or 2TB.

Regional considerations

The best time to buy an iPhone varies depending on where you live.

In the U.S., major shopping periods such as Black Friday and Cyber Monday can bring substantial retailer and carrier promotions.

In India, Diwali remains one of the most important shopping periods for electronics. Amazon, Flipkart, Apple resellers, banks, and carriers can all offer different combinations of discounts, cashback, exchange bonuses, and promotional pricing.

But you should keep in mind that there are more factors than the headline price. Taxes, exchange rates, warranty coverage, eSIM requirements, and regional model differences can all affect whether importing an iPhone is actually worthwhile.

For example, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at ₹1,64,900 in India, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at ₹1,79,900. The 2TB Pro Max reaches ₹3,29,900 in India.

If you’re buying internationally, I would also check whether the model supports the cellular bands used by your carrier and whether Apple’s warranty and service coverage apply in your country.

So, when is the best time to buy an iPhone in 2026?

If you want the iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max, I suggest buying around launch only if you can take advantage of a good trade-in or carrier promotion. There’s little reason to wait several months simply hoping Apple will lower the official price.

If you want the best value, I’d wait for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, holiday promotions, or a strong retailer/carrier deal on the iPhone 17 or another older model.

If you’re considering the iPhone 17 or 17e, be aware that Apple has unexpectedly increased its prices by $100. That makes retailer discounts particularly important. The iPhone 17 now starts at $899, while the 17e starts at $699.

And if you don’t need an iPhone immediately, waiting is arguably more attractive than usual this year. Apple’s split release cycle means the September 2026 launch isn’t the complete iPhone 18 generation, so the lineup could change again as Apple continues its new release schedule.

My bottom line

I wouldn’t treat September as an automatic “buy now” or “buy the old model” moment anymore.

  • Buy at launch if you want the newest Pro model and have a strong trade-in or carrier offer.
  • Wait for Black Friday if you’re primarily looking for a discount.
  • Buy refurbished if value matters more than having the newest hardware.
  • Wait for the next release window if you’re happy with your current iPhone and don’t need to upgrade immediately.

Most importantly, watch the total configuration price, not just the starting price. In 2026, Apple’s storage pricing can turn what looks like a $1,299 phone into a $2,499 purchase surprisingly quickly.

Signing off

I hope this guide helps you decide not only when to buy an iPhone, but whether you should buy one right now at all. If you’re considering a purchase in 2026, check out our guide on which iPhone to buy.

  • Best MagSafe accessories to enhance your iPhone experience

title.rendered: Apple Watch Siri Recap will summarize your conversations, but it won’t record audio

content.rendered:
Apple is bringing Siri Recap to the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4. The Apple Intelligence feature can listen for the moments you choose, turn a conversation into a short summary, and save the result in the Siri app so you can check it later.

Apple says Siri Recap is designed to help you stay present during meetings, classes, or everyday conversations. The feature will arrive in beta later this year, starting in English, and it will not be available on every Apple Watch.

Siri Recap creates notes, not a full transcript

When enabled, Siri Recap uses the Apple Watch microphone to capture the substance of a conversation and generate a title and key points. Apple describes the result as a high-level summary rather than a word-for-word transcript.

The summaries can be reviewed, edited, deleted, or exported from the Siri app. If you do not save them, Apple says Siri Recaps automatically delete after seven days.

The feature does not identify who said each line. It may still include a person’s name if that name comes up in the conversation, but it does not label people as "Speaker A" or "Speaker B." That makes Siri Recap more like quick personal notes than a meeting recorder.

Apple also warns that summaries can be incomplete or inaccurate. Important details may be left out or misunderstood, so Siri Recap should not replace checking an important instruction, appointment, or agreement with the people involved.

Siri Recap is opt-in and can be scheduled

Siri Recap only runs when you turn it on. Apple says you can control it from the Watch app on your iPhone, set a schedule based on time or location, and switch it off from Control Center at any point.

Apple says the watch does not create or store an audio recording. Audio is processed through the Secure Exclave in the S11 chip, then deleted after processing. The final summaries use Private Cloud Compute when needed, and saved summaries sync through iCloud with end-to-end encryption.

That privacy design will matter to anyone who finds an always-listening summary feature uncomfortable. It does not remove every social question around recording a conversation, but Apple has at least made activation deliberate and visible rather than automatic.

You need a new Apple Watch and a supported iPhone

Apple’s current support requirements list:

  • Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4
  • iPhone 16 or later, including iPhone Air and iPhone Duo
  • Apple Intelligence and Siri AI beta support
  • English at launch, with more languages to follow

Siri Recap and the related Live Rewind feature will be available in beta later this year. Live Rewind is separate from Siri Recap. It shows a text snippet from the previous 15 seconds when you double-press the Digital Crown, which is useful when you missed a sentence and do not need a full summary.

The feature is part of the larger watchOS 27 update, which also brings Siri AI closer to the wrist. Apple Watch users who still rely on the older Siri experience can review this guide to using Siri on Apple Watch while waiting for the beta.

Siri Recap sounds useful for people who leave meetings with a vague memory of the important parts. Its real test will be whether the summaries are accurate enough to trust and unobtrusive enough to use around other people.

title.rendered: Apple now accepting App Store submissions built with iOS 27, macOS 27, and more

content.rendered:
Apple is now accepting App Store submissions built with the latest operating-system SDKs. Developers can use the Xcode 27 Release Candidate to build, test with TestFlight, and submit apps for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27, visionOS 27, and watchOS 27.

Apple announced the change in an Apple Developer update on September 9, ahead of the public rollout of the new software. Developers no longer need to wait for the final operating-system releases to send compatible updates through App Review.

Developers can submit apps for all six platforms

The submission window covers apps and games built for:

  • iOS 27
  • iPadOS 27
  • macOS 27
  • tvOS 27
  • visionOS 27
  • watchOS 27

Apple says the latest SDKs let developers take advantage of Apple Intelligence, the Foundation Models framework, design changes, and new App Store features. The immediate task for developers is to download Xcode 27, test the app on the new software, and send the build through App Store Connect.

The change also gives users a clearer signal that third-party apps are being prepared for the new releases. Features that depend on updated APIs or the new Apple Intelligence tools can now move from beta testing toward public availability.

macOS 27 is the cutoff for Intel support

Apple is using this release to draw a harder line on the Mac. macOS 26 is the final release that supports Intel Macs and Rosetta. macOS 27 will run on Apple silicon Macs only.

Developers who still ship universal Mac apps can set their Xcode build architecture to arm64 only, rebuild the app, and resubmit it. That removes Intel support from the app and lets the team focus on Apple silicon, but it also means older Macs will need a compatible previous version.

You can check the affected hardware in this macOS 27 compatibility guide. Apps can still support Intel Macs when they target macOS 26, but a macOS 27 build needs Apple silicon.

The wider App Store deadline arrives in April 2027

Apple’s current submission window is optional in the short term, but the SDK requirements will become mandatory later. Starting in April 2027, apps and games uploaded to App Store Connect must meet these minimums:

  • iOS and iPadOS apps must use the iOS and iPadOS 27 SDK or later.
  • tvOS apps must use the tvOS 27 SDK or later.
  • visionOS apps must use the visionOS 27 SDK or later.
  • watchOS apps must use the watchOS 27 SDK or later.

Apple’s developer page does not list a matching April 2027 minimum SDK requirement for macOS in that section, but the Apple silicon-only rule for macOS 27 still applies. Developers also need to account for App Review, which covers app updates, in-app purchases, metadata, and other submitted content.

The move comes as Apple continues to update how the App Store handles newer software and AI-powered apps. Its work on App Store rules for AI agents shows why the review process will matter as much as the new SDK features. For now, the message to developers is straightforward: the new platforms are open for business, and the migration clock has started.

title.rendered: iPhone 14, 15 and 16 get another free year of satellite features

content.rendered:
Apple is extending free access to its iPhone satellite features for another year. The extension covers existing iPhone 14, iPhone 15, and iPhone 16 users who activated their device in a supported country or region before midnight Pacific Time on September 9.

Apple confirmed the change in its iPhone Duo announcement, alongside the launch of its first foldable iPhone. It means eligible owners can keep using satellite features without a new charge for at least another year.

Who gets the extra year

The extension applies to:

  • iPhone 14 models
  • iPhone 15 models
  • iPhone 16 models

The iPhone must have been activated in a country or region where Apple satellite features are supported before the September 9 cutoff. Availability still depends on the user’s location, device model, and the feature being used.

Apple has not announced what it will charge, if anything, when the free period eventually ends. For now, owners of these older iPhones can continue using the service without changing their plan.

What remains free

Apple’s satellite tools are designed for moments when there is no cellular or Wi-Fi connection. They include Emergency SOS via satellite, Messages via satellite, Find My location sharing, and Roadside Assistance via satellite where supported.

The features do not turn an iPhone into a normal satellite phone. Messages can take longer to send, and the phone needs a reasonably clear view of the sky. Trees, buildings, mountains, and other obstructions can make a connection slower or impossible.

If you own a compatible iPhone, Apple’s satellite connectivity guide explains which features work in your region. You can also follow this guide to using Emergency SOS via satellite or the guide to sending messages via satellite on iPhone before heading somewhere with no signal.

Emergency SOS remains the most important use case. When a normal emergency call cannot connect, the iPhone can guide you through a short questionnaire and help send the details to emergency services. Apple’s satellite network relies on Globalstar and has limited bandwidth, so it is meant for short, urgent communication rather than regular texting.

Apple is still extending the trial year by year

This is at least the third extension for iPhone 14 owners. Apple originally included two years of free satellite access with the iPhone 14, then extended the period as newer iPhone generations added the same hardware.

The annual extensions give existing owners more time, but they also leave the long-term pricing question open. Apple has not said whether satellite access will become a subscription, remain free for basic safety features, or be bundled with another service.

For now, the practical answer is simple: eligible iPhone 14, 15, and 16 owners get another free year, but the service still depends on regional availability and a clear path to the sky.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Series 12: Everything you need to know about

content.rendered:
Apple’s September 2026 event was packed with exciting announcements, but one of the biggest highlights was the reveal of the new Apple Watch Series 12. At first glance, it might not look like a major hardware upgrade. However, Apple has done some real magic on the software and feature side this time around, which massively improves the wearable experience.

So, if you’re wondering what’s new, what’s different, and whether Apple Watch Series 12 is worth the price, here’s a complete breakdown of everything it brings to the table.

Apple Watch Series 12 specifications at a glance (Detailed overview)

Designs & colors: What’s new

The Apple Watch Series 12’s design can be seen as an evolution of its predecessors. Rather than bringing a major design overhaul, Apple has focused on making subtle changes and improvements across the board, including new materials, finishes, and strap options. The wearable is available in two sizes, 42mm and 46mm. Depending on what you choose, you’ll also have three different case materials to pick from:

  • Aluminum: Dark Bronze, Light Gold, Black, and Space Gray
  • Titanium: Radiant Gold and Natural Titanium
  • Ceramic: Pearl White and Night Blue

That’s right, the Apple Watch Series 12 colors will depend on the case you choose. For the first time, Apple has also introduced ceramic as a casing option, available in Pearl White and Night Blue, giving the watch a more premium look. On the other hand, the aluminum models feature Ceramic Shield 2, which makes them more durable and better for everyday use.

Apple is also bringing a wide range of new strap colors and finishes. This includes the likes of Sport Band, Sport Loop, Nike Sport Band, Modern Buckle, and Milanese Loop, giving users tons of ways to customize the watch.

Battery and charging: A major battery boost

Battery life is another area where the Apple Watch Series 12 brings some major changes. Although Apple still promises up to 24 hours of regular use, the bigger improvement comes with outdoor workouts. The Series 12 will now last for up to 10 hours, which is a 25% boost compared to the previous generation.

Charging is also now lightning quick. A 15-minute charge can deliver up to 12 hours of normal use, and a 30-minute charge can take the watch to 80%. When you need to stretch that battery even further, Low Power Mode can come in handy, providing up to 38 hours of battery life. It’s fair to say that the Apple Watch Series 12 battery life won’t disappoint you.

Performance: New S11 chip

The Apple Watch Series 12 gets a major performance boost, all thanks to Apple’s new S11 chip. The processor is paired with a 4-core Neural Engine and 54GB of storage, which gives the watch all the power needed to handle everyday tasks and its advanced features.

However, the S11 chip isn’t just about making the watch faster. It plays a crucial role in powering some of Apple’s new health and intelligence features, including the Health Sensing System, accurate HRV and step tracking, and the new Audio Intelligence system.

Health sensing system

Apple is putting a major focus on the new Health Sensing System in the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, and for a good reason. It has added new sensors that are designed to collect health data more frequently and accurately, which gives a clearer picture.

With these sensors, the Series 12 can take heart measurements every five seconds throughout the day. This is all possible due to the use of more power-efficient LEDs that allow the watch to capture the readings on a more frequent basis without affecting the battery life.

The heart rate variability (HRV) tracking will measure the variation in time between individual heartbeats. HRV can provide useful insights into stress and recovery.

Apple has brought a new Readiness feature that considers your recent activity, training, sleep score, and other vital signs to show how prepared your body is for the day ahead. On top of that, major improvements have been made to step tracking to make it more accurate during everyday movement and workouts.

Audio Intelligence

One of the most interesting additions to the Apple Watch Series 12 is Audio Intelligence. Basically, it uses the watch’s built-in microphone to make everyday interactions even more convenient for you. Here’s how it works with these four features –

  • Sound Recognition: The watch can identify sounds such as sirens, doorbells, and alarms, and immediately send you an alert.
  • Live Rewind: A double press of the Digital Crown will let you pull up a text snippet of the previous 15 seconds.
  • Siri Recap – Once the conversation ends, Apple Intelligence can analyze it and provide you with a brief summary of what was discussed.
  • Shazam – The watch can identify songs playing around you and display the track information.

Availability and Pricing

When it comes to Apple Watch Series 12 price, it starts at $399, which is the same starting price as the previous generation. Unlike the iPhone lineup, Apple hasn’t increased the price of its latest watch this time around.

When it comes to monthly plans, the Series 12 can be financed at $33.25 per month over 12 months. Pre-orders are now available live in more than 50 countries, and the watch will officially hit the stores on September 18, 2026.

Final thoughts: Should you upgrade?

There’s no denying that Apple Watch Series 12 is packed with great features. You have the likes of the new S11 chip, Health Sensing System, and useful things like Live Rwwind and Siri Recap. However, it’s not a must-have upgrade for everyone. The overall design and functionality of the watch are still the same.

If you already own a recent Apple Watch edition, it might be a better idea to save your money and wait for what Apple comes up with next. However, for those still using an older model, the Series 12 can prove to be a great upgrade. It has better battery life, faster charging, and all the new AI-powered features, which make it a great pick for the price.

title.rendered: Best iPhone Duo cases you can buy right now

content.rendered:
I’ll be honest: when Apple finally announced the iPhone Duo, the first thing I started thinking about was the case. A foldable iPhone changes what I expect from a case.

With a regular iPhone, I mostly care about drop protection, grip, camera protection, and MagSafe compatibility. With the iPhone Duo, I also have to consider the hinge, folding mechanism, dual displays, thickness, magnets, and how the case behaves when the phone is opened and closed.

That makes choosing an iPhone Duo case considerably more complicated than picking a case for an iPhone 18 Pro. So, if you’re already planning to buy the iPhone Duo, these are the six cases I would put on my shortlist right now.

Quick note: The iPhone Duo will be available on October 23. My recommendations below are based on the manufacturers’ published specifications, designs, materials, protection features, and compatibility information available at launch. I’ll update the list once these cases are actually in hand.

What I will look for when buying an iPhone Duo case

The iPhone Duo has a completely different set of mechanical demands, so I would check these things first.

1. Hinge protection

The hinge is one of the most important moving parts on a foldable phone, and it is also one of the areas I don’t want exposed to unnecessary scratches or impacts. A good iPhone Duo case should protect the hinge without preventing the phone from opening completely or making the folded phone unnecessarily thick.

2. Protection without destroying the Duo’s thin design

Apple is making a big deal about how thin the iPhone Duo is when unfolded. I don’t want to spend $1,999 on a remarkably thin foldable phone and then turn it into a chunky brick with a case.

I’m looking for a case that protects the phone while keeping the Duo comfortable enough to carry and use.

3. MagSafe and wireless charging

MagSafe compatibility is another feature I wouldn’t compromise on. The iPhone Duo supports wireless charging, and Apple’s own case uses built-in magnets specifically designed to align with the phone and support MagSafe and Qi2 charging.

However, there’s an important distinction between having magnets and having a case that works properly with every charger or accessory. For example, Spigen itself warns that some magnetic or wireless chargers may be affected by certain Duo case designs.

4. Raised edges around both displays and cameras

I want a visible lip around the displays and camera area, especially because the Duo has two screens. In case I lay my phone on the table, I don’t want the display glass or the camera area to touch the surface first.

5. Grip

A foldable phone can feel awkward when folded because of its unusual proportions. A slippery case is therefore a deal-breaker for me.

I prefer textured fabric, TPU, or other materials that give me enough grip without feeling sticky.

6. The case must not interfere with folding

This sounds obvious, but it matters more on the Duo than on a conventional iPhone.

The case has to accommodate the hinge movement and both folded and unfolded positions. A case that looks fantastic in product photos but fights the hinge when I open the phone isn’t worth buying.

Top 6 cases I’d recommend for iPhone Duo

1. Apple iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand: Best overall

If I were buying an iPhone Duo on launch day and wanted the least complicated case choice, this is where I’d start.

Apple’s iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand is designed specifically for the Duo and uses Apple’s TechWoven material, making it thin and lightweight. The special highlight of this case is a kickstand, which will help to keep the device at an angle suitable for reading, watching video or making FaceTime calls.

What I particularly like is that the kickstand folds back into the case when I don’t need it. That makes considerably more sense to me than carrying a separate stand around. The case also has built-in magnets to support MagSafe, Qi2 25W, and Qi-certified wireless charging while the case remains attached.

Pros

  • Designed specifically by Apple for iPhone Duo
  • Multiple viewing angles
  • Supports MagSafe and Qi2 charging
  • TechWoven exterior looks more premium than a basic silicone case
  • Available in navy blue and taupe

Cons

  • $129 makes it one of the more expensive options
  • Folio design won’t appeal to people who prefer minimal cases
  • Adds more coverage than an ultra-thin case

Best for: If I were buying just one case without wanting to experiment with third-party options, this would be my pick.

Check out on Apple

2. Spigen Tough Armor Pro MagFit: Best for protection

Spigen is probably the first brand I’d look at if my biggest concern were accidentally dropping a $1,999 foldable phone.

The Tough Armor Pro uses a PC and TPU construction with Air Cushion Technology, raised edges around the screen and camera, and dedicated hinge protection. Spigen says the new Pro hinge protector is slimmer and can lie completely flat when the phone is open.

That’s exactly the sort of engineering I want from a foldable case. The case also has an integrated magnetic ring system for MagSafe accessories and wireless charging, although Spigen warns that the hinge cover can make some accessories incompatible.

Pros

  • Strong PC + TPU construction
  • Dedicated slim hinge protection
  • Available in Black and Metal Slate
  • Considerably cheaper than Apple’s $129 folio

Cons

  • More rugged and bulky than minimalist cases
  • Hinge protection can interfere with some magnetic accessories
  • Not the case I’d choose if showing off the Duo’s thin design is the priority

Best for: This is the case I’d recommend to someone who is more worried about drops than keeping the Duo ultra-thin.

Check out on Amazon

3. Ridge iPhone Duo Case: Best slim premium case

The Ridge case is the one I’d choose if I wanted something that feels more like a premium accessory than traditional rugged phone armor.

The iPhone Duo version uses lightweight Kevlar fiber construction with TPU bumpers and is designed around an 8-foot drop-protection rating. It also has raised edges around the screen and camera and supports MagSafe and Qi wireless charging without removing the case.

I particularly like the idea of pairing this with the Duo because the phone itself is such a design-focused product. A huge protective case would hide much of what makes it interesting. Ridge also provides full access to the camera control area and offers a lifetime warranty and a 99-day risk-free trial.

Pros

  • 8-foot drop protection
  • Premium carbon-fiber-style appearance
  • Slimmer aesthetic than rugged cases
  • 99-day risk-free trial

Cons

  • $99 is expensive for a relatively minimalist case
  • The textured premium construction won’t appeal to everyone
  • May feel less protective than a full rugged case

Best for: For my taste, this is one of the most attractive options on the list.

Check out on Ridge

4. SPIDERCASE Magnetic Case with Stand: Best budget protection with convenience

SPIDERCASE is the option I’d consider when I don’t want to spend $70–$130 on my first iPhone Duo case.

Its appeal is straightforward: 15ft drop protection, built-in screen protector, auto-closing hinge protector, magnetic functionality, and a more practical design with a kickstand rather than a luxury finish.

That’s important because I wouldn’t necessarily recommend spending $129 on a case before I even know how I personally use the Duo. A less expensive case can be a smart way to live with the phone first and figure out what I actually need.

Pros

  • More affordable than Apple’s official case
  • Full body protection-focused design
  • Practical everyday form factor
  • Good option for buyers who don’t want to spend heavily

Cons

  • Less premium than Apple’s or Ridge’s designs
  • Bulk may be higher than a minimalist case
  • I’d want to test hinge movement and wireless charging before calling it a definitive winner

Best for: Anyone who wants affordable protection while keeping the initial accessory cost under control.

Check out on Amazon

5. FNTCASE Clear Magnetic Case: Best clear case

I understand the appeal of a clear case here. Apple is giving the iPhone Duo a very distinctive foldable design, and I wouldn’t necessarily want to cover it all with a black rugged case. The FNTCASE option is aimed at buyers who want transparent protection while keeping the phone’s design visible.

It offers a clear PC/TPU construction, magnetic compatibility, anti-yellowing treatment, raised screen and camera protection, and a screen protector included in the package. The case also offers decent drop protection, with flexible TPU bumpers and a rigid polycarbonate back, plus corner air cushions designed to absorb impacts.

Pros

  • Clear design shows off the Duo
  • Magnetic/MagSafe compatibility
  • Anti-yellowing design
  • Includes a screen protector

Cons

  • Clear cases can still show fingerprints and wear
  • Long-term yellowing is something I’d want to verify myself
  • Less premium-looking than Apple’s or Ridge’s cases

Best for: People who don’t want to hide the iPhone Duo’s design behind a bulky case.

Check out on Amazon

6. Mkeke TechWoven Case: Best fabric alternative

The Mkeke case caught my attention because it takes a similar general direction to Apple’s TechWoven case but at a different price point.

The Duo version uses a high-density tech-woven material with a soft-touch finish. It also includes MagSafe compatibility, raised camera and screen protection, and drop protection. Mkeke says the woven surface is designed to resist abrasion, fingerprints, stains, pilling, fraying, and discoloration.

I like this approach because fabric cases can make a foldable phone feel much more comfortable in the hand than hard plastic.

Pros

  • Premium woven texture with soft-touch feel
  • MagSafe compatible
  • Resistant to fingerprints and stains
  • More distinctive than a basic TPU case

Cons

  • Fabric won’t appeal to people who prefer rugged cases
  • Long-term durability still needs real-world testing
  • Less established than Apple’s official case

Best for: People who want the Apple-style fabric experience without automatically buying Apple’s $129 case.

Check out on Amazon

Don’t Buy an iPhone Duo Case Just Because It Says “MagSafe”

This is the biggest thing I learned from looking through the first wave of Duo cases. On a conventional iPhone, I can get away with treating MagSafe compatibility as a simple yes-or-no feature. With the Duo, the hinge changes the equation.

Spigen’s own documentation makes this clear: its Tough Armor Pro supports MagFit, but some accessories may be incompatible due to the hinge cover.

So I will be careful to check if the specific case works with the MagSafe charger, stand, wallet, and accessories I already use.

Protect your pricey foldable!

The iPhone Duo is unlike any iPhone Apple has made before, so I’m not surprised that choosing a case is already proving more complicated than choosing one for a conventional iPhone.

The good news is that there are already some genuinely interesting options.

  • My overall pick is Apple’s iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand because it offers the most integrated experience and was designed specifically around the Duo.
  • If protection is my number-one priority, I’d take the Spigen Tough Armor Pro (Mag Fit).
  • If I want something thinner and more premium, the Ridge Carbon is the one I’d be most tempted to try.
  • And if I simply want to spend less while I figure out how I actually use the Duo, I’d look at SPIDERCASE or FNTCASE rather than immediately spending $129 on a case.

So, which iPhone Duo case would you pick for your new foldable iPhone? Let me know in the comments below!

  • Best iPhone Duo accessories I’d actually buy

title.rendered: iPhone Duo vs Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Which foldable should you buy?

content.rendered:
Apple has finally entered the foldable phone market with iPhone Duo, but Google is already on store shelves with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Both phones give you a phone-sized outer screen and a larger tablet-like display inside, but they make very different trade-offs.

Here is the short version: buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold if you want a foldable now, a larger display, a lighter design, and a more flexible zoom camera. Wait for iPhone Duo if you already use an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Pencil and want a foldable that fits naturally into that ecosystem. Apple’s phone also offers a 2TB storage option and a strong video feature set, but it costs $100 more at list price and does not arrive in the U.S. until October 23.

iPhone Duo vs Pixel 11 Pro Fold specs at a glance

Apple announced iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026. Google announced the Pixel 11 Pro Fold in August, and it is already available in the U.S.

These are official specifications, not independent test results. Apple and Google measure battery life differently, so the battery claims should not be treated as a direct winner-takes-all comparison.

Design and displays

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the better fit if you want the biggest canvas. Its 8-inch inner display is larger than the iPhone Duo’s 7.6-inch screen, and its 6.5-inch outer display is also much more spacious than Apple’s 5.4-inch cover screen. That extra room should make typing, reading, and multitasking more comfortable without opening the phone every time.

The size advantage does not make the Pixel bulky. At 8.4 ounces, it is 0.56 ounces lighter than iPhone Duo. Google also lists the Pixel at 0.4 inches thick when folded, compared with 0.44 inches for Apple’s phone.

Apple takes a different approach. iPhone Duo is shorter and wider when open, with a 7.6-inch inner display in a 6.48 x 4.64-inch body. The phone also supports ProMotion up to 120Hz on both displays, an Always-On display, Dynamic Island, and Apple Pencil USB-C support. Apple lists up to 3,000 nits of outdoor peak brightness, while Google lists up to 3,600 nits peak brightness on both Pixel displays.

The choice is simple: get the Pixel for more screen space and lower weight, or choose iPhone Duo if you prefer Apple’s display features and want to use an Apple Pencil with the foldable. The Pixel is the more practical mini-tablet, while the iPhone is the more compact Apple device when folded.

Cameras: Pixel wins zoom, iPhone wins video flexibility

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold has the more versatile camera hardware. Its rear system includes a 48MP main camera, a 10.5MP ultrawide camera with autofocus and Macro Focus, and a dedicated 10.8MP 5x telephoto camera with optical image stabilization. Google also supports Super Zoom up to 30x.

iPhone Duo uses two 48MP rear cameras: a main camera and an ultrawide camera. The main camera gives you 2x optical-quality telephoto framing, but there is no dedicated telephoto lens. Its official optical-quality range runs from 0.5x through 2x, with up to 10x digital zoom.

That makes the Pixel the safer pick for concerts, sports, travel, and distant subjects. The dedicated 5x camera gives it a real hardware advantage instead of asking the main camera to crop aggressively.

Apple’s response is video. iPhone Duo can record 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 120 frames per second with its Fusion Main camera. It also supports Center Stage, Dual Capture, and Audio Mix features designed for people who record themselves and their surroundings. The Pixel records rear video up to 4K at 60 frames per second and adds Video Boost, Night Sight Video, and 10-bit HDR.

Choose the Pixel for zoom and camera flexibility. Choose iPhone Duo if video recording, FaceTime, and Apple’s camera tools matter more than having a dedicated telephoto lens.

Software and ecosystem

This is the decision that will matter most after the hardware comparison. iPhone Duo runs iOS 27, while the Pixel 11 Pro Fold runs Android 17. Our iOS 27 vs Android 17 comparison covers the wider software differences, but the foldable choice is mostly about the devices and services you already use.

If you have a Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, or an iPad, iPhone Duo should feel familiar from day one. FaceTime, iMessage, AirDrop, Apple Intelligence, and Apple Pencil support all work in the same Apple environment. The trade-off is that Apple’s phone is eSIM-only, so anyone who relies on a physical SIM should check with their carrier before buying.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the more flexible multitasking device. Google highlights Split Screen, Drag & Drop, Instant View, app bubbles, Gemini features, and Circle to Search. It also includes seven years of Android version updates, security updates, and Pixel Drops. The Pixel supports one physical Nano-SIM alongside eSIM, which makes it easier to move between carriers or use a backup line.

If you are switching from Android to Apple, read our guide on how to transfer data from Android to iPhone before you buy. The transfer is manageable, but your watch, messaging habits, and app purchases may affect the real cost of changing ecosystems.

Performance and battery

iPhone Duo uses Apple’s A20 Pro chip. Apple lists a six-core CPU, a seven-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses Google Tensor G6 with 16GB of RAM and a Titan M3 security chip.

Those chip names do not tell us which phone will feel faster in every app. Apple and Google optimize their processors for different workloads, and iPhone Duo is not available for independent testing yet. For now, the safe conclusion is that both phones have current flagship hardware, while the real performance gap will have to wait for hands-on reviews.

Battery claims are similarly difficult to compare. Apple says iPhone Duo lasts up to 24 hours in typical use and lists up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display or 31 hours on the inner display. Google gives the Pixel 11 Pro Fold a 24-plus-hour claim and lists a typical 4,806mAh battery.

Apple says iPhone Duo can reach 50% in about 20 minutes with a 60W-capable adapter. Google says the Pixel can reach 50% in about 30 minutes with a 30W USB-C PPS charger or higher. Apple sells its adapter separately, so remember to budget for a compatible charger if you do not already have one.

Durability and long-term ownership

Both phones have an IP68 rating, but that does not make either one waterproof or immune to damage. Foldable hinges and large flexible displays still deserve more care than a regular slab phone.

iPhone Duo uses a titanium foldable design with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and a Ceramic Shield back. Google says the Pixel uses a new gearless hinge, a glass fiber composite back, and ultra-strong ceramic outer cover glass. Google also says the Pixel is three times more durable than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold in its internal testing. That is a generational claim, not a direct durability test against iPhone Duo.

The Pixel has the clearer published software-support promise: seven years of OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates. Apple has a long history of supporting iPhones for years, but the iPhone Duo specifications page does not give a fixed support duration in the same way.

U.S. price and availability

iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 with 256GB of storage. Preorders open October 16, and the phone goes on sale in the U.S. on October 23. The top 2TB model gives Apple a storage tier Google does not offer.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold starts at $1,899 with 256GB and is already available. Google offers 512GB and 1TB versions, but no 2TB model. Google Store promotions and trade-in values can change, so use the $1,899 list price for a fair comparison and treat any discount as a temporary bonus.

The $100 difference matters at this price, especially because Google also gives you larger displays and a dedicated telephoto camera. That gives the Pixel an advantage for shoppers who want a foldable without paying extra for Apple’s ecosystem.

Which foldable should you buy?

For most people buying a foldable phone today, the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the better choice. It costs less, is lighter, has larger displays, includes a dedicated 5x telephoto camera, supports a physical SIM, and is available now. Its seven-year update promise also makes the ownership case easier to explain.

Buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold if you:

  • want the larger inner and outer displays;
  • care about zoom, travel, or close-up photography;
  • want a lighter foldable for daily use;
  • need a physical SIM option;
  • want to buy the phone now; or
  • prefer Android multitasking and Gemini features.

Buy iPhone Duo if you:

  • already use an iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, or iPad;
  • want Apple’s video tools and Dolby Vision recording;
  • plan to use Apple Pencil USB-C;
  • want up to 2TB of storage; or
  • are willing to wait until October 23 for iOS on a foldable.

My pick is the Pixel 11 Pro Fold for most foldable shoppers and iPhone Duo for committed Apple users. The Pixel is the better value and the more capable camera phone on paper. iPhone Duo is the more interesting choice if your daily life already runs through Apple, but wait for independent reviews before paying $1,999 for a first-generation foldable.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: What’s new and should you upgrade?

content.rendered:
Apple has finally pushed its Pro lineup forward with the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The new model is faster, smarter, and more capable than the predecessor, but the differences aren’t obvious at first glance.

Both phones share a similar design and many of the same features, so I wondered what has actually changed and whether it’s worth upgrading. To find the answer, I’ve compared the iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro Max across the camera, performance, battery life, AI features, price, and more to see where the new model really stands out.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: Quick comparison

The interesting part is that several headline specifications remain unchanged. The real difference is what Apple has improved underneath them.

Design and display: What actually changed?

If I were upgrading purely for the screen, I wouldn’t.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max retains the familiar 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR display, 120Hz ProMotion, Always-On display, and 3000-nit peak outdoor brightness. The dimensions are also essentially unchanged at 163.4mm tall, 78mm wide, and 8.75mm thick. Although it’s ~16 grams heavier than the 17 Pro Max.

The biggest visible change is actually the Dynamic Island. Apple has redesigned it to occupy less space while displaying more information. The iPhone 18 Pro Max can show up to three Live Activities simultaneously, which could make things such as sports scores, navigation and music controls more useful at a glance.

The material story also stays familiar. The iPhone 18 Pro Max uses an aluminum unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back. The new finishes are Black, Silver, Glacier and Burgundy, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue options.

If you’re buying the iPhone 18 Pro Max, protect its display with one of the best iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max screen protectors I’d actually buy.

My takeaway: the iPhone 18 Pro Max doesn’t offer a design overhaul. It’s a refinement. The smaller Dynamic Island is the change I expect to notice most in everyday use.

A20 Pro vs A19 Pro: The biggest performance upgrade

This is where I feel the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts to separate itself from its predecessor.

The new A20 Pro is built using a 2-nanometer process and features a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says it has 50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, while the GPU can be up to 40% faster. This same chip powers the new foldable iPhone Duo.

But the raw speed isn’t the part I find most interesting.

Apple has redesigned the chip packaging and paired it with a next-generation vapor chamber, which can deliver up to a 40% gain in sustained performance over the previous generation. That matters because sustained performance is what I care about when a phone is rendering video, playing a demanding game, or processing AI workloads for several minutes.

The Neural Engine is another major change. A20 Pro has 32 Neural Engine cores in total, giving it twice the AI processing capability Apple attributes to A19 Pro. That extra headroom is particularly important as Apple pushes more AI processing directly onto the iPhone. We have shared a more detailed breakdown in our A20 Pro guide.

For everyday apps, I don’t expect the iPhone 18 Pro Max to suddenly feel twice as fast. But for gaming, video editing, and on-device AI, this is one of the more meaningful generational upgrades.

Camera: The upgrade I’d pay attention to

If I had to pick one reason to buy the iPhone 18 Pro Max over the iPhone 17 Pro Max, I’d pick the camera.

The headline feature is Apple’s new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture. This is something the iPhone 17 Pro Max doesn’t have. The aperture can move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4.0.

Why does that matter? A wider aperture can let in more light, while a narrower aperture can give you greater depth of field. Apple says the system can automatically adjust for lighting and depth of field, while photographers can manually select the aperture from the Camera app.

New Pro controls allow manual adjustment of aperture, shutter speed, and white balance, alongside a histogram. Moreover, Photographic Styles 3 adds new texture and grain controls, and Smart focus tracking helps capture moving subjects.

The rest of the camera system remains familiar. The iPhone 18 Pro Max still has 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide and 48MP Fusion Telephoto cameras, with 4x and 8x optical-quality telephoto options. The 18MP Centre Stage front camera also carries over.

There are meaningful video upgrades too, including the ability to apply Cinematic effects after recording and new 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse capabilities.

If you bought the iPhone 17 Pro Max mainly for its camera, the iPhone 18 Pro Max gives you the clearest reason to consider upgrading.

Battery life and charging: How much better is it?

Battery life is another area where the iPhone 18 Pro Max makes a noticeable numerical jump.

The iPhone 17 Pro Max offers up to 39 hours of video playback. The iPhone 18 Pro Max reaches up to 43 hours, a four-hour increase. Apple attributes the improvement to a larger battery combined with the efficiency gains of its new silicon.

Charging is faster, too. The iPhone 18 Pro Max can get around seven hours of video playback from a five-minute wired charge, according to Apple’s testing. Moreover, you can get up to 50% in around 15 minutes when using a 60W-capable adapter or higher with Adjustable Voltage Supply.

This is the sort of upgrade I appreciate more than a benchmark score. If I leave home with a nearly empty phone, a few minutes connected to a charger suddenly become much more useful. For heavy users, the battery upgrade alone makes the iPhone 18 Pro Max more attractive.

Looking for a charger or other add-ons for your new phone? Explore our guide to the best iPhone 18 Pro accessories.

AI and Siri: iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max

This is where the A20 Pro upgrade becomes more relevant. Both phones support Apple Intelligence, but the iPhone 18 Pro Max launches with iOS 27 and the new Siri AI experience.

Siri AI is designed to understand personal context across apps such as Messages, Mail, and Photos. It can also use on-screen awareness, answer questions, and interact with what you’re seeing through the Camera app.

Apple is also adding more AI-powered tools across iOS 27, including improved Clean Up, Image Playground, Spatial Reframing, and Safari’s Notify Me feature.

The important distinction is that the iPhone 18 Pro Max has considerably more AI processing headroom, thanks to the A20 Pro’s Neural Engine and Neural Accelerators.

That doesn’t mean the iPhone 17 Pro Max suddenly becomes useless for Apple Intelligence. Instead, I see the 18 Pro Max as the better long-term choice if AI is going to become a major part of how I use my phone.

Connectivity with the new Apple C2 Modem

The iPhone 18 Pro Max also gets Apple’s C2 modem system, replacing the previous generation’s C1X.

C2 works alongside the A20 Pro and introduces AI-powered improvements intended to improve cellular quality and reliability. Apple says it can deliver faster uploads in selected markets while consuming 15% less energy than C1X. It also supports mmWave in the US.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max also retains Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread through Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip.

I wouldn’t upgrade from an iPhone 17 Pro Max solely for the modem. But improved cellular efficiency, reliability, and upload speeds are the kind of behind-the-scenes upgrades that can make a flagship feel better over years of ownership.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs iPhone 17 Pro Max: Price difference

This is where the decision becomes more complicated.

The iPhone 17 Pro Max launched at $1,199, with 256GB storage. It was also available in 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB configurations.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299 in the US and continues to offer 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage options.

The bigger point is that the iPhone 17 Pro Max is still an extremely capable phone. If retailers offer meaningful discounts on it, the older model could become the better value.

What hasn’t changed?

This is an important part of the comparison because the iPhone 18 Pro Max isn’t a complete redesign.

The following remain broadly familiar:

  • 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR display with ProMotion up to 120Hz
  • Always-On display
  • Aluminum unibody construction
  • 48MP Ultra Wide camera
  • 48MP Telephoto camera with up to 8x optical-quality zoom
  • 18MP Centre Stage front camera
  • Camera Control
  • Action button
  • USB-C
  • Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread
  • 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage options

The iPhone 17 Pro Max already introduced a major camera and thermal-performance overhaul, so Apple isn’t starting from scratch with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

That’s why I’d describe this generation as a deeper refinement rather than a visual revolution.

My verdict: Should you upgrade?

If I already owned an iPhone 17 Pro Max, I wouldn’t upgrade just because the number changed from 17 to 18. But I would seriously consider the iPhone 18 Pro Max if camera photography, sustained performance, battery life, or AI were priorities for me.

Buy iPhone 18 Pro Max if you:

  • Want the best iPhone camera Apple currently offers.
  • Shoot a lot of photos or video.
  • Play demanding games or edit video on my phone.
  • Want maximum battery life.
  • Like to use the newest Siri AI features.
  • Are upgrading from an iPhone 15 Pro Max or older.

Keep the iPhone 17 Pro Max if:

  • You’re already happy with its camera.
  • Battery life already feels like enough.
  • Don’t care much about AI features.
  • Mostly use your phone for messaging, social media, and streaming.
  • You are getting the 17 Pro Max at a significant discount.

My bottom line: the iPhone 18 Pro Max is not the kind of upgrade that makes the iPhone 17 Pro Max obsolete. Instead, Apple has taken an already powerful flagship and attacked the areas that matter most over a long ownership period, such as camera flexibility, sustained performance, battery life, charging, cellular efficiency, and AI.

If I were buying a Pro Max today and the price difference were reasonable, I’d choose the iPhone 18 Pro Max. But if I already owned the iPhone 17 Pro Max, I’d upgrade only if I genuinely cared about the new camera system or AI capabilities.

So, would you upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, or stick with the iPhone 17 Pro Max for another year? Let me know which one you’d choose.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Ultra 4: Everything you need to know about

content.rendered:
After months of anticipation and rumours, Apple has finally revealed the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Although it doesn’t pack major hardware upgrades compared to its predecessors, Apple has brought on tons of new features, design overhauls, and AI capabilities that will undoubtedly enhance the overall experience of the wearable.

So, if you’re wondering what’s new, what’s changed, and whether it’s worth the upgrade, here’s a complete breakdown of the Apple Watch Ultra 4.

Apple Watch Ultra 4 specifications at a glance (Detailed overview)

Designs & colours: What’s new

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 sticks to the classic design that has defined the Ultra lineup. It brings back a familiar rectangular display and titanium build, but with minor upgrades such as a larger and brighter screen. The company is also putting effort into sustainability, stating that the new wearable is made up of 45% recycled materials, with the titanium case made entirely from recycled titanium.

In terms of finishes, Apple is offering two different options: Natural Titanium and Black Titanium. The company has also introduced new colour options for Trail Loop, Alpine Loop, and Ocean Bands, which means more customisation options for users. For those who want a premium touch, they can also choose the Apple Watch Hermes edition. This one comes with a Grand H titanium band featuring a built-in extension system.

Battery and charging: A major battery boost

Apple has gone all out when it comes to the battery life upgrades for Apple Watch Ultra 4. Now, users will be able to get 50 hours of battery life under normal use, which means just a single charge can get you around two days of use.

Those who switch to Low Power Mode can expect the wearable to last up to 84 hours. Apple has also brought in improvements to the Extended Workout and Max Extended Workout modes, which make Apple Watch Ultra 4 the right choice for longer activities and endurance workouts.

Charging speeds have also been given a look. Now, Apple Watch Ultra 4 can get 18 hours of additional battery life with just 15 minutes of charging. Users will now be able to easily top up their wearable whenever they’re running low, and quickly get back into the action.

Performance: New S11 chip

Under the hood of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is the new S11 chip. This features a 4-core Neural Engine and 64GB of storage. As you’d expect, Apple has dubbed it its most powerful chip ever used in a wearable. While that might not sound like much on paper, it’s actually the foundation for many of Ultra 4’s new health, audio, AI, and tracking capabilities. The chip is also responsible for the new Siri experience in watchOS 27.

Health sensing system

The major highlight of the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is its new Health Sensing System. It’s powered by the wearable’s sensors, S11 chip, and advanced algorithms to collect and interpret health data. Now, the watch can take your heart rate readings every five seconds, which gives it more data to analyse and monitor your heart throughout the game.

The system also brings frequent heart-rate variability (HRV) measurements into the play, which will give users a great understanding of their body’s overall wellness and recovery. This works right alongside the Readiness score, which will estimate how well a person is prepared for the day ahead. Apple has also made upgrades to step tracking, which means it will be more accurate than ever before.

Audio Intelligence

Another thing that’s worth keeping an eye out for is Audio Intelligence. What’s this about? Well, it makes use of the wearable’s built-in microphone, the new S11 chip, Apple Intelligence, and other components to bring four unique features to the table:

  • Sound Recognition: If you’re someone who leaves your iPhone behind, the Ultra 4 can now detect important sounds such as doorbells, sirens, and alarms, and send you an alert.
  • Live Rewind: Missed something in a conversation? A double press of the Digital Crown will let you pull up a text snippet of the previous 15 seconds.
  • Siri Recap: Apple Intelligence can now summarise everything you’ve been discussing with someone else and give you a summary.
  • Shazam: You no longer have to wonder what song is playing around you. The wearable can identify the track and display the result.

Of course, a wearable listening to conversations and sounds around you raises privacy concerns. However, Apple has assured that Audio Intelligence isn’t designed to record and store things. The S11 chip comes with a Secure Enclave that keeps all the audio processing completely isolated. Once it’s been used, the audio will be instantly deleted.

Availability and pricing

Despite speculation that the current hardware shortages and rising prices could push the Apple Watch Ultra 4 price sky-high, Apple has kept things unchanged. The wearable starts at $799 in the U.S, which matches the launch price of its predecessor.

When it comes to monthly plans, the Ultra 4 can be financed at $66.58 per month over 12 months. Pre-orders are now available live in more than 50 countries, and the wearable will officially hit the stores on September 18, 2026.

Final thoughts: Should you upgrade?

The biggest question now is whether or not the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is worth the upgrade. Ultimately, that comes down to what you’re looking for from your wearable. If a longer battery life, more advanced health tracking, and new Audio Intelligence features are important to you, the Ultra 4 is undoubtedly a good pick.

However, if you’re someone already rocking a previous-generation Apple Watch Ultra, there’s no reason to upgrade. Sure, the Ultra 4 does bring major improvements, but they don’t completely change the experience or design. However, if you’re someone coming from an old Apple Watch, the Ultra 4 has enough features to make the upgrade completely worth it.

title.rendered: Apple A20 Pro: Everything You Need to Know About the New iPhone Chip

content.rendered:
Apple introduced A20 Pro with iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max on September 9. The same chip also appears in Apple’s technical specifications for iPhone Duo.

Apple says A20 Pro is built using the latest 2-nanometer process technology. It combines a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. The company also claims higher memory bandwidth, faster graphics, and twice the AI processing of A19 Pro.

Those numbers come from Apple’s own comparisons. They describe Apple’s intended gains, but they are not independent benchmark results. A20 Pro’s real gaming performance, thermals, and battery efficiency will need hands-on testing after the new iPhones ship.

What A20 Pro includes

Apple’s iPhone Duo technical specifications provide the clearest breakdown of the chip:

The CPU handles general app and system work. The GPU handles graphics and games, while the Neural Engine and Neural Accelerators are aimed at machine-learning tasks such as Apple Intelligence features and computational photography. The core count tells us how Apple has built the chip, not how every app will perform.

What Apple’s 2nm claim means

Apple says A20 Pro is built using the latest 2-nanometer process technology. A process node is a manufacturing generation, not a performance score by itself. It does not tell us the chip’s clock speeds, its real power draw, or how quickly a particular game will run.

TSMC’s 2nm page offers general context. TSMC describes its N2 process as using first-generation nanosheet transistor technology and says volume production began in the fourth quarter of 2025. Apple does not name TSMC or specify that transistor structure on its A20 Pro pages, so TSMC’s description should not be read as independent confirmation of Apple’s exact implementation.

Apple’s A20 Pro comparisons with A19 Pro

Apple’s Newsroom announcement gives three headline comparisons with A19 Pro:

  • 50% more memory bandwidth.
  • Graphics performance up to 40% faster.
  • Double the AI processing power.

Apple ties the AI claim to the new Dual 16-core Neural Engine and its 32 total cores. More memory bandwidth can help move data between the chip and memory, while the larger GPU and Neural Accelerators give Apple more hardware for graphics and machine-learning workloads.

The important qualifier is “Apple says.” These are company comparisons, not independent tests. They also do not mean every app will run 50% faster or that every game will show a 40% frame-rate increase.

The package and cooling design matter too

The process node is only part of A20 Pro’s design. Apple says the package is inspired by its M-series chips, with the silicon die placed side by side with memory. That moves memory out of the chip’s thermal path and lets A20 Pro attach directly to a next-generation vapor chamber.

Apple says the vapor chamber has three times the surface area of the previous generation on iPhone 17 Pro. With new thermally conductive materials and the new package, Apple claims up to 40% better sustained performance than the previous generation.

That claim is separate from the up-to-40% graphics comparison with A19 Pro. The graphics number describes Apple’s chip comparison. The sustained-performance number describes Apple’s claim for the chip and cooling system against the previous iPhone Pro generation. Neither is an independent test. For background, the earlier iPhone 17 Pro vapor-chamber design shows why heat management matters during long workloads, but its gaming results do not tell us how A20 Pro will perform.

What A20 Pro could change in daily use

Camera processing

Apple says the Neural Engine accelerates computational photography. That could give the new camera pipeline more room for tasks such as image processing, low-light adjustments, video effects, and Apple’s Reference Image features on iPhone 18 Pro. The final photo still depends on the camera sensors, lenses, software, and Apple’s image processing choices. A20 Pro’s core count alone cannot prove better photos.

Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

The Dual 16-core Neural Engine is designed for on-device AI models. Apple says A20 Pro brings double the AI processing power of A19 Pro, while Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute for heavier work.

That hardware headroom should matter most as iOS 27 expands Siri AI and Apple Intelligence across apps, photos, the Camera app, and system actions. It does not make every Siri request local, and it does not remove software, language, or regional availability limits. Apple is rolling out Siri AI as a beta with iOS 27.

Graphics and gaming

The 7-core GPU, Neural Accelerators, hardware ray tracing, and larger vapor chamber give A20 Pro the hardware Apple is using to target demanding games and longer AI workloads. That combination targets the kind of long, demanding work where heat can limit performance.

Real frame rates, surface temperatures, throttling, and battery drain still need independent testing. Apple has not published those results for A20 Pro.

Battery efficiency

Apple calls A20 Pro its most powerful and efficient iPhone chip design yet and links the new iPhones’ battery improvements partly to more efficient Apple silicon. That does not isolate the chip’s contribution. Battery size, the display, the C2 modem, software, and the workload all affect how long an iPhone lasts.

A20 Pro is separate from N1 and C2

A20 Pro is the main application processor. It is not the wireless or cellular modem hardware.

Apple says iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max use N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Apple also identifies C2 as its next-generation cellular modem system. The iPhone Duo specifications list A20 Pro, N1, and C2 as separate components too.

In practice, these chips work as part of the same phone, but they have different jobs. A20 Pro handles apps, graphics, camera computation, and on-device AI. N1 handles wireless networking. C2 handles cellular connections and their related power demands.

Which iPhones get A20 Pro?

Apple lists A20 Pro in iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. The phones do not have identical designs, batteries, displays, or cooling systems, so the same chip name does not guarantee identical sustained performance across all three models.

For context, U.S. iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max preorders begin at 5 a.m. PT on September 12, with availability on September 18. iPhone Duo preorders begin at 5 a.m. PT on October 16, with availability on October 23.

title.rendered: Download official iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max wallpapers

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, bringing new colours and a fresh set of wallpapers to match. If you love Apple’s wallpapers, you don’t have to wait for the new iPhone to enjoy them. Here, you can download the official iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max wallpapers in high resolution for free and give your current iPhone a fresh look.

iPhone 18 Pro lineup brings fresh new colours

Apple’s latest Pro models come in Black, Silver, Glacier, and the new Burgundy finishes, with colour-matched back glass. So, the wallpapers below are designed around that same understated, glowing aesthetic.

The wallpapers have that distinctive Apple feel with dark gradients, soft lighting, curved shapes, and just the right amount of glow to make the Lock Screen look luxurious without competing with my icons or widgets.

If you want the iPhone 18 Pro feel on your existing iPhone, these are worth trying.

Download iPhone 18 Pro stock wallpapers

I’ve included all the official versions so you can switch the personality of your iPhone depending on your mood.

Download: Black | Glacier | Silver | Burgundy

The wallpapers have the same subtle curves and glowing edges, which work surprisingly well with iOS 27’s redesigned Liquid Glass interface.

  • Black: The most dramatic option, with a deep charcoal background and subtle white highlights.
  • Glacier: A soft icy-blue version that gives the Lock Screen a brighter, cleaner appearance.
  • Silver: The minimalist choice, with an almost-white metallic glow.
  • Burgundy: My favourite of the four, with a rich red wine tone that matches Apple’s new Pro finish.

Tap the Download button above to save the wallpapers in the original resolution to your device gallery.

What’s new in iPhone 18 Pro?

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max bring a mix of performance, camera, and design upgrades that make Apple’s latest Pro lineup more capable and polished.

At the heart of the new models is the A20 Pro chip, which delivers faster performance and improved capabilities for demanding tasks and AI features. Apple has also upgraded the main camera with a 48MP Fusion sensor and variable aperture, giving users more control over their photos.

The Pro models also get improved battery life and a redesigned Dynamic Island that can show more Live Activities. However, in terms of design, Apple retained the iPhone 17 Pro’s camera plateau. For me, the new Burgundy finish is among the most eye-catching changes, giving the iPhone 18 Pro a distinctly fresh look.

Final thoughts

You don’t need to buy an iPhone 18 Pro to enjoy its new look. Just download your favourite wallpaper, set it on your iPhone, and give your Lock Screen a fresh makeover.

Know someone excited about the iPhone 18 Pro? Share these wallpapers with them; they’ll thank you later!

You might also like:

  • Download the official iPhone Duo wallpapers
  • Download iPhone 18 Pro burgundy wallpapers
